summary.en: Han officers Chen Tang and Gan Yanshou led an army of Han troops and Western Regions levies into the Talas valley and stormed the fortress of the breakaway Xiongnu chanyu Zhizhi, killing him and ending the Xiongnu schism in the west.
summary.zh: 汉朝将领陈汤、甘延寿率汉兵及西域诸国兵深入塔拉斯河谷，攻破自立的匈奴郅支单于的城池并将其斩杀，结束了匈奴在西方的分裂势力。

sources.title: Ban Gu, Hanshu (Book of Han), ch. 70: biographies of Chen Tang and Gan Yanshou
Thomas J. Barfield, The Perilous Frontier: Nomadic Empires and China (1989)
Wikidata Q870947

note: Zhizhi’s fort lay on the Talas river near modern Taraz; the exact site is unknown, so coordinates are approximate.

summary.en: Bumin of the Ashina clan, whose Türks had served the Rouran as ironworkers, defeated his overlords and took the title Il-Qaghan; within a generation the first Turkic empire stretched from Manchuria to the Black Sea.
summary.zh: 阿史那氏的土门原为柔然役使的“锻奴”，他击败柔然，自号伊利可汗；不到一代人的时间，第一突厥汗国的疆域便从东北亚延伸至黑海。

sources.title: Linghu Defen et al., Zhoushu (Book of Zhou), ch. 50: the Tujue
Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Denis Sinor (ed.), The Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia (1990)

note: No separate Wikidata item exists for the event, so no QID is given (Q15146034 is the khaganate itself, inception 551 on Wikidata). Chinese sources (Zhoushu) date the victory over the Rouran to 552. Coordinates approximate the Ötüken uplands.

story.en:
The Zhoushu, the official history of the Northern Zhou, says the Ashina Türks lived on the southern slopes of the Altai and worked iron for the Rouran khagan. When their chief Bumin asked Anagui, the Rouran ruler, for a princess in marriage, Anagui replied with contempt that a blacksmith slave had no business making such a request.

Bumin turned instead to the Western Wei court at Chang’an, which sent him Princess Changle in 551. The next year he attacked and routed the Rouran; Anagui took his own life, and Bumin proclaimed himself Il-Qaghan. He died within months, but his sons Muqan and his brother Istämi pressed the conquest east and west.

Within thirty years the Türk khaganate reached from Manchuria to the steppes north of the Black Sea. It traded silk with Iran and Byzantium through Sogdian middlemen and set the pattern, and the very titles, of steppe empire for the next millennium.
story.zh:
北周官修史书《周书》记载，阿史那突厥居于金山（阿尔泰山）之阳，为柔然可汗冶铁。首领土门向柔然可汗阿那瓌求娶公主，阿那瓌回以辱骂，说“尔是我锻奴，何敢发是言也”。

土门转而与长安的西魏结好，西魏于551年将长乐公主嫁给他。次年土门大破柔然，阿那瓌自杀，土门自号伊利可汗。他数月后去世，但其子木杆可汗与其弟室点密继续向东西两方征伐。

不到三十年，突厥汗国东起满洲，西至黑海以北草原，并经粟特商人之手与伊朗、拜占庭进行丝绸贸易。它为此后千年的草原帝国奠定了模式，连可汗等称号也由此沿用。

name.en: Fall of the Hephthalites (Battle of Gol-Zarriun)

summary.en: Western Turkic forces under Istämi, in alliance with the Sasanian king Khosrow I, crushed the Hephthalite army near Bukhara; the victors partitioned the Hephthalite realm along the Oxus.
summary.zh: 室点密率领的西突厥军队与萨珊国王库思老一世结盟，在布哈拉附近大败嚈哒军，胜利者以阿姆河为界瓜分了嚈哒领土。

sources.title: Ferdowsi, Shahnameh (reign of Khosrow Anushirvan)
Denis Sinor (ed.), The Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia (1990)
Étienne de la Vaissière, Sogdian Traders: A History (2005)
Wikidata Q13600791

note: Dated between 557 and 563 by different authors; Wikidata gives 560.

summary.en: Succession quarrels among Ashina princes, encouraged by Sui China’s diplomacy, split the Turkic Khaganate into eastern and western halves, which thereafter followed separate histories.
summary.zh: 阿史那氏诸王子争夺汗位，隋朝又从中离间，突厥汗国由此分裂为东、西两部，此后各自发展。

sources.title: Wei Zheng et al., Suishu (Book of Sui), ch. 84: the Tujue
Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Wikidata Q154875

note: A diffuse conflict; coordinates mark the eastern khaganate’s Ötüken heartland.

summary.en: Memorial steles for Kül Tegin (732) and Bilge Qaghan (735) in the Orkhon valley carry the oldest known extended texts in a Turkic language, written in Old Turkic runiform script and recounting the Second Turkic Khaganate’s history.
summary.zh: 立于鄂尔浑河谷的阙特勤碑（732年）和毗伽可汗碑（735年）以古突厥卢尼文字刻写，是已知最早的长篇突厥语文献，记述了后突厥汗国的历史。

sources.title: Talat Tekin, A Grammar of Orkhon Turkic (1968)
Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Orkhon inscriptions
Wikidata Q334704

note: Wikidata dates the inscriptions only to the 8th century; the stele dates 732 and 735 come from their texts and Chinese records.

story.en:
In 1889 the Russian explorer Nikolai Yadrintsev found two great stone steles near the Kokshin Orkhon river, inscribed on one face in Chinese and on the others in an unknown runic-looking script. For four years scholars argued over what language it was. In December 1893 the Danish linguist Vilhelm Thomsen announced that he had cracked it: the first words he read were “Tengri” (heaven) and “Türk”.

The texts, composed by Bilge Qaghan’s nephew Yollïg Tegin, speak in the khagan’s own voice. They recall how the Türks fell under Tang rule for fifty years and rose again under Ilterish and the counsellor Tonyukuk, praise the battles of the prince Kül Tegin, and warn the Turkic begs that Chinese silk and sweet words would lure them south to their ruin.

The steles are the oldest long texts in any Turkic language. Their call to stay on the Ötüken uplands has made them a founding document of Turkic identity from Mongolia to Turkey.
story.zh:
1889年，俄国探险家雅德林采夫在鄂尔浑河畔发现两通巨大石碑，一面刻汉文，其余各面刻着一种形似如尼文的未知文字。学界争论了四年仍不知其为何种语言。1893年12月，丹麦语言学家汤姆森宣布破译成功，他最先读出的词是“腾格里”（天）和“突厥”。

碑文由毗伽可汗之侄药利特勤撰写，以可汗的口吻叙事：突厥曾臣服唐朝五十年，后在骨咄禄（颉跌利施可汗）和谋臣暾欲谷领导下复兴；碑文颂扬阙特勤的战功，并告诫突厥诸匐：唐人的丝绸与甜言蜜语会诱使他们南下而走向灭亡。

这两通碑是现存最早的长篇突厥语文献。碑文中留守于都斤山的告诫，使之成为从蒙古到土耳其的突厥认同的奠基文献。

summary.en: An Abbasid army, aided by defecting Karluks, defeated the Tang general Gao Xianzhi near the Talas river, marking the limit of Tang power west of the Tian Shan. Later tradition credits prisoners taken there with bringing paper-making to Samarkand.
summary.zh: 阿拔斯军队在倒戈的葛逻禄人协助下，于怛罗斯河附近击败唐将高仙芝，标志着唐朝势力在天山以西的极限。后世传说此役被俘的唐人将造纸术传入撒马尔罕。

sources.title: Du Huan, Jingxingji (Record of Travels), preserved in Du You’s Tongdian, ch. 193
Christopher I. Beckwith, Empires of the Silk Road (2009)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Talas
Wikidata Q492415

note: The transfer of paper-making through Talas prisoners is a medieval tradition (al-Tha‘alibi) that many historians now doubt.

story.en:
In 750 the Tang commander Gao Xianzhi, a general of Korean descent who had already led an army across the Pamirs, executed the king of Chach (Tashkent) after promising him safety. The king’s son fled to the Abbasid governor of Khurasan, Abu Muslim, who sent an army under Ziyad ibn Salih north to meet the Tang.

The armies met in July 751 near the Talas river. Chinese accounts say the battle lasted five days, until the Karluk Turks serving with the Tang changed sides and attacked them from behind. Gao Xianzhi escaped with a few thousand men. Among the captives was Du Huan, who spent a decade in the caliphate and wrote one of the earliest Chinese descriptions of Kufa and the Muslim world before returning home by sea in 762.

Talas did not by itself end Tang power in Central Asia; the An Lushan rebellion, which broke out four years later, forced the garrisons home. But it became a symbol of the meeting of the Chinese and Islamic worlds.
story.zh:
750年，曾率军翻越帕米尔高原的高丽裔唐将高仙芝在许以安全之后，杀害了石国（塔什干）国王。石国王子逃往阿拔斯王朝呼罗珊总督阿布·穆斯林处求援，后者派齐亚德·伊本·萨利赫率军北上迎击唐军。

751年7月，两军在怛罗斯河附近相遇。据中国史料，双方鏖战五日，直到随唐军作战的葛逻禄部临阵倒戈，从背后夹击唐军。高仙芝仅率数千人突围。被俘者中有杜环，他在阿拉伯世界生活了十余年，762年经海路回国，著《经行记》，是中国最早记述库法和伊斯兰世界的文献之一。

怛罗斯之战本身并未终结唐朝在中亚的势力，四年后爆发的安史之乱才迫使西域驻军东撤。但此战成为中华世界与伊斯兰世界相遇的象征。

name.en: Kyrgyz sack Ordu-Baliq; Uyghur Khaganate falls
name.zh: 黠戛斯攻破回鹘牙帐，回鹘汗国灭亡

summary.en: Yenisei Kyrgyz forces sacked Ordu-Baliq, the walled Uyghur capital on the Orkhon; the Uyghurs scattered south and west to Gansu and the Turfan basin, where they founded the Ganzhou and Qocho kingdoms.
summary.zh: 黠戛斯军队攻破鄂尔浑河畔的回鹘都城牙帐（斡耳朵八里），回鹘人四散南迁西徙，在河西走廊和吐鲁番盆地分别建立甘州回鹘与高昌回鹘。

sources.title: Colin Mackerras, The Uighur Empire according to the T’ang Dynastic Histories (1972)
Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Wikidata Q2475401

note: The QID is the city site of Ordu-Baliq.

story.en:
Around 821 the Arab traveller Tamim ibn Bahr crossed the steppe to the Uyghur capital on the Orkhon and described a great walled city with twelve iron gates, crowded markets and farmland all around: a nomad empire’s capital that looked like a city of the settled world.

Two decades later the khaganate was failing. Chinese sources report famine, epidemics among people and herds, and heavy snows that killed the livestock in 839, alongside murderous quarrels at court. In 840 a disaffected Uyghur commander brought the Yenisei Kyrgyz, with a reported 100,000 horsemen, against the capital. They killed the qaghan, burned Ordu-Baliq and carried off the Tang princess Taihe.

The Uyghurs scattered. Some fled to the Tang frontier and were broken there; others founded kingdoms at Ganzhou in the Gansu corridor and at Qocho in the Turfan oasis, where Uyghur culture turned to farming, Buddhism and trade. Mongolia would not host a comparable empire until Genghis Khan.
story.zh:
约821年，阿拉伯旅行者塔米姆·伊本·巴赫尔穿越草原抵达鄂尔浑河畔的回鹘都城，描述了一座有十二道铁门、市集繁盛、四周农田环绕的大城：一个游牧帝国的都城，看上去却像定居世界的城市。

二十年后，汗国已经衰落。中国史料记载，839年回鹘遭遇饥荒、人畜疫病和大雪，牲畜大量冻死，宫廷中又相互残杀。840年，一名心怀不满的回鹘将领引黠戛斯人（据称十万骑）进攻都城，杀死可汗，焚毁斡耳朵八里，并掳走唐朝太和公主。

回鹘由此四散。一部投奔唐边，后被击破；另一些人在河西走廊建立甘州回鹘，在吐鲁番绿洲建立高昌回鹘，转向农耕、佛教和商贸。此后直到成吉思汗兴起，蒙古高原再未出现同等规模的帝国。

summary.en: Built in Bukhara as the Samanid family tomb, this cube of intricately patterned baked brick is one of the oldest surviving monuments of Islamic Central Asia and a symbol of the Persian cultural revival the dynasty sponsored.
summary.zh: 这座位于布哈拉的萨曼家族陵墓以图案繁复的烧砖砌成立方体，是中亚现存最古老的伊斯兰建筑之一，也是萨曼王朝倡导的波斯文化复兴的象征。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Historic Centre of Bukhara
S. Frederick Starr, Lost Enlightenment: Central Asia’s Golden Age (2013)
Wikidata Q1268850

note: Construction is dated within Ismail Samani’s and Nasr II’s reigns (892–943); the exact date is debated.

summary.en: Seljuk Turkmen led by Tughril and Chaghri Beg routed the Ghaznavid sultan Mas‘ud I near Merv, winning Khurasan and launching the Seljuk empire that took Baghdad in 1055.
summary.zh: 图格里勒与查格里率领的塞尔柱突厥蛮人在梅尔夫附近击溃伽色尼苏丹马苏德一世，夺取呼罗珊，开启了1055年进入巴格达的塞尔柱帝国。

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth, The Ghaznavids: Their Empire in Afghanistan and Eastern Iran (1963)
Abu’l-Fazl Bayhaqi, Tarikh-i Bayhaqi
Wikidata Q26493

story.en:
Through the 1030s the Seljuk Turkmen, led by the brothers Tughril and Chaghri, had been raiding Khurasan, the richest province of the Ghaznavid sultan Mas‘ud I. Mas‘ud answered with a heavy professional army of Turkish slave soldiers and war elephants, trained for set-piece battles in India.

In May 1040 he marched across the waterless country between Sarakhs and Merv. The Seljuks harried his columns, filled in or held the wells, and waited. By the time the armies met at the small fort of Dandanaqan, the Ghaznavid troops were exhausted by heat and thirst; parts of the army deserted, and the rest broke. Mas‘ud fled to Ghazni and then towards India, where his own officers deposed and killed him.

The Seljuks proclaimed their rule over Khurasan on the battlefield and sent news of the victory to the caliph. Fifteen years later Tughril entered Baghdad as sultan, and within a generation the Seljuks ruled from the Oxus to Anatolia.
story.zh:
1030年代，突厥蛮塞尔柱部在图格里勒和恰格里兄弟率领下，不断侵掠伽色尼王朝苏丹马苏德一世最富庶的呼罗珊省。马苏德以一支由突厥奴隶兵和战象组成的精锐常备军应战，这支军队惯于在印度进行正面会战。

1040年5月，他率军穿越萨拉赫斯与梅尔夫之间的无水地带。塞尔柱人不断袭扰其行军队列，填塞或控制水井，以逸待劳。两军在小堡丹丹坎相遇时，伽色尼士兵已因酷热和干渴而精疲力竭，部分部队逃散，余部随即崩溃。马苏德逃回伽色尼，又转往印度，最终被部下废黜杀害。

塞尔柱人在战场上宣布统治呼罗珊，并向哈里发报捷。十五年后图格里勒以苏丹身份进入巴格达，一代人之内，塞尔柱人的统治从阿姆河延伸到安纳托利亚。

summary.en: The Qara Khitai under Yelü Dashi crushed the Seljuk sultan Sanjar and his Karakhanid vassals near Samarkand, becoming overlords of Transoxiana; garbled reports of the battle fed the European legend of Prester John.
summary.zh: 耶律大石率领的西辽军队在撒马尔罕附近大败塞尔柱苏丹桑贾尔及其喀喇汗附庸，成为河中地区的宗主；关于此役的讹传助长了欧洲“约翰长老”的传说。

sources.title: Michal Biran, The Empire of the Qara Khitai in Eurasian History (2005)
Ibn al-Athir, al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh
Wikidata Q3950956

summary.en: A great kurultai at the source of the Onon river acclaimed Temüjin as Chinggis (Genghis) Khan, uniting the Mongol and Turkic tribes of the steppe into the Yeke Mongghol Ulus, the Great Mongol State.
summary.zh: 斡难河源头召开的大忽里勒台推举铁木真为成吉思汗，将草原上的蒙古及突厥诸部统一为“也客·蒙古·兀鲁思”，即大蒙古国。

sources.title: The Secret History of the Mongols, tr. Igor de Rachewiltz (2004)
Igor de Rachewiltz, “The title Činggis Qan/Qaγan re-examined” (1989)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Genghis Khan

note: No separate Wikidata item exists for the 1206 kurultai, so no QID is given (Q12557 is the Mongol Empire). The location near the Onon source is approximate.

story.en:
By 1206 Temüjin had defeated every rival confederation on the Mongolian plateau: the Tatars who, the Secret History says, had poisoned his father, the Kereits of his former patron Ong Khan, the Naimans of the Altai, and his blood brother turned enemy Jamukha. That spring the leaders of the steppe gathered at the source of the Onon and raised his white standard of nine tails.

The Secret History of the Mongols describes what followed as a reorganisation rather than a coronation. Temüjin took the title Chinggis Khan and named ninety-five commanders of a thousand, breaking up the old tribes into decimal units loyal to him. He expanded his day and night guard to ten thousand men, and made his adopted brother Shigi Qutuqu chief judge, ordering decisions to be written down in the Uyghur script.

The shaman Teb Tengri, who claimed heaven had chosen Temüjin, soon tried to rival him and was killed. The new state, the Yeke Mongghol Ulus, was built for war; within five years it attacked the Jin.
story.zh:
到1206年，铁木真已击败蒙古高原上所有敌对部落联盟：据《蒙古秘史》毒死其父的塔塔儿人、曾是其庇护者的王汗所领的克烈部、阿尔泰山的乃蛮部，以及由安答转为仇敌的札木合。这年春天，草原首领们会聚于斡难河源，树起九斿白纛。

《蒙古秘史》所记载的与其说是加冕，不如说是一次重组。铁木真称成吉思汗，任命九十五名千户长，把旧有部落打散编入只效忠于他的十进制单位；他把宿卫与箭筒士扩充为万人怯薛，并任命义弟失吉忽秃忽为大断事官，下令以畏兀儿文字记录判决。

自称上天选中铁木真的萨满帖卜腾格里不久企图与其分庭抗礼，结果被处死。这个新国家“大蒙古国”为战争而建，五年之内便进攻金朝。

summary.en: After Otrar’s governor Inalchuq massacred a Mongol trade caravan in 1218 and the shah executed Genghis Khan’s envoy, the khan’s sons besieged the city for months; its fall opened the Mongol conquest of Khwarazm.
summary.zh: 1218年讹答剌守将亦纳勒术屠杀蒙古商队，花剌子模沙又处死成吉思汗的使者；成吉思汗诸子随后围城数月，此城陷落揭开了蒙古征服花剌子模的序幕。

sources.title: Ata-Malik Juvaini, Tarikh-i Jahangushay (The History of the World-Conqueror), tr. J. A. Boyle (1958)
An-Nasawi, Sirat al-Sultan Jalal al-Din Mankubirti
Wikidata Q111943842

story.en:
In 1218 a caravan of some 450 Muslim merchants sent by Genghis Khan arrived at Otrar, the Khwarazmian frontier city on the Syr Darya. The governor, Inalchuq, a kinsman of the shah’s powerful mother Terken Khatun, accused them of spying, seized their goods and had them killed. When Genghis sent an envoy to demand Inalchuq’s surrender, Shah Muhammad II had the envoy executed and his escorts’ beards shaved.

Genghis came in person the next autumn. He left his sons Chagatai and Ögedei to besiege Otrar while other columns struck elsewhere. The city held for about five months; after it fell, Inalchuq fought on in the citadel for another month, reportedly throwing bricks when his arrows ran out, before he was taken and put to death. A later story says molten silver was poured into his eyes and ears.

The affair gave Genghis Khan his cause, and the war it began destroyed the Khwarazmian state within three years.
story.zh:
1218年，成吉思汗派出的一支约450名穆斯林商人组成的商队抵达花剌子模锡尔河边城讹答剌。守将亦纳勒术是苏丹之母、权势显赫的秃儿罕可敦的亲族，他诬指商人为间谍，没收货物并将其杀害。成吉思汗遣使要求交出亦纳勒术，摩诃末二世却处死使者，并剃去随从的胡须。

次年秋，成吉思汗亲征，留察合台与窝阔台围攻讹答剌，其余各路分兵他处。城池坚守约五个月，城破后亦纳勒术又在内堡死守一个月，据说箭尽之后仍投掷砖块，最终被俘处死。后世传说称蒙古人将熔化的银液灌入他的眼耳。

此事给了成吉思汗出兵的理由，由此引发的战争在三年之内摧毁了花剌子模国家。

name.en: Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire

summary.en: Genghis Khan’s armies destroyed the Khwarazmian empire, razing Bukhara, Samarkand, Gurganj, Merv and Nishapur and pursuing Jalal al-Din to the Indus; the conquest killed vast numbers and brought Transoxiana and Khurasan under Mongol rule.
summary.zh: 成吉思汗大军摧毁花剌子模帝国，相继攻破布哈拉、撒马尔罕、玉龙杰赤、梅尔夫和内沙布尔，并追击札兰丁至印度河；此役杀戮极重，河中与呼罗珊从此归于蒙古统治。

label.zh: 大军集结于额尔齐斯河

sources.title: Ata-Malik Juvaini, Tarikh-i Jahangushay (The History of the World-Conqueror), tr. J. A. Boyle (1958)
Rashid al-Din, Jami al-Tawarikh (tr. W. M. Thackston)
Timothy May, The Mongol Conquests in World History (2012)
Wikidata Q431177

note: The route combines several Mongol columns (Gurganj by Jochi, Chagatai and Ögedei; Merv and Nishapur by Tolui; the Indus by Genghis Khan).

story.en:
On paper Shah Muhammad II had the larger army, but he distrusted his Qangli Turkish commanders and spread his troops among the city garrisons instead of meeting the Mongols in the field. Genghis Khan took the cities one by one: Otrar, Bukhara and Samarkand in 1219–20, then Gurganj, Merv and Nishapur in 1221. Juvaini says the Mongols broke the dams of the Amu Darya to flood Gurganj.

The shah himself fled west across Iran, pursued by Jebe and Subutai, and died on an island in the Caspian in the winter of 1220–21. At Nishapur, where Genghis’s son-in-law Toquchar had been killed, the city was razed and, by the chroniclers’ account, even its cats and dogs were slain. His son Jalal al-Din raised new armies in Afghanistan until Genghis caught him on the Indus.

The cities of Khurasan and Transoxiana lost much of their population and irrigation. Mongol power now bordered Iran and the Caucasus, the base from which Hulagu would later found the Ilkhanate.
story.zh:
账面上花剌子模苏丹摩诃末二世兵力更多，但他不信任康里突厥将领，把军队分散到各城驻守，而不在野战中迎击蒙古人。成吉思汗逐一攻城：1219—1220年取讹答剌、布哈拉、撒马尔罕，1221年取玉龙杰赤、梅尔夫和内沙布尔。志费尼记载，蒙古人掘开阿姆河堤坝水淹玉龙杰赤。

苏丹本人一路西逃穿越伊朗，遭哲别和速不台追击，1220—1221年冬死于里海中的一座小岛。成吉思汗的女婿脱忽察儿战死于内沙布尔，该城因此被夷为平地，据史家所记连猫狗都未幸免。其子札兰丁在阿富汗重新募兵，直到在印度河畔被成吉思汗追上。

呼罗珊和河中地区的城市人口和灌溉系统损失惨重。蒙古势力从此与伊朗和高加索接壤，旭烈兀日后正是以此为基地建立伊儿汗国。

summary.en: Genghis Khan took Bukhara in February 1220 after its Turkic garrison fled; Juvaini says he addressed its notables from the pulpit of the Friday mosque, calling himself the punishment of God, before the city burned.
summary.zh: 1220年2月，布哈拉的突厥守军逃散后成吉思汗攻占该城；据志费尼记载，他在聚礼清真寺讲坛上对城中显贵自称“上天之罚”，随后城市被焚。

sources.title: Ata-Malik Juvaini, Tarikh-i Jahangushay (The History of the World-Conqueror), tr. J. A. Boyle (1958)
Timothy May, The Mongol Conquests in World History (2012)
Wikidata Q110970851

summary.en: Khwarazm’s new capital surrendered after a short siege in March 1220; the Mongols massacred much of the garrison and deported its artisans, and the old city on the Afrasiyab mound was never fully reoccupied.
summary.zh: 1220年3月，花剌子模新都撒马尔罕在短暂围攻后投降；蒙古人屠杀大部分守军并迁走工匠，阿夫拉西阿卜高地上的旧城此后再未完全恢复。

sources.title: Ata-Malik Juvaini, Tarikh-i Jahangushay (The History of the World-Conqueror), tr. J. A. Boyle (1958)
Timothy May, The Mongol Conquests in World History (2012)
Wikidata Q7510363

story.en:
Shah Muhammad had made Samarkand his capital only a few years earlier and packed it with a garrison that Juvaini puts at 110,000 men, many of them Qangli Turks, behind newly built walls. Genghis Khan arrived in March 1220 driving crowds of prisoners from Bukhara ahead of his army, so that the defenders saw what looked like an endless host.

After a few days of fighting the Turkish troops, hoping to be taken into Mongol service as fellow nomads, came out and surrendered, and the city’s religious leaders opened the gates. The Mongols drove the inhabitants out to be counted, killed the Turkish garrison, and stormed the citadel. Some 30,000 craftsmen were divided among the Mongol princes and sent east.

When the Daoist master Changchun passed through on his way to meet Genghis Khan in 1221, he was told that only about a quarter of the former population remained. The old city on the Afrasiyab plateau was abandoned, and later Samarkand grew up to the south.
story.zh:
撒马尔罕成为花剌子模首都才没几年，苏丹在新修的城墙后屯驻重兵，志费尼称有11万人，其中多为康里突厥人。1220年3月，成吉思汗驱赶从布哈拉掳来的大批俘虏走在军前，守军望去只见敌军漫山遍野。

激战数日后，突厥守军以为同为游牧者可以被蒙古收编，便出城投降，城中宗教领袖也打开城门。蒙古人把居民驱出城外清点，屠杀突厥守军，并攻破内城。约三万名工匠被分给诸王，押往东方。

1221年道士丘处机西行觐见成吉思汗途经此地，听说城中居民仅剩原来的四分之一左右。阿夫拉西阿卜高地上的旧城从此荒废，后来的撒马尔罕在其南面重建。

summary.en: Tolui’s army took Merv, one of the great cities of the Islamic world, after it surrendered in February 1221 and slaughtered most of its people; the oasis never regained its former size.
summary.zh: 1221年2月，梅尔夫这座伊斯兰世界的大城向拖雷军投降后，大部分居民遭屠戮；该绿洲此后再未恢复昔日规模。

sources.title: Ata-Malik Juvaini, Tarikh-i Jahangushay (The History of the World-Conqueror), tr. J. A. Boyle (1958)
UNESCO World Heritage List: State Historical and Cultural Park “Ancient Merv”
Wikidata Q39081822

note: Contemporary death tolls (over a million) are not credible as counts, though the massacre was real and enormous.

summary.en: Genghis Khan caught Jalal al-Din Mingburnu on the banks of the Indus and destroyed his army; the Khwarazmian prince escaped by riding his horse into the river and fled to the Delhi Sultanate.
summary.zh: 成吉思汗在印度河畔追上札兰丁并歼灭其军，这位花剌子模王子策马跃入河中脱身，逃往德里苏丹国。

sources.title: Ata-Malik Juvaini, Tarikh-i Jahangushay (The History of the World-Conqueror), tr. J. A. Boyle (1958)
An-Nasawi, Sirat al-Sultan Jalal al-Din Mankubirti
Wikidata Q3269760

summary.en: On a reconnaissance raid around the Caspian, Jebe and Subutai lured a coalition of Rus’ princes and Cumans to the Kalka river and destroyed it; the captured princes were crushed beneath a victory platform.
summary.zh: 哲别与速不台绕里海进行远程侦察，将罗斯诸王公与钦察人的联军诱至迦勒迦河并将其击溃；被俘的王公被压死在庆功的木台之下。

label.en: Leaves Khurasan in pursuit of the shah
label.zh: 自呼罗珊追击花剌子模沙

sources.title: The Chronicle of Novgorod 1016–1471, tr. R. Michell & N. Forbes (1914)
Timothy May, The Mongol Conquests in World History (2012)
Carl Sverdrup, The Mongol Conquests: The Military Operations of Genghis Khan and Sübe’etei (2017)
Wikidata Q570204

note: Route stops are approximate; the Volga Bulgar episode is reported by Ibn al-Athir.

story.en:
Sent to hunt down the fleeing Khwarazm shah, Jebe and Subutai rode on through Iran, defeated the Georgians, and crossed the Caucasus in 1222. North of the mountains they split the Alans from their Cuman allies by bribing the Cumans, then defeated each in turn. The Cuman khan Köten fled to his son-in-law, Prince Mstislav of Galich, warning that the Rus’ would be next.

A coalition of Rus’ princes marched into the steppe and killed the Mongol envoys sent to them. The Mongols retreated for days, drawing the pursuers out, then turned at the Kalka river in late May 1223. The Cumans broke first and fled through the Rus’ lines. Mstislav of Kyiv held out in a fortified camp for three days and surrendered on a promise that no princely blood would be shed; the Mongols kept the letter of that promise by laying the captives under boards and feasting on top until they were crushed.

The raiders went home through the Volga Bulgar lands, where Ibn al-Athir says they were ambushed. They returned in strength in 1237.
story.zh:
哲别和速不台奉命追击逃亡的花剌子模苏丹，一路穿越伊朗，击败格鲁吉亚人，并于1222年翻越高加索山。在山北，他们以财物收买钦察人，使其与阿兰人分离，再各个击破。钦察首领忽滩逃往女婿加利奇王公姆斯季斯拉夫处，警告说罗斯人将是下一个目标。

罗斯诸王公组成联军进入草原，并杀死前来的蒙古使者。蒙古人连日后退，诱敌深入，1223年5月底在迦勒迦河畔回身反击。钦察人首先溃逃，冲乱了罗斯军阵。基辅王公姆斯季斯拉夫在设防营地坚守三日，以“不流王公之血”的承诺为条件投降；蒙古人按字面守诺，把俘虏压在木板下，在板上设宴，将其活活压死。

这支远征军经伏尔加保加尔人的地界东返，据伊本·艾西尔记载曾遭其伏击。1237年，蒙古大军卷土重来。

name.zh: 阿里不哥与忽必烈汗位之争

summary.en: After Möngke’s death his brothers Kublai and Ariq Böke were each elected Great Khan; Kublai won by cutting Karakorum’s grain supply from China, but the empire’s unity was lost and it split into four khanates.
summary.zh: 蒙哥死后，其弟忽必烈与阿里不哥分别被推举为大汗；忽必烈切断汉地对哈拉和林的粮食供应而获胜，但帝国统一从此瓦解，分裂为四大汗国。

sources.title: Morris Rossabi, Khubilai Khan: His Life and Times (1988)
Timothy May, The Mongol Conquests in World History (2012)
Wikidata Q16871984

story.en:
When the Great Khan Möngke died besieging a Song fortress in Sichuan in 1259, two of his brothers moved at once. Ariq Böke, left in charge of Mongolia, held Karakorum and was elected khan there by a kurultai in 1260. Kublai, campaigning in China, had himself proclaimed at his own city of Kaiping (Shangdu) that May. Each claimed to be the rightful successor.

The war was decided less by battles than by supplies. Karakorum depended on grain from north China, which Kublai controlled, and he cut it off. Ariq Böke’s chosen ruler for Central Asia, Alghu, turned against him. Starved and abandoned, Ariq Böke surrendered at Shangdu in 1264. Kublai spared him, and he died two years later.

Kublai had won the throne, but the other branches of the family never fully accepted him. The Golden Horde and the Ilkhanate were already at war over the Caucasus, and Ögedei’s grandson Kaidu fought him from Central Asia for decades. The single Mongol empire had become four.
story.zh:
1259年大汗蒙哥在四川围攻宋军堡垒时去世，他的两个弟弟立即行动。留守蒙古本土的阿里不哥据有哈拉和林，1260年在当地忽里勒台上被推举为大汗；正在中国作战的忽必烈则于同年五月在自己的开平府（上都）即位。双方都自称合法继承人。

这场战争与其说靠会战，不如说靠补给决胜。哈拉和林依赖华北粮食，而华北在忽必烈手中，他切断了粮道。阿里不哥委派治理中亚的阿鲁忽也倒戈相向。饥困孤立之下，阿里不哥于1264年在上都投降。忽必烈赦免了他，他两年后去世。

忽必烈赢得了汗位，但家族其他支系从未真正接受他。金帐汗国与伊儿汗国已为高加索开战，窝阔台之孙海都在中亚与他对抗数十年。统一的蒙古帝国就此分为四大汗国。

name.zh: 比比哈努姆清真寺兴建

summary.en: Begun after the Indian campaign with plunder and craftsmen from Delhi, Timur’s congregational mosque in Samarkand was among the largest in the Islamic world; its hurried construction left it prone to collapse.
summary.zh: 帖木儿征印度归来后，以从德里掠来的财富和工匠在撒马尔罕兴建这座聚礼清真寺，其规模居伊斯兰世界前列；因施工仓促，此后屡有坍塌。

sources.title: Ruy González de Clavijo, Embassy to Tamerlane 1403–1406 (tr. Guy Le Strange, 1928)
UNESCO World Heritage List: Samarkand – Crossroad of Cultures
Wikidata Q679218

note: Wikidata records 1404, the completion date.

name.zh: 古尔-艾米尔陵（帖木儿陵）

summary.en: Built for Timur’s grandson Muhammad Sultan, who died in 1403, the ribbed turquoise-domed mausoleum became the dynastic tomb of Timur, Shah Rukh and Ulugh Beg and a model for Mughal tombs.
summary.zh: 此陵原为1403年去世的帖木儿之孙穆罕默德·苏丹而建，其带棱纹的青绿色穹顶陵墓后成为帖木儿、沙哈鲁和兀鲁伯的王朝墓地，并成为莫卧儿陵墓的范本。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Samarkand – Crossroad of Cultures
Lisa Golombek & Donald Wilber, The Timurid Architecture of Iran and Turan (1988)
Wikidata Q1256223

name.en: Ulugh Beg Madrasa on the Registan
name.zh: 雷吉斯坦广场兀鲁伯经学院

summary.en: Ulugh Beg founded this madrasa on Samarkand’s Registan, where astronomy and mathematics were taught alongside religious sciences; it is the oldest of the three madrasas framing the square.
summary.zh: 兀鲁伯在撒马尔罕雷吉斯坦广场创建这所经学院，除宗教学科外还讲授天文与数学；它是环绕广场的三座经学院中最古老的一座。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Samarkand – Crossroad of Cultures
Lisa Golombek & Donald Wilber, The Timurid Architecture of Iran and Turan (1988)
Wikidata Q492144

summary.en: Ulugh Beg’s three-storey observatory housed a huge meridian arc of about 40 m radius; his team, including al-Kashi and Qadi-zada al-Rumi, compiled the Zij-i Sultani star catalogue, the most precise since Ptolemy.
summary.zh: 兀鲁伯的三层天文台内建有半径约40米的巨型子午仪；他与卡西、卡迪扎德·鲁米等学者编成《苏丹历数书》星表，是托勒密以来最精确的星表。

sources.title: Aydın Sayılı, The Observatory in Islam (1960)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ulugh Beg
Wikidata Q608580

note: Construction is usually dated 1424–1429 (Wikidata: 1420s); the Zij-i Sultani was completed c. 1437 and revised to 1449, when the observatory was abandoned.

story.en:
Ulugh Beg, governor of Samarkand for his father Shah Rukh, was a prince who preferred mathematics to war. In the 1420s he built an observatory on a hill north-east of the city. Its chief instrument was a vast meridian arc, a sextant of about 40 metres radius sunk into a trench in the rock, from which the positions of the Sun and stars could be read with unusual precision.

He gathered the best astronomers of the Islamic world there, including Ghiyath al-Din al-Kashi and Qadi-zada al-Rumi. Their Zij-i Sultani gave tables for the planets and a catalogue of 1,018 stars, the first major independent star catalogue since Ptolemy’s, and a value for the sidereal year within about a minute of the modern one.

In 1449, two years after becoming head of the dynasty, Ulugh Beg was killed on his son’s orders, and the observatory was soon pulled down. In 1908 the archaeologist Vasily Vyatkin found the buried arc. Ulugh Beg’s star catalogue was published in Oxford in 1665.
story.zh:
兀鲁伯替父亲沙哈鲁治理撒马尔罕，是一位比起征战更爱数学的王子。1420年代，他在城东北的一座山丘上修建天文台。主要仪器是一具巨大的子午弧仪，即半径约40米、嵌入岩石沟槽中的六分仪，可以异常精确地测定太阳和恒星的位置。

他在此汇集了伊斯兰世界最优秀的天文学家，包括卡西和卡迪扎德·鲁米。他们编成的《苏丹历表》载有行星表和一份收录1018颗恒星的星表，这是自托勒密以来第一部重要的独立星表；其测定的恒星年长度与现代数值仅差约一分钟。

1449年，成为家族之首才两年的兀鲁伯被儿子下令杀害，天文台随后被拆毁。1908年，考古学家维亚特金发现了深埋地下的弧仪。兀鲁伯的星表于1665年在牛津出版。

name.en: Kerei and Janibek found the Kazakh Khanate
name.zh: 克烈与贾尼别克建立哈萨克汗国

summary.en: The Jochid sultans Kerei and Janibek broke with Abu’l-Khayr’s Uzbek ulus and led their followers to the Chu and Talas valleys under Moghulistan’s protection; their khanate is regarded as the origin of Kazakh statehood.
summary.zh: 术赤后裔克烈与贾尼别克两位苏丹脱离阿布海尔的乌兹别克兀鲁思，率部众迁至楚河与塔拉斯河流域，受东察合台汗国庇护；他们建立的汗国被视为哈萨克国家的开端。

sources.title: Mirza Muhammad Haidar Dughlat, Tarikh-i Rashidi (tr. N. Elias & E. Denison Ross, 1895)
Martha Brill Olcott, The Kazakhs, 2nd ed. (1995)

note: No separate Wikidata item exists for the event, so no QID is given (Q1433867 is the khanate, inception 1465). Mirza Haidar gives AH 870 (1465–66); other dates (1456, 1459) are proposed. Coordinates approximate the Chu valley.

story.en:
In the mid-fifteenth century the Uzbek khan Abu’l-Khayr ruled the steppe north of the Syr Darya. After the Oirats defeated him badly near Sygnak in 1457, two Jochid sultans, Kerei and Janibek, who had their own claims to rule, broke away and led their followers east into Moghulistan. Its khan, Esen Buqa, welcomed them as a buffer and let them graze the western Chu valley.

The historian Mirza Haidar Dughlat, writing in the next century, says the newcomers came to be called Qazaq, “free wanderers”, and that their numbers swelled to some 200,000 as Abu’l-Khayr’s subjects deserted him. When Abu’l-Khayr died around 1468, his ulus fell apart and many more joined the Kazakhs.

Under Janibek’s son Kasym Khan in the early sixteenth century the khanate ruled most of the steppe, by Haidar’s figure a million people. Its division into three hordes, the Senior, Middle and Junior Zhuz, shaped Kazakh society until the Russian conquest. Kazakhstan celebrated the khanate’s 550th anniversary in 2015.
story.zh:
十五世纪中叶，乌兹别克汗阿布海尔统治锡尔河以北的草原。1457年他在昔格纳黑附近惨败于瓦剌之后，两位各有继承权主张的术赤系苏丹克烈与贾尼别克脱离他，率部众东迁至东察合台汗国（蒙兀儿斯坦）。其汗也先不花视他们为屏障，允许他们在楚河西部河谷游牧。

十六世纪的史家米尔咱·海达尔·杜格拉特记载，这些新来者被称为“哈萨克”，意为“自由的漫游者”；随着阿布海尔的属民纷纷来投，其人数增至约20万。阿布海尔约于1468年去世后，其兀鲁思瓦解，更多人投奔哈萨克人。

十六世纪初贾尼别克之子哈斯木汗在位时，汗国控制了草原大部，据海达尔所记人口达百万。汗国分为大、中、小三个玉兹，这一格局一直延续到俄国征服。2015年哈萨克斯坦隆重纪念哈萨克汗国建立550周年。

summary.en: Shaybanid Uzbek forces under Ubaydullah annihilated a Safavid army under Najm-e Sani that was backing Babur’s bid to retake Samarkand, fixing the Uzbek–Persian frontier and ending Babur’s Central Asian ambitions.
summary.zh: 乌拜杜拉率领的昔班尼乌兹别克军队全歼了纳吉姆·萨尼统率、支持巴布尔夺回撒马尔罕的萨法维军队，由此确定乌兹别克与波斯的边界，巴布尔在中亚的雄心也就此破灭。

sources.title: Babur, Baburnama (tr. Wheeler M. Thackston, 1996)
R. D. McChesney, “Central Asia vi. In the 16th–18th centuries”, Encyclopaedia Iranica
Wikidata Q4138186

name.zh: 清朝平定准噶尔与准噶尔人大屠杀

summary.en: Qing armies under the Qianlong emperor destroyed the Dzungar Khanate after Amursana’s revolt; war, massacre and smallpox killed most of the Dzungar Oirats, and their lands became part of Qing Xinjiang.
summary.zh: 阿睦尔撒纳叛清后，乾隆帝派兵彻底摧毁准噶尔汗国；战争、屠杀与天花使准噶尔卫拉特人大部分死亡，其故地并入清朝新疆。

sources.title: Peter C. Perdue, China Marches West: The Qing Conquest of Central Eurasia (2005)
Wei Yuan, Shengwuji (Record of Imperial Military Exploits) (1842)
Wikidata Q4462644

note: Estimates of the death toll vary widely; Perdue follows Wei Yuan’s figure that some 40% died of smallpox and 30% were killed.

story.en:
The Dzungar Khanate was the last great nomad empire, a rival of the Qing for half a century. After its ruler Galdan Tseren died in 1745 his heirs fought one another, and in 1754 the noble Amursana fled to Beijing and offered to help the Qianlong emperor conquer his homeland. A Qing army took the Ili valley almost unopposed in 1755.

Amursana had expected to be made khan of all the Oirats. Instead the Qing planned to divide them among four khans, and he rose in revolt. Qianlong now ordered that the Dzungars be destroyed, and his commanders killed men of fighting age and many others. Smallpox spread through the camps at the same time. Amursana fled to Russian Siberia, where he died of smallpox in 1757.

The nineteenth-century scholar Wei Yuan wrote that of the Dzungars’ several hundred thousand households, four in ten died of smallpox, two in ten fled to Russia or the Kazakhs, and three in ten were killed by the Qing armies. These proportions are a later estimate, not a count; modern historians put the population before the war at perhaps 600,000. The Qing repopulated Ili with Manchu bannermen, Xibe and Solon soldiers, Han farmers and Muslim cultivators from the Tarim oases.
story.zh:
准噶尔汗国是最后一个伟大的游牧帝国，与清朝争衡半个世纪。1745年首领噶尔丹策零去世后，其子嗣相互残杀；1754年贵族阿睦尔撒纳投奔北京，表示愿助乾隆帝征服故土。1755年清军几乎未遇抵抗便占领伊犁河谷。

阿睦尔撒纳原本期望成为统领卫拉特全体的大汗，清廷却打算分设四汗，他于是起兵反清。乾隆遂下令剿灭准噶尔，清军诛杀了青壮男子以及其他许多人；与此同时天花在营地中蔓延。阿睦尔撒纳逃往俄国西伯利亚，1757年死于天花。

十九世纪学者魏源写道，准噶尔“数十万户”中，十分之四死于天花，十分之二逃入俄罗斯和哈萨克，十分之三被清军所杀。这些比例是后人的估算而非统计；现代史家推测战前准噶尔人口约为60万。清朝随后向伊犁迁入满洲八旗、锡伯与索伦官兵、汉族农民以及来自塔里木绿洲的穆斯林垦民。

summary.en: General Mikhail Chernyaev stormed Tashkent, the largest city of the Kokand Khanate, without clear orders from St Petersburg; it became the capital of the Russian Governorate-General of Turkestan in 1867.
summary.zh: 切尔尼亚耶夫将军未经圣彼得堡明确授权便攻陷浩罕汗国最大的城市塔什干；1867年该城成为俄国突厥斯坦总督区首府。

sources.title: Alexander Morrison, The Russian Conquest of Central Asia: A Study in Imperial Expansion, 1814–1914 (2020)
Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021)
Wikidata Q4527027

note: Russian sources use Julian dates (city stormed 15–17 June O.S. = 27–29 June N.S. 1865).

story.en:
By 1864 Russian columns advancing from Siberia and the Syr Darya had joined up at Chimkent, and Tashkent, the commercial centre of the Kokand Khanate with perhaps 100,000 people, lay a few days’ march south. St Petersburg wanted a defensible frontier, not a war for a great city. General Mikhail Chernyaev decided otherwise.

In May 1865 Kokand’s regent Alimqul was killed in a clash outside the walls. In June, with fewer than 2,000 men, Chernyaev stormed the city at night through the Kamelan gate. After two days of street fighting the elders surrendered. Chernyaev told them they could keep their religion and customs, and toured the bazaar without an escort to show his confidence.

The government accepted the fait accompli but recalled him the next year. In 1867 Tashkent became the seat of the Governor-General of Turkestan under Konstantin von Kaufman, and a Russian new town of straight avenues grew up beside the old city, the start of the colonial capital that became Soviet Tashkent.
story.zh:
到1864年，自西伯利亚和锡尔河方向推进的俄军已在奇姆肯特会合。浩罕汗国的商业中心塔什干约有十万人口，就在南面数日行程之外。圣彼得堡想要的是一条可守的边界，而不是为一座大城开战，切尔尼亚耶夫将军却另有主张。

1865年5月，浩罕摄政阿利姆库尔在城外交战中阵亡。6月，切尔尼亚耶夫以不足两千人在夜间经卡梅兰门攻城，巷战两日后长老们投降。他向他们保证可以保留宗教和习俗，还不带卫兵巡视巴扎以示从容。

政府接受了既成事实，但第二年就将他召回。1867年塔什干成为考夫曼领导下的突厥斯坦总督府驻地，旧城旁兴起了街道笔直的俄罗斯新城，这就是后来苏联塔什干的殖民首府雏形。

summary.en: After a failed attack in 1879, General Mikhail Skobelev besieged the Teke Turkmen fortress of Geok Tepe and stormed it in January 1881, followed by the slaughter of fleeing defenders and civilians; it completed Russia’s conquest of the Turkmen.
summary.zh: 1879年进攻失败后，斯科别列夫将军围攻帖克土库曼人的格奥克捷佩要塞，于1881年1月攻破并屠杀出逃的守军与平民，完成了俄国对土库曼人的征服。

summary.en: Mongolian revolutionaries led by Damdin Sükhbaatar, backed by the Red Army, expelled Baron Ungern-Sternberg’s White forces from Urga; the regime they founded proclaimed the Mongolian People’s Republic, the second communist state, in 1924.
summary.zh: 苏赫巴托尔领导的蒙古革命者在苏俄红军支持下，将恩琴男爵的白军逐出库伦；他们建立的政权于1924年宣布成立蒙古人民共和国，成为世界上第二个社会主义国家。

sources.title: Charles R. Bawden, The Modern History of Mongolia (1968)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Mongolia
Wikidata Q2081446

story.en:
After the fall of the Qing, Outer Mongolia had declared independence under the Bogd Khan, but in 1919 Chinese troops reoccupied Urga and ended its autonomy. In February 1921 the White Russian warlord Baron Roman von Ungern-Sternberg drove the Chinese out and restored the Bogd Khan, then ruled the city with arbitrary terror.

A small Mongolian People’s Party, founded in 1920, had sent a delegation including Damdin Sükhbaatar and Khorloogiin Choibalsan to seek Soviet help; a popular story says Sükhbaatar carried their appeal hidden in the handle of his whip. In March 1921 their partisans took Kyakhta on the Russian border, and in July, together with the Red Army, they entered Urga. Ungern was captured and shot in Novosibirsk.

The new government kept the Bogd Khan as a figurehead. Sükhbaatar died in 1923 and the Bogd Khan in 1924, after which the Mongolian People’s Republic was proclaimed and Urga renamed Ulaanbaatar, “Red Hero”. For seventy years Mongolia was a close Soviet ally.
story.zh:
清朝灭亡后，外蒙古在博克多汗领导下宣布独立，但1919年中国军队重新进驻库伦，取消了其自治。1921年2月，白俄军阀恩琴（温甘伦）驱逐中国军队，扶博克多汗复位，随后在城中实行恣意恐怖统治。

1920年成立的蒙古人民党派出包括苏赫巴托尔和乔巴山在内的代表团寻求苏俄援助；据一则流传甚广的故事，苏赫巴托尔把求援信藏在马鞭柄中带出。1921年3月，其游击队攻占俄蒙边境的恰克图（买卖城），7月与红军一同进入库伦。恩琴被俘，在新西伯利亚被枪决。

新政府保留博克多汗为虚君。苏赫巴托尔于1923年、博克多汗于1924年相继去世，此后蒙古人民共和国宣告成立，库伦改名乌兰巴托，意为“红色英雄”。此后七十年，蒙古一直是苏联的亲密盟友。

name.en: National delimitation of Soviet Central Asia

summary.en: Soviet authorities dissolved the Turkestan, Bukharan and Khorezm republics and redrew the region on ethnic lines, creating the Uzbek and Turkmen SSRs and autonomous units that later became Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan.
summary.zh: 苏联当局撤销突厥斯坦、布哈拉和花剌子模共和国，按民族重新划分该地区，设立乌兹别克和土库曼加盟共和国以及日后成为哈萨克斯坦、吉尔吉斯斯坦和塔吉克斯坦的自治单位。

sources.title: Arne Haugen, The Establishment of National Republics in Soviet Central Asia (2003)
Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021)
Wikidata Q56558925

story.en:
In 1924 Soviet Central Asia still followed old political lines: the Turkestan Autonomous Republic, the former colonial governorate, and the Bukharan and Khorezm people’s republics that had replaced the emir and the khan. Moscow and local communists decided to replace them with republics named after nations, on the principle that each people should have its own territory.

Commissions drew borders using census data on language and identity, which often did not match how people lived. The Uzbek SSR, created in October 1924, received the great cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and the Fergana valley, and a Tajik autonomous republic within it. The Turkmen SSR was created at the same time; the Kazakh and Kyrgyz units became full republics in 1936. Tajikistan became a separate republic in 1929 and gained Khujand, but not Samarkand or Bukhara, whose Persian-speaking populations Tajik intellectuals claimed.

The new map created the five states that became independent in 1991, and the enclaves and tangled borders of the Fergana valley.
story.zh:
1924年时，苏联中亚仍沿用旧的政治区划：由沙俄总督区演变而来的突厥斯坦自治共和国，以及取代埃米尔和汗的布哈拉、花剌子模两个人民共和国。莫斯科与当地共产党人决定以民族命名的共和国取而代之，原则是每个民族都应有自己的领土。

划界委员会依据有关语言和认同的人口统计来划线，但这常常与人们的实际生活不符。1924年10月成立的乌兹别克苏维埃社会主义共和国获得撒马尔罕、布哈拉和费尔干纳谷地等大城市，境内还设有塔吉克自治共和国。土库曼加盟共和国同时建立；哈萨克和吉尔吉斯单位于1936年升格为加盟共和国。塔吉克斯坦于1929年成为独立的加盟共和国并获得苦盏，但没有得到塔吉克知识分子所主张的、以波斯语人口为主的撒马尔罕和布哈拉。

新地图奠定了1991年独立的中亚五国，也留下了费尔干纳谷地错综复杂的飞地与边界。

name.en: First Soviet atomic test at Semipalatinsk
name.zh: 苏联首次核试验（塞米巴拉金斯克）

summary.en: The Soviet Union detonated its first atomic bomb, RDS-1, at the Semipalatinsk test site in Kazakhstan; some 456 tests there over four decades exposed nearby populations to radiation until the site closed in 1991.
summary.zh: 苏联在哈萨克斯坦塞米巴拉金斯克试验场引爆第一颗原子弹RDS-1；此后四十年间在此进行了约456次核试验，周边居民长期受辐射危害，直至1991年试验场关闭。

sources.title: David Holloway, Stalin and the Bomb (1994)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Semipalatinsk
Wikidata Q586755

story.en:
At 7 a.m. on 29 August 1949 a plutonium bomb on a tower in the steppe west of Semipalatinsk exploded with a force of about 22 kilotons. The device, RDS-1, closely followed the American Fat Man design, which Soviet intelligence had obtained through spies including Klaus Fuchs. Its scientific director, Igor Kurchatov, and the security chief Lavrentiy Beria watched from a bunker.

American aircraft detected radioactive debris over the Pacific within days, and on 23 September President Truman announced that the Soviet Union had the bomb. The American monopoly had lasted four years; the arms race that followed defined the Cold War.

For the Kazakhs living around the Polygon, as the 18,000 square kilometre test site was called, the cost was long. Over 40 years some 456 nuclear tests were held there, more than a hundred of them in the open air, and villagers were rarely warned or moved. In 1989 the poet Olzhas Suleimenov founded the Nevada-Semipalatinsk anti-nuclear movement, and on 29 August 1991 Kazakhstan closed the site.
story.zh:
1949年8月29日早晨7时，塞米巴拉金斯克以西草原上一座铁塔上的钚弹爆炸，当量约2.2万吨TNT。这枚名为RDS-1的装置几乎照搬美国“胖子”原子弹的设计，苏联情报机构通过克劳斯·富克斯等间谍获得了相关资料。科学负责人库尔恰托夫和安全主管贝利亚在掩体中观看了爆炸。

数日之内美国飞机便在太平洋上空探测到放射性尘埃，9月23日杜鲁门总统宣布苏联已拥有原子弹。美国的核垄断只维持了四年，随之而来的军备竞赛界定了冷战。

对居住在这片面积1.8万平方公里、被称为“波利贡”的试验场周围的哈萨克人来说，代价是长期的。四十年间这里进行了约456次核试验，其中一百多次在大气层中，村民很少得到警告或疏散。1989年诗人奥尔扎斯·苏莱曼诺夫发起“内华达—塞米巴拉金斯克”反核运动，1991年8月29日哈萨克斯坦关闭了试验场。

summary.en: Khrushchev’s programme sent hundreds of thousands of volunteers to plough the steppe of northern Kazakhstan and Siberia for wheat; harvests rose at first, but erosion and dust storms followed, and settlers changed Kazakhstan’s ethnic balance.
summary.zh: 赫鲁晓夫的计划派遣数十万志愿者开垦哈萨克斯坦北部和西伯利亚的草原种植小麦；初期收成增加，但随后出现水土流失和沙尘暴，移民也改变了哈萨克斯坦的民族构成。

name.zh: 加加林乘东方一号从拜科努尔升空

summary.en: Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space, launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on the Kazakh steppe aboard Vostok 1 for a single 108-minute orbit of the Earth.
summary.zh: 尤里·加加林乘东方一号飞船从哈萨克草原上的拜科努尔航天发射场升空，绕地球一周历时108分钟，成为进入太空的第一人。

sources.title: Asif A. Siddiqi, Challenge to Apollo: The Soviet Union and the Space Race (NASA SP-2000-4408, 2000)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Vostok
Wikidata Q182524

story.en:
At 9:07 Moscow time on 12 April 1961 Senior Lieutenant Yuri Gagarin, a 27-year-old pilot from a village near Smolensk, lifted off from the launch pad in the Kazakh steppe at Tyuratam. As the R-7 rocket rose he called out “Poyekhali!” (“Let’s go!”). The flight was controlled automatically; Gagarin had a sealed envelope with the code to unlock manual control in an emergency.

Vostok 1 made a single orbit in 108 minutes. On re-entry the descent module failed at first to separate cleanly from the equipment section and tumbled, but the cables burned through. As planned, Gagarin ejected at about 7 kilometres and landed by parachute in a field near Engels on the Volga, where a farmer’s wife and her daughter were the first to meet him.

The launch site was officially called Baikonur, after a mining settlement hundreds of kilometres away, to mislead Western intelligence. Gagarin became the most famous man in the world, and the Space Race gained a new urgency: within weeks President Kennedy committed the United States to the Moon.
story.zh:
1961年4月12日莫斯科时间9时07分，来自斯摩棱斯克附近村庄、27岁的空军上尉尤里·加加林从哈萨克草原丘拉塔姆的发射台升空。R-7火箭上升时，他喊出了“Поехали！”（“出发了！”）。飞行由自动系统控制，加加林身边有一个密封信封，内有紧急情况下解锁手动操纵的密码。

“东方1号”用108分钟绕地球一周。再入时，返回舱起初未能与设备舱干净分离而翻滚，后来连接电缆烧断才脱离。按计划，加加林在约7公里高度弹射，跳伞降落在伏尔加河畔恩格斯附近的田野里，最先迎接他的是一位农妇和她的女儿。

为了迷惑西方情报机构，发射场官方名称取自数百公里外的一个矿业小镇“拜科努尔”。加加林成了世界上最有名的人，太空竞赛也更加紧迫：数周之后，肯尼迪总统宣布美国要登上月球。

summary.en: A shallow earthquake directly beneath Tashkent destroyed much of the old city and left some 300,000 people homeless, though relatively few died; the city was rebuilt as a Soviet showcase capital.
summary.zh: 一次震源极浅的地震发生在塔什干正下方，摧毁了大部分老城，约30万人无家可归，但死亡人数相对较少；该城随后被重建为苏联的样板城市。

summary.en: Soviet irrigation schemes diverting the Amu Darya and Syr Darya to cotton fields caused the Aral Sea, once the world’s fourth-largest lake, to shrink to a fraction of its size, ruining fisheries and spreading salt dust.
summary.zh: 苏联将阿姆河与锡尔河水引去灌溉棉田，致使曾为世界第四大湖的咸海面积大幅萎缩，渔业崩溃，盐尘四散。

sources.title: Philip Micklin, “The Aral Sea disaster”, Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences 35 (2007)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Aral Sea
Wikidata Q35883

note: End year 2014 marks the first complete drying of the eastern basin; the northern Small Aral has partly recovered since the Kokaral dam (2005).

story.en:
In 1960 the Aral Sea covered about 68,000 square kilometres and supported a fishing industry that sent fish across the Soviet Union. Soviet planners had decided that the waters of the Amu Darya and Syr Darya were worth more on cotton fields than in a desert lake, and vast canals such as the Karakum Canal carried them away. By the 1980s almost no river water reached the sea.

The sea split into a northern and a southern part and kept shrinking. The port of Moynaq in Karakalpakstan ended up more than a hundred kilometres from the water, its rusting fishing boats left on the sand. Winds lifted salt and pesticide residues from the exposed seabed, a new desert now called the Aralkum, and health in the region declined. A Soviet biological weapons test site on Vozrozhdeniya Island became joined to the mainland.

In 2005 Kazakhstan, with the World Bank, completed the Kokaral dam to hold water in the northern Small Aral. Its level rose and fish returned, but the larger southern basin is largely gone.
story.zh:
1960年，咸海面积约6.8万平方公里，渔业产品远销苏联各地。苏联计划者认为，阿姆河和锡尔河的水用于棉田比流入沙漠中的湖泊更有价值，卡拉库姆运河等巨大渠道把河水引走。到1980年代，几乎已没有河水流入咸海。

咸海分裂为南北两部分并持续萎缩。卡拉卡尔帕克斯坦的港口穆伊纳克最终距水边一百多公里，锈蚀的渔船搁浅在沙地上。风从裸露的湖床上卷起盐分和农药残留，这片新沙漠如今称为“阿拉尔库姆”，当地居民健康状况随之恶化。复兴岛上的苏联生物武器试验场也与陆地连成一片。

2005年，哈萨克斯坦在世界银行支持下建成科卡拉尔大坝，把水留在北部的小咸海。其水位回升，鱼类重返，但南部更大的湖盆已基本消失。

summary.en: Eleven former Soviet republics met in Alma-Ata to found the Commonwealth of Independent States, confirming the end of the USSR four days before Gorbachev resigned; Kazakhstan, the last republic to leave, had declared independence on 16 December.
summary.zh: 前苏联11个加盟共和国在阿拉木图会晤，成立独立国家联合体，确认苏联解体，四天后戈尔巴乔夫辞职；最后宣布独立的哈萨克斯坦已于12月16日独立。

sources.title: Serhii Plokhy, The Last Empire: The Final Days of the Soviet Union (2014)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Commonwealth of Independent States
Wikidata Q1786449

story.en:
On 8 December 1991 the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus met in a hunting lodge in the Belovezha forest and declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist, replacing it with a Commonwealth of Independent States. The Central Asian leaders, who had not been invited, were alarmed at being left out of what looked like a Slavic union.

Kazakhstan’s president Nursultan Nazarbayev, who had worked hard to save a reformed union, now hosted the meeting that buried it. On 21 December, in Alma-Ata, eleven republics signed declarations joining the Commonwealth as equal founders, guaranteeing existing borders and agreeing on joint control of nuclear weapons. Georgia sent only an observer, and the Baltic states stayed away.

Four days later Mikhail Gorbachev resigned and the red flag was lowered over the Kremlin. For the Central Asian republics, independence came less as the result of national movements than as a consequence of the union’s collapse, and their Soviet-era leaders mostly stayed in power.
story.zh:
1991年12月8日，俄罗斯、乌克兰和白俄罗斯领导人在别洛韦日森林的一处狩猎别墅会晤，宣布苏联不复存在，并以独立国家联合体取而代之。未获邀请的中亚领导人对被排除在一个看似斯拉夫联盟之外深感不安。

曾竭力挽救一个改革后的联盟的哈萨克斯坦总统纳扎尔巴耶夫，如今主持了为它送葬的会议。12月21日在阿拉木图，十一个共和国签署宣言，以平等创始国身份加入独联体，保证现有边界，并就核武器的共同管控达成一致。格鲁吉亚只派观察员出席，波罗的海三国未参加。

四天后戈尔巴乔夫辞职，克里姆林宫上空的红旗降下。对中亚各共和国而言，独立与其说是民族运动的成果，不如说是联盟解体的结果，苏联时期的领导人大多继续执政。

summary.en: Regional factions—the former communist establishment against an Islamist and democratic opposition—fought a war that killed tens of thousands and displaced over a million; a UN-brokered peace accord was signed in Moscow in June 1997.
summary.zh: 前共产党当权派与伊斯兰及民主派反对派等地方势力之间爆发内战，造成数万人死亡、百余万人流离失所；1997年6月在联合国斡旋下于莫斯科签署和平协议。

sources.title: Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021)
Shirin Akiner, Tajikistan: Disintegration or Reconciliation? (2001)
Wikidata Q1122110

summary.en: According to al-Tha'alibi's 11th-century account, Chinese prisoners taken at the Battle of Talas in 751 taught papermaking in Samarkand. Paper was already known in Central Asia, but Samarkand paper became famous, and the craft reached Baghdad by the 790s and then Egypt, Spain and Europe.
summary.zh: 据11世纪塔阿利比的记载，751年怛罗斯之战中被俘的中国工匠在撒马尔罕传授造纸术。纸张此前已为中亚所知，但“撒马尔罕纸”从此闻名，造纸技艺于790年代传至巴格达，随后传入埃及、西班牙和欧洲。

sources.title: Britannica: paper
Wikipedia: History of paper
Jonathan M. Bloom, Paper Before Print: The History and Impact of Paper in the Islamic World (2001)

note: The Talas story comes from al-Tha'alibi (d. 1038) and is probably simplified; Sogdian letters on paper predate 751. No Wikidata item exists for the event.

story.en:
The story is told by the Persian man of letters al-Tha‘alibi, writing in the early eleventh century: among the Chinese soldiers captured at Talas in 751 were men who knew how to make paper, and they set up the craft in Samarkand. By his day “Samarkand paper” was famous, and he counted it among the city’s specialities, as Egypt was known for papyrus.

Historians now treat the tale as a simplification. Paper had reached Central Asia centuries earlier: the Sogdian Ancient Letters of the early fourth century were written on it. What changed in the eighth century was large-scale production for the new Islamic empire, using rags and hemp rather than the mulberry bark of China.

The consequences were immense. A paper mill is said to have opened in Baghdad in the 790s, under the Barmakid viziers of Harun al-Rashid, and the cheap new material carried the bureaucracy, the scholarship and the book trade of the Abbasid age. From there the craft travelled to Egypt, Morocco and Spain, reaching Christian Europe in the twelfth century.
story.zh:
这个故事出自十一世纪初的波斯文人萨阿利比：751年怛罗斯之战中被俘的中国士兵里有懂得造纸的人，他们在撒马尔罕传授了这门手艺。到他生活的年代，“撒马尔罕纸”已闻名遐迩，他把它与埃及的纸莎草并列为当地特产。

如今史家认为这一说法过于简化。纸张早在数百年前就已传入中亚：四世纪初的粟特古信札就写在纸上。八世纪真正的变化，是为新兴的伊斯兰帝国大规模生产纸张，所用原料是破布和麻，而非中国的桑树皮。

其影响极其深远。据说790年代，在哈伦·拉希德的巴尔马克家族宰相主持下，巴格达开设了造纸坊；这种廉价的新材料支撑起阿拔斯时代的官僚体制、学术和图书贸易。造纸术又从这里传到埃及、摩洛哥和西班牙，并于十二世纪传入基督教欧洲。

summary.en: Overland routes linked China with Central Asia, Iran and the Mediterranean, carrying silk, horses, glass, paper and spices. Sogdian merchants of Samarkand and Bukhara handled much of the traffic, which also spread Buddhism, Manichaeism, the Church of the East and Islam, and in the 14th century, plague.
summary.zh: 陆上商路连接中国与中亚、伊朗和地中海，运送丝绸、马匹、玻璃、纸张和香料。撒马尔罕和布哈拉的粟特商人承担了大部分贸易，这些商路还传播了佛教、摩尼教、景教和伊斯兰教，14世纪时也传播了鼠疫。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor
Britannica: Silk Road
Wikipedia: Silk Road

note: The routes opened after Zhang Qian's missions (c. 138–126 BCE), before the atlas begins; the span 1–1450 is conventional. Marker at Merv, a junction of the routes.

story.en:
The name is modern: the German geographer Ferdinand von Richthofen coined “Seidenstraße” in 1877. The thing itself was a web of caravan tracks that linked oasis to oasis across Central Asia after the Han envoy Zhang Qian opened contact with the western kingdoms in the second century BCE. Few traders travelled its whole length. Goods moved in relays, from Chang’an to Dunhuang, across the Tarim Basin, over the Pamirs to Samarkand and Merv, and on to Iran and Syria.

For centuries the people most at home on these roads were the Sogdians of Samarkand and Bukhara, whose merchant colonies ran from the Crimea to north China. Their letters, contracts and shrines show families spread over thousands of kilometres.

Ideas travelled with the silk. Buddhism reached China this way, followed by Manichaeism, the Church of the East and Islam; paper went west, and glass, horses and grapes went east. In the fourteenth century the plague may have travelled too. In 2014 UNESCO listed the Chang’an–Tianshan corridor as a World Heritage site.
story.zh:
“丝绸之路”这个名称是近代才有的：1877年德国地理学家李希霍芬创造了“Seidenstraße”一词。它所指的是一张商队路网：公元前二世纪汉朝使者张骞与西域诸国建立联系之后，这些道路把中亚的一个个绿洲连接起来。很少有商人走完全程，货物以接力方式转运：从长安到敦煌，穿越塔里木盆地，翻越帕米尔到撒马尔罕和梅尔夫，再到伊朗和叙利亚。

数百年间，最熟悉这些道路的是撒马尔罕和布哈拉的粟特人，他们的商业聚落从克里米亚延伸到华北。他们留下的书信、契约和祠庙显示，一个家族可以分散在数千公里之外。

思想随丝绸一起流动。佛教经此传入中国，随后是摩尼教、景教和伊斯兰教；纸张西传，玻璃、马匹和葡萄东来。十四世纪，鼠疫可能也沿此传播。2014年，“丝绸之路：长安—天山廊道路网”被列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录。

summary.en: Brought to Ghazni by Mahmud of Ghazni, al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and wrote a systematic study of Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and customs, completed around 1030. Its comparative, source-based method has led many to call him a founder of Indology and anthropology.
summary.zh: 比鲁尼被伽色尼的马哈茂德带到伽色尼后学习梵文，撰写了一部系统研究印度宗教、哲学、天文和风俗的著作，约1030年完成。书中依据原典进行比较的方法，使许多人称他为印度学和人类学的奠基者。

sources.title: Britannica: al-Biruni
Encyclopaedia Iranica: BĪRŪNĪ, ABŪ RAYḤĀN
Wikipedia: India (Al-Biruni)

note: Wikidata gives 1017, the year al-Biruni reached Ghazni; the book was completed c. 1030, shortly after Mahmud's death.

story.en:
When Mahmud of Ghazni annexed Khwarazm in 1017, he carried off its scholars, and al-Biruni went with them to Ghazni. Over the following years he travelled with the sultan’s campaigns into the Punjab. While Mahmud looted temples, al-Biruni found pandits who would teach him Sanskrit and read with him the texts of Indian astronomy, philosophy and law.

The book he finished around 1030 is remarkable for its method. He describes Hindu beliefs from their own scriptures, compares them with Greek ideas, and says plainly when his informants disagree. He also records how hard it was to learn: Indians, he complains, believed that no country, science or people was like theirs. From the Punjab he also made his famous measurement of the Earth, working out its radius from the dip of the horizon seen from a mountain near the fort of Nandana.

The book was little read for centuries. Edward Sachau’s English translation of 1888 brought it to wide attention, and it is now regarded as a founding work of the comparative study of religion.
story.zh:
1017年伽色尼的马哈茂德吞并花剌子模，把当地学者掳到伽色尼，比鲁尼也在其中。此后数年他随苏丹出征旁遮普。马哈茂德劫掠寺庙之时，比鲁尼却找到愿意教他梵文的班智达，与他们一同研读印度的天文、哲学和法典。

他约于1030年完成的这部书以方法著称：他依据印度教自己的经典描述其信仰，与希腊思想相比较，并坦率指出信息来源之间的分歧。他也记下了学习的艰难，抱怨印度人相信没有哪个国家、哪门学问、哪个民族能与他们相比。也是在旁遮普，他完成了著名的地球测量，从南达纳要塞附近一座山上观测地平线的俯角，算出了地球半径。

这部书在此后数百年间少有人读。1888年萨豪的英译本使它广为人知，如今它被视为比较宗教研究的奠基之作。

summary.en: An R-7 rocket launched from the Soviet test range at Tyuratam (later Baikonur) in Kazakhstan put Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, into orbit. Its radio beeps, picked up around the world, opened the Space Age and spurred the United States to create NASA.
summary.zh: 一枚R-7火箭从苏联位于哈萨克斯坦秋拉塔姆（后称拜科努尔）的试验场升空，将第一颗人造地球卫星斯普特尼克1号送入轨道。它发出的无线电信号被世界各地接收，开启了太空时代，并促使美国成立国家航空航天局。

sources.title: NASA History: Sputnik and the Origins of the Space Age
Britannica: Sputnik
Wikipedia: Sputnik 1

note: Marker at Site 1 ("Gagarin's Start") of the Baikonur Cosmodrome.

story.en:
Sergei Korolev, the chief designer of the R-7 intercontinental missile, had argued for months that his rocket could put a satellite in orbit before the Americans. When the elaborate scientific satellite he had planned fell behind, he built a simple one instead: a polished aluminium sphere 58 centimetres across, weighing 83.6 kilograms, with four whip antennae and a radio transmitter.

It was launched from Tyuratam on the night of 4 October 1957. Circling the Earth every 96 minutes, Sputnik broadcast a beep on frequencies that radio amateurs all over the world could pick up, and its rocket stage could be seen from the ground. The batteries died after three weeks; the satellite burned up in the atmosphere in January 1958.

The impact far outweighed the hardware. Americans feared that a country able to orbit a satellite could hit their cities with missiles. Congress created NASA in 1958 and poured money into science education, and Khrushchev, delighted by the propaganda success, demanded more space firsts.
story.zh:
R-7洲际导弹总设计师科罗廖夫数月来一直坚持，他的火箭能抢在美国人之前把卫星送入轨道。原定的复杂科学卫星进度落后，他转而制造了一颗简单的卫星：直径58厘米、重83.6公斤的抛光铝球，带有四根鞭状天线和一台无线电发射机。

1957年10月4日夜，卫星从丘拉塔姆发射升空。“斯普特尼克”每96分钟绕地球一周，发出的“哔哔”信号全世界的无线电爱好者都能收听到，其火箭末级在地面肉眼可见。三周后电池耗尽，卫星于1958年1月坠入大气层烧毁。

其影响远远超过这件硬件本身。美国人担心，一个能把卫星送入轨道的国家也能用导弹打击他们的城市。国会于1958年设立美国国家航空航天局，并大举投资科学教育；赫鲁晓夫则对这一宣传胜利大喜过望，要求取得更多太空“第一”。

summary.en: Monks and patrons in the Bamiyan valley carved two colossal standing Buddhas, about 38 and 55 metres high, into the cliff in the 6th and early 7th centuries; Xuanzang described them around 630. The Taliban blew them up in March 2001; the valley is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
summary.zh: 巴米扬河谷的僧侣和施主于6世纪至7世纪初在崖壁上凿出两尊高约38米和55米的巨型立佛，约630年玄奘曾记述其盛况。2001年3月，两尊大佛被塔利班炸毁；该河谷现为世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Cultural Landscape and Archaeological Remains of the Bamiyan Valley
Britannica: Bamiyan
Wikipedia: Buddhas of Bamiyan

note: Radiocarbon dates: eastern (38 m) Buddha c. 544–595, western (55 m) c. 591–644; the span shown is approximate.

story.en:
The valley of Bamiyan, high in the Hindu Kush, lay on the road between Bactria and Gandhara. In the sixth and early seventh centuries its Buddhist community carved two colossal standing Buddhas into the sandstone cliff, the larger about 55 metres tall, and honeycombed the rock with hundreds of painted caves for monks.

The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang passed through around 630 and saw the statues gleaming with gold and ornaments, and dozens of monasteries. Long after the valley became Muslim, the giants remained a landmark mentioned by geographers and travellers.

In February 2001 the Taliban leader Mullah Omar ordered all statues in Afghanistan destroyed as idols. Over several weeks in March, despite pleas from UNESCO and Muslim governments, the Buddhas were blown up with tanks, artillery and explosives. The empty niches became a symbol of cultural destruction. In 2003 the valley was inscribed as a World Heritage site, and studies of its caves later found some of the world’s oldest known oil paintings, from the seventh century.
story.zh:
巴米扬河谷高踞兴都库什山中，地处巴克特里亚通往犍陀罗的道路上。六世纪至七世纪初，当地佛教僧团在砂岩崖壁上凿出两尊巨大的立佛，大者高约55米，又在崖壁上开凿了数百个绘有壁画的僧窟。

约630年，中国僧人玄奘途经此地，看到佛像“金色晃曜，宝饰焕烂”，还有数十座寺院。在河谷改信伊斯兰教很久以后，这两尊巨像仍是地理学家和旅行者笔下的地标。

2001年2月，塔利班领导人奥马尔下令摧毁阿富汗境内一切被视为偶像的雕像。尽管联合国教科文组织和多个穆斯林国家政府恳请保护，3月间佛像仍在数周内被坦克、火炮和炸药摧毁。空荡的佛龛成为文化毁灭的象征。2003年巴米扬河谷被列入世界遗产名录，此后对石窟的研究还发现了七世纪的油画，属于世界上已知最早的油画之一。

summary.en: Syriac gravestones of a Church of the East community near Lake Issyk-Kul record a spike in deaths in 1338–39, some from “pestilence”. In 2022 ancient DNA from these burials identified Yersinia pestis ancestral to the Black Death strains, pointing to this region as a source shortly before the plague reached Europe.
summary.zh: 伊塞克湖附近景教社群的叙利亚文墓碑记录了1338至1339年死亡人数的激增，部分碑文称死于“瘟疫”。2022年对这些墓葬的古DNA研究鉴定出鼠疫耶尔森菌，属于黑死病菌株的直系祖先，表明此地是黑死病传入欧洲前不久的源头之一。

sources.title: M. A. Spyrou et al., "The source of the Black Death in fourteenth-century central Eurasia", Nature 606 (2022)
Wikipedia: Black Death

note: Marker at Burana, one of the two cemeteries (with Kara-Djigach near Bishkek) sampled in the 2022 study. Whether the outbreak spread widely from here is debated. No Wikidata item exists for the event.

story.en:
In the 1880s Russian archaeologists excavated two cemeteries of the Church of the East near Bishkek and Tokmok, in the Chüy valley south of Lake Issyk-Kul. Hundreds of gravestones carried inscriptions in Syriac and Turkic. The orientalist Daniel Chwolson noticed that an unusual number dated from 1338 and 1339, and that some said the dead had died of “pestilence”.

More than a century later, a team led by the historian Philip Slavin and geneticists at the Max Planck Institute in Leipzig and the University of Tübingen took DNA from teeth of people buried in those years. Their 2022 study in Nature identified Yersinia pestis, the plague bacterium, in several individuals. The strain sat at the root of the burst of lineages that includes the Black Death, and was closely related to strains still found in marmots of the Tian Shan.

The finding suggests that the pandemic that killed perhaps half of Europe’s population in 1347–51 began in or near Central Asia, perhaps spreading west along the trade routes of the Mongol khanates.
story.zh:
1880年代，俄国考古学家在伊塞克湖以南楚河谷地的比什凯克和托克马克附近，发掘了两处东方教会（景教）墓地。数百块墓碑刻有叙利亚文和突厥文铭文。东方学家赫沃利森注意到，其中格外多的墓碑年代为1338年和1339年，有的还写明死者死于“瘟疫”。

一个多世纪后，由历史学家菲利普·斯拉文与莱比锡马普研究所和图宾根大学遗传学家组成的团队，从这些年份下葬者的牙齿中提取DNA。他们于2022年在《自然》杂志发表研究，在数人身上检出鼠疫耶尔森菌。这一菌株位于包括黑死病在内的一系列谱系的分化根部，并与至今仍见于天山旱獭的菌株关系密切。

这一发现表明，1347—1351年可能夺去欧洲半数人口的大瘟疫起源于中亚或其附近，或许沿着蒙古诸汗国的商路向西传播。

name.en: Xiongnu split into Northern and Southern

summary.en: Bi, a grandson of Huhanye Chanyu, broke with the reigning chanyu, took his grandfather’s title and submitted to the Eastern Han with eight tribes. The Southern Xiongnu settled inside the Chinese frontier as Han allies, while the Northern Xiongnu held Mongolia until their defeat in 89–91.
summary.zh: 呼韩邪单于之孙比与在位单于决裂，袭用祖父称号，率八部归附东汉。南匈奴作为汉朝盟友入居塞内，北匈奴则继续据有漠北，直至89—91年被击溃。

sources.title: Fan Ye, Hou Hanshu, ch. 89: the Southern Xiongnu
Thomas J. Barfield, The Perilous Frontier: Nomadic Empires and China (1989)
Britannica: Xiongnu

note: No Wikidata item exists for the split. The marker approximates the Ordos, where the Southern chanyu’s court was settled at Meiji in 50 CE.

name.en: An Shigao begins translating Buddhist texts in Luoyang

summary.en: A Parthian prince who had renounced his throne, An Shigao reached the Han capital Luoyang around 148 and began the first systematic translation of Buddhist texts into Chinese, chiefly on meditation and doctrine. Central Asian monks would dominate Chinese Buddhist translation for the next three centuries.
summary.zh: 安世高原为安息王子，让位出家，约148年抵达东汉都城洛阳，开始首次系统地将佛经译为汉文，主要涉及禅修与教义。此后三百年间，来自中亚的僧人一直主导着汉译佛经事业。

sources.title: Erik Zürcher, The Buddhist Conquest of China (1959; 3rd ed. 2007)
Jan Nattier, A Guide to the Earliest Chinese Buddhist Translations (2008)
Wikipedia: An Shigao

note: The arrival year 148 comes from Sengyou’s 6th-century catalogue; his princely origin rests on later biographies. No Wikidata item exists for the event (Q1267947 is the monk).

summary.en: A bundle of letters by Sogdian merchants and their families, lost in a watchtower west of Dunhuang around 313–314, describes the sack of Luoyang by the “Huns”, famine in north China and a trading network reaching Samarkand. Aurel Stein found them in 1907; they are the oldest substantial Sogdian texts.
summary.zh: 约313—314年遗落在敦煌以西一座烽燧中的一批粟特商人及其家属的书信，记述了“匈人”攻陷洛阳、华北饥荒以及远达撒马尔罕的贸易网络。斯坦因于1907年发现这批信札，它们是现存最早的成批粟特语文献。

sources.title: Nicholas Sims-Williams, “The Sogdian Ancient Letters” (translation), Silk Road Seattle
Étienne de la Vaissière, Sogdian Traders: A History (2005)
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Ancient Letters (N. Sims-Williams)

note: Most scholars date the letters to 313–314 from their description of Luoyang’s fall in 311; a minority prefer the early 3rd century. The marker approximates Stein’s watchtower T.XII.a near the Yumen pass.

story.en:
In 1907 Aurel Stein was clearing a ruined Han watchtower in the desert west of Dunhuang when he found a mailbag of letters, folded and tied in silk, that had never been delivered. They were written in Sogdian, the language of Samarkand, and turned out to date from the early fourth century.

Letter II, written by a merchant named Nanai-vandak to partners in Samarkand, reports that the emperor had fled Luoyang, that the city and its palaces had been burned by the “Huns”, and that the Sogdians and Indians there had starved. It is a direct witness to the fall of Luoyang in 311, and its word for the attackers, xwn, has fed the long debate over whether the Huns of Europe descended from the Xiongnu.

Letter III is more personal. A woman named Miwnay, abandoned in Dunhuang with her daughter by a husband who had gone off trading, writes that she would rather be the wife of a dog or a pig than his. The letters show how far Sogdian families were spread and how fragile their lives could be.
story.zh:
1907年，斯坦因在敦煌以西沙漠中清理一座汉代烽燧废墟时，发现了一包从未寄出的信件，信件折叠后用丝绳系住。它们用撒马尔罕的语言粟特语写成，年代为四世纪初。

二号信札是商人那奈·万达克写给撒马尔罕合伙人的，信中报告皇帝已逃离洛阳，城池和宫殿被“匈人”焚毁，城中的粟特人和印度人都已饿死。这是311年洛阳陷落的直接见证；信中称攻城者为xwn，这一词语也成为长期争论欧洲匈人是否源自匈奴的依据之一。

三号信札则更为私人化。一位名叫米薇的妇女被外出经商的丈夫抛弃在敦煌，带着女儿生活，她在信中写道，宁可做狗或猪的妻子，也不愿再做他的妻子。这些信札显示了粟特家族分布之广，以及他们生活的脆弱。

name.en: The Huns reach the Pontic steppe
name.zh: 匈人进入黑海北岸草原

summary.en: Horsemen the Romans called Huns crossed the Volga and the Don, conquered the Alans and broke the Gothic realm of Ermanaric. Fleeing Goths begged to cross the Danube in 376, setting off the crisis that led to Rome’s defeat at Adrianople.
summary.zh: 被罗马人称为匈人的骑兵渡过伏尔加河和顿河，征服阿兰人，击溃埃尔曼纳里克的哥特王国。逃难的哥特人于376年请求渡过多瑙河，由此引发危机，导致罗马在阿德里安堡战败。

label.en: Alans of the Don defeated and absorbed
label.zh: 顿河阿兰人被击败并被吸纳
格鲁森尼哥特人溃败，埃尔曼纳里克死去

label.en: Tervingi Goths flee to the Danube
label.zh: 瑟文吉哥特人逃至多瑙河

sources.title: Ammianus Marcellinus, Res Gestae XXXI.2–3
Peter Heather, The Fall of the Roman Empire (2005)
Britannica: Hun (people)

note: Ammianus gives no exact dates before 376; the 370 start is conventional. Whether the Huns descended from the Xiongnu is debated. No Wikidata item exists for the event; route stops are approximate.

story.en:
To the Roman officer Ammianus Marcellinus the Huns appeared out of nowhere, a people “beyond the Sea of Azov” who lived on horseback, ate half-raw meat warmed under their saddles and owed allegiance to no king. Modern historians still argue over where they came from; their name echoes the Xiongnu of Mongolia, and archaeology shows steppe customs such as cranial deformation and bronze cauldrons moving west, but no unbroken trail.

Around 370 they crossed the Volga and fell on the Alans, Iranian-speaking nomads of the Don steppe, killing many and taking the rest into their following. Then they attacked the Greuthungi, the Goths of Ermanaric, an old king whose realm Ammianus describes as vast. Ermanaric took his own life rather than face defeat. The Tervingi Goths further west tried to hold the Dniester and failed.

In 376 tens of thousands of Goths gathered on the Danube and asked Emperor Valens to let them in. Roman mistreatment turned the refugees into an army, which destroyed Valens and his field army at Adrianople two years later.
story.zh:
在罗马军官阿米安·马塞林笔下，匈人仿佛凭空出现：他们来自“亚速海之外”，生活在马背上，吃在马鞍下焐热的半生肉，不服从任何国王。现代史家至今仍在争论他们的来历：其名称与蒙古高原的匈奴相呼应，考古材料也显示颅骨变形、青铜鍑等草原习俗向西传播，但并无一条连贯的线索。

约370年，他们渡过伏尔加河，袭击顿河草原上讲伊朗语的游牧民阿兰人，杀死许多人并把其余的人纳入麾下。接着他们进攻埃尔曼纳里克统治的格鲁森尼哥特人；阿米安称这位老国王的疆域十分辽阔，他宁愿自尽也不愿面对失败。更西面的瑟文吉哥特人试图守住德涅斯特河，同样失败。

376年，数以万计的哥特人聚集在多瑙河畔，请求皇帝瓦伦斯准许入境。罗马官员的虐待把难民变成了一支军队，两年后他们在阿德里安堡全歼瓦伦斯及其野战军。

name.en: Lü Guang takes Kucha and carries off Kumarajiva
name.zh: 吕光破龟兹，携鸠摩罗什东归

summary.en: A Former Qin army under Lü Guang conquered the Tarim kingdom of Kucha and seized its famous monk Kumarajiva. When Former Qin collapsed, Lü Guang founded the Later Liang state in Gansu and kept Kumarajiva there for seventeen years.
summary.zh: 前秦大将吕光率军攻灭塔里木盆地的龟兹国，掳走名僧鸠摩罗什。前秦崩溃后，吕光在河西建立后凉，把鸠摩罗什留在凉州十七年。

sources.title: Huijiao, Gaoseng zhuan (Biographies of Eminent Monks), ch. 2: Kumarajiva
Fang Xuanling et al., Jinshu, ch. 122: Lü Guang
Britannica: Kumarajiva

name.en: Hephthalites kill the Sasanian king Peroz
name.zh: 嚈哒人击杀萨珊国王卑路斯

summary.en: The Sasanian king Peroz I, who had already been captured once by the Hephthalites and ransomed, invaded their lands again and was killed with much of his army. Iran paid the Hephthalites tribute for decades and its next king, Kavad, won his throne with their help.
summary.zh: 萨珊国王卑路斯一世此前已被嚈哒人俘虏过一次并以赎金获释，他再度进犯嚈哒，结果与大部分军队一同战死。此后数十年伊朗向嚈哒纳贡，下一任国王喀瓦德也是借助嚈哒之力夺得王位的。

sources.title: Procopius, History of the Wars I.3–4
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Hephthalites
Wikipedia: Battle of Herat (484)

note: The battlefield is not securely located; sources place it east of Iran near Herat or Balkh. No Wikidata item was found for the battle.

story.en:
Peroz had come to the throne in 459 with Hephthalite help, and his relations with his eastern neighbours went from bad to worse. In one campaign he was surrounded and captured, and had to leave his son Kavad as a hostage until a huge ransom was paid. Procopius says he also swore never to march against the Hephthalites again.

In 484 he broke that oath. Procopius tells a story that later writers repeated: the Hephthalite king had a long, deep trench dug across the plain and covered with reeds and earth, leaving a narrow path in the middle. His horsemen pretended to flee along the path, and the Persian cavalry charging after them fell into the trench. Peroz died with his sons and many nobles; one tale says he threw away a famous pearl from his ear so that no one else would wear it.

For a generation Iran paid tribute to the Hephthalites. Kavad, the former hostage, won his throne with Hephthalite troops in 498. Only his son Khosrow I, allied with the new Turkic power, destroyed the Hephthalite realm around 560.
story.zh:
卑路斯于459年在嚈哒人帮助下登上王位，但他与东方邻国的关系每况愈下。在一次战役中他被包围俘虏，不得不把儿子喀瓦德留作人质，直到付清巨额赎金。普罗科匹厄斯说他还发誓永不再进攻嚈哒。

484年，他背弃了誓言。普罗科匹厄斯记下一个后世反复转述的故事：嚈哒国王在平原上挖了一条又长又深的壕沟，用芦苇和泥土覆盖，只在中间留一条窄路。嚈哒骑兵沿窄路佯装败逃，追击的波斯骑兵纷纷坠入沟中。卑路斯与诸子及许多贵族一同战死；一则传说称他临死前扔掉了耳上一颗著名的珍珠，以免被别人佩戴。

此后一代人的时间里，伊朗向嚈哒纳贡。昔日的人质喀瓦德于498年借嚈哒兵力夺得王位。直到其子库思老一世与新兴的突厥结盟，才在约560年灭亡嚈哒。

name.en: Turkic–Byzantine embassies of Maniakh and Zemarchus
name.zh: 突厥与拜占庭互派使节（马尼亚赫与蔡马库斯）

summary.en: After Iran refused to let Turkic silk pass, the Western Türk ruler Istämi sent the Sogdian merchant Maniakh to Constantinople in 568 to propose an alliance. Emperor Justin II answered by sending Zemarchus, who crossed the steppe to Istämi’s camp in the Tian Shan in 569.
summary.zh: 伊朗拒绝突厥丝绸过境后，西突厥统治者室点密于568年派粟特商人马尼亚赫出使君士坦丁堡，提议结盟。拜占庭皇帝查士丁二世回派蔡马库斯，他于569年穿越草原抵达室点密在天山的牙帐。

label.zh: 马尼亚赫使团抵达君士坦丁堡

label.en: Zemarchus sails to the Caucasus coast
label.zh: 蔡马库斯渡海至高加索沿岸
在艾克塔格觐见室点密

label.en: Accompanies the Turks on campaign near Talas
label.zh: 随突厥军队行至怛逻斯附近

sources.title: Menander Protector, History, frr. 10.1–10.5, tr. R. C. Blockley (1985)
Étienne de la Vaissière, Sogdian Traders: A History (2005)
Denis Sinor (ed.), The Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia (1990)

note: Ektag (“White Mountain”) is not located precisely; the marker places it in the eastern Tian Shan. No Wikidata item exists for the embassies (Q189282 is Zemarchus).

story.en:
The new Turkic empire controlled the silk of the Tarim oases, and its Sogdian subjects wanted to sell it in the west. Their spokesman Maniakh first went to the Sasanian king Khosrow I, who, according to the Byzantine historian Menander, bought the silk and burned it in front of the envoys, and later had a second Turkic embassy poisoned.

Istämi then sent Maniakh the long way round, north of the Caspian and over the Caucasus, to Constantinople. He arrived in 568 with a letter in Turkic script and offered Justin II silk and an alliance against Persia. The emperor, whose own subjects had recently learned to raise silkworms, sent back the general Zemarchus.

Menander’s account of Zemarchus’s journey is one of the earliest Western descriptions of the steppe. At Istämi’s camp the envoys were led between fires to purify them, then shown into silk-hung tents where the khagan sat on a golden throne on wheels. Zemarchus followed the Turks on campaign towards Persia before returning home in 571. The alliance helped draw Byzantium into its long war with Iran.
story.zh:
新兴的突厥帝国控制着塔里木绿洲的丝绸，其粟特属民希望把丝绸卖到西方。据拜占庭史家弥南德记载，粟特代表马尼亚赫起初前往萨珊国王库思老一世处，库思老买下丝绸后当着使者的面将其焚毁，后来又毒死了第二批突厥使者。

室点密于是派马尼亚赫绕远路，经里海以北、越过高加索前往君士坦丁堡。他于568年抵达，带着一封突厥文字书写的国书，向查士丁二世提供丝绸并提议联合对抗波斯。当时拜占庭人刚学会养蚕，皇帝派将军蔡马库斯回访。

弥南德对蔡马库斯旅程的记述是西方最早的草原描写之一。在室点密的牙帐，使者们先被引着从火堆间穿过以示洁净，再被带进悬挂丝绸的帐幕，可汗坐在一张装有轮子的金座上。蔡马库斯随突厥军队向波斯方向出征，571年返回。这一联盟促使拜占庭卷入与伊朗的长期战争。

summary.en: Songtsen Gampo, the first emperor of Tibet, founded the Jokhang (Rasa Trulnang) in his new capital at Lhasa; tradition links it to his Nepali queen Bhrikuti, while the Jowo statue brought by the Tang princess Wencheng later became its holiest image. It remains the most sacred temple in Tibet.
summary.zh: 吐蕃第一位赞普松赞干布在新都拉萨兴建大昭寺（惹萨幻显殿）；传统说法将其与尼泊尔王妃尺尊公主联系在一起，而唐朝文成公主带来的觉卧佛像后来成为寺中最神圣的佛像。它至今仍是西藏最神圣的寺庙。

sources.title: Matthew T. Kapstein, The Tibetans (2006)
UNESCO: Historic Ensemble of the Potala Palace, Lhasa
Wikipedia: Jokhang

note: The founding date is traditional; Tibetan histories give 639, 647 or 652, and 639 follows Wikidata. The roles of the two foreign queens come from later Buddhist histories.

story.en:
Later Tibetan histories, written centuries after the event, tell the founding of the Jokhang as a story of geomancy and queens. Songtsen Gampo had married Bhrikuti, a princess of Nepal, and Wencheng, a princess of the Tang. Wencheng, skilled in Chinese divination, found that the land of Tibet was like a demoness lying on her back, and that the lake on the plain of Lhasa was her heart. The temple was to be built on the filled-in lake to pin her down.

According to the legend, goats carried the earth to fill the lake, and the place was called Ra-sa, “goat earth”, which became Lhasa. Bhrikuti is said to have built the main temple with Nepali craftsmen, whose work survives in its oldest carved door frames and pillars.

The Jowo Shakyamuni, a statue of the Buddha as a young prince believed to have come from China with Wencheng, was moved into the Jokhang later and became the holiest image in Tibet. Pilgrims still prostrate themselves along the Barkhor circuit around it.
story.zh:
成书于数百年后的藏文史籍，把大昭寺的创建讲述成一个关于堪舆和王妃的故事。松赞干布娶了尼泊尔的尺尊公主和唐朝的文成公主。精通汉地卜算的文成公主看出，吐蕃大地犹如一个仰卧的罗刹女，拉萨平原上的湖泊正是她的心脏，须在填湖之处建寺将其镇住。

传说中，山羊驮土填湖，此地因此称为“惹萨”（羊土），后来演变为“拉萨”。据说尺尊公主带领尼泊尔工匠修建了主殿，寺中最古老的雕花门框和柱子至今仍保留着他们的手艺。

据信由文成公主从中国带来的觉卧释迦牟尼像，表现佛陀少年王子时的形象，后来被移入大昭寺，成为西藏最神圣的佛像。朝圣者至今仍沿着环绕大昭寺的八廓街磕长头转经。

summary.en: Appointed governor of Khurasan in 705, Qutayba ibn Muslim led Umayyad armies across the Oxus year after year, taking Bukhara in 709, Khwarazm and Samarkand in 712 and raiding Chach and Fergana. His campaigns made Transoxiana a frontier of the caliphate, though Sogdian revolts continued for decades.
summary.zh: 屈底波·伊本·穆斯林于705年任呼罗珊总督，此后年年率倭马亚军队渡过阿姆河，709年取布哈拉，712年取花剌子模和撒马尔罕，并进袭石国和费尔干纳。他的征战使河中成为哈里发国的边疆，但粟特人的反抗又持续了数十年。

label.en: Qutayba arrives at Merv as governor
label.zh: 屈底波到梅尔夫就任总督

label.en: Killed by his own troops in Fergana
label.zh: 在费尔干纳被部下杀死

sources.title: al-Tabari, The History of al-Tabari, vols. 23–24, tr. M. Hinds and D. S. Powers
H. A. R. Gibb, The Arab Conquests in Central Asia (1923)
Hugh Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)

note: Wikidata’s item covers the whole Arab conquest of Transoxiana (c. 673–751); this record follows its decisive phase under Qutayba. Dates follow al-Tabari.

story.en:
Arab raiders had crossed the Oxus for half a century without staying. Qutayba ibn Muslim, a tough Iraqi commander sent to Khurasan in 705, changed that. Each spring he led his army across the river and each winter brought it back to Merv, until the cities of Sogdia were worn down.

Bukhara fell in 709 after several failed campaigns, and Qutayba planted an Arab garrison in half of every house, according to the local historian Narshakhi. In 712 he intervened in a civil war in Khwarazm and then marched suddenly on Samarkand. Its ruler Ghurak held out for a month before agreeing to pay tribute and to let Qutayba build a mosque. Al-Tabari reports that when the city’s idols were burned, the ashes yielded gold and silver nails worth some 50,000 mithqals.

Qutayba pushed on to Chach and Fergana. When the new caliph Sulayman, his political enemy, came to power in 715, Qutayba tried to rebel, but his own exhausted troops turned on him and killed him in Fergana. Arab rule over Transoxiana was fragile for another generation, until the victory at Talas in 751.
story.zh:
半个世纪以来，阿拉伯劫掠者多次渡过阿姆河，却从未久留。705年被派往呼罗珊的伊拉克悍将屈底波改变了这一局面。他每年春天率军渡河，冬天退回梅尔夫，直到把粟特诸城拖垮。

几次出征失败后，布哈拉于709年陷落。据当地史家纳尔沙希记载，屈底波让阿拉伯驻军住进每户人家的一半房屋。712年他介入花剌子模内战，随即突袭撒马尔罕。城主乌勒伽坚守一个月后，同意纳贡并允许屈底波修建清真寺。塔巴里记载，城中偶像被焚烧后，从灰烬中得到价值约五万米斯卡勒的金银钉。

屈底波继续进兵石国和费尔干纳。715年，他的政敌苏莱曼继任哈里发，屈底波企图反叛，但疲惫不堪的部下倒戈，在费尔干纳将他杀死。阿拉伯人对河中的统治在此后一代人的时间里仍不稳固，直到751年怛罗斯之战获胜。

name.en: Devashtich’s last stand on Mount Mugh
name.zh: 迪瓦什蒂奇困守穆格山

summary.en: Devashtich, ruler of Panjikent, who claimed the title of king of Sogdia, joined a revolt against Arab rule and was besieged in a castle on Mount Mugh in the upper Zeravshan valley. He surrendered and was executed. His archive, found in 1932–33, is the richest set of Sogdian documents.
summary.zh: 片治肯特城主迪瓦什蒂奇自称粟特王，参加反抗阿拉伯统治的起义，被围困在泽拉夫尚河上游穆格山的城堡中。他投降后被处死。1932—1933年发现的其档案，是现存最丰富的粟特文书。

sources.title: Frantz Grenet & Étienne de la Vaissière, “The Last Days of Panjikent”, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 8 (2002)
Frantz Grenet and Étienne de la Vaissière, “The Last Days of Panjikent”, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 8 (2002)
Wikipedia: Devashtich

note: Mount Mugh lies near the village of Khayrabad in the upper Zeravshan; the coordinates are approximate. No Wikidata item exists for the siege (Q753663 is Devashtich).

story.en:
In the spring of 1932 a shepherd in the mountains of the upper Zeravshan, in Soviet Tajikistan, found a wicker basket full of old writing in the ruins of a castle on a crag called Mount Mugh. Soviet orientalists went out the next year and recovered some 80 documents on leather, paper and wood, most in Sogdian.

They turned out to be the papers of Devashtich, lord of Panjikent, a prosperous Sogdian city whose painted houses have since been excavated. In 721–22, as Arab rule hardened, he claimed the title of king of Sogdia and joined a rising. When it failed he fled up the valley to Mount Mugh with his household. The documents include letters from his agents, a marriage contract, land leases and a letter in Arabic he had written to the Arab governor.

Al-Tabari records the end: besieged by the governor Sa‘id al-Harashi, Devashtich came down on a promise of safety and was killed and crucified. Panjikent was abandoned within a few decades. Today the district around it bears his name.
story.zh:
1932年春，苏联塔吉克斯坦泽拉夫尚河上游山区的一位牧羊人，在一座名叫穆格山的山崖上的城堡废墟里，发现了一个装满古代文书的柳条筐。次年苏联东方学家前往考察，找到约80件写在皮革、纸和木头上的文书，大多为粟特文。

这些文书属于片治肯特城主迪瓦什蒂奇。片治肯特是一座富庶的粟特城市，其绘有壁画的宅院后来已被发掘。721—722年阿拉伯统治趋严，他自称粟特王并加入起义；起义失败后，他带着家人沿河谷逃往穆格山。文书中有其代理人的来信、一份婚约、土地租约，以及他写给阿拉伯总督的一封阿拉伯文信。

塔巴里记载了结局：被总督赛义德·哈拉希围困后，迪瓦什蒂奇在得到安全承诺后下山，结果被杀并被钉上十字架。数十年内片治肯特便被废弃。如今当地的区仍以他的名字命名。

summary.en: Bögü Qaghan, who led Uyghur troops to help the Tang recover Luoyang from the An Lushan rebels in 762, met Manichaean priests there and brought four of them home. Manichaeism became the religion of the Uyghur court, the only state in history to adopt it.
summary.zh: 牟羽可汗于762年率回鹘军队助唐从安史叛军手中收复洛阳，在那里结识了摩尼教僧侣，并带四人回国。摩尼教由此成为回鹘宫廷的宗教，回鹘是历史上唯一以摩尼教为国教的国家。

sources.title: Karabalgasun inscription (c. 821)
Colin Mackerras, The Uighur Empire According to the T’ang Dynastic Histories (1972)
Britannica: Manichaeism

note: The conversion is dated 762–763 from the Karabalgasun inscription and a Turkic Manichaean text; some scholars see a longer, contested process. No Wikidata item exists for the event.

story.en:
When the An Lushan rebellion threw the Tang into chaos, the emperors turned to the Uyghurs for cavalry, at a high price in silk and plunder. In 762 Bögü Qaghan himself led an army to recapture the eastern capital Luoyang from the rebels, and his troops looted the city.

In Luoyang he met Manichaean priests, followers of the third-century Persian prophet Mani, who taught that the world was a battleground between Light and Darkness. The trilingual Karabalgasun inscription, set up at the Uyghur capital about sixty years later, says that the khagan took four of them home in 763 and that the Uyghurs, who had been “a nation of blood-eaters”, became “vegetarians”. A Turkic text from Turfan describes the khagan’s repentance and the people’s joy.

The new faith tied the Uyghurs to the Sogdian merchants who served as their advisers and traders. Manichaean temples appeared in Tang cities under Uyghur protection, and after 840 the religion survived in the Uyghur kingdom of Qocho, whose painted Manichaean books are among the finest relics of the faith.
story.zh:
安史之乱使唐朝陷入混乱，皇帝们以大量丝绸和战利品为代价向回鹘借兵。762年，牟羽可汗亲率大军从叛军手中收复东都洛阳，其部众在城中大肆劫掠。
