在洛阳，他结识了摩尼教僧侣。摩尼教由三世纪的波斯先知摩尼创立，宣称世界是光明与黑暗交战的战场。约六十年后立于回鹘都城的三语《九姓回鹘可汗碑》记载，可汗于763年带四名僧侣回国，回鹘人从“茹血之国”变成了“蔬饭之乡”。吐鲁番出土的一份突厥语文献描写了可汗的忏悔和民众的欢欣。

新信仰把回鹘人与担任其谋士和商人的粟特人联系在一起。在回鹘的庇护下，唐朝城市中出现了摩尼教寺院。840年以后，这一宗教在高昌回鹘王国延续下来，那里绘制精美的摩尼教经卷是该宗教最珍贵的遗物之一。

summary.en: Emperor Trisong Detsen founded Samye in the Yarlung region with the Indian abbot Shantarakshita; its plan represented the Buddhist cosmos, with a central temple for Mount Meru. The first Tibetan monks were ordained there, and Buddhism became the empire’s official religion.
summary.zh: 赞普赤松德赞与印度堪布寂护在雅砻地区兴建桑耶寺，其布局象征佛教宇宙，中央大殿代表须弥山。第一批藏族僧人在此受戒，佛教成为吐蕃的官方宗教。

sources.title: Sam van Schaik, Tibet: A History (2011)
Matthew T. Kapstein, The Tibetans (2006)
Wikipedia: Samye

note: Dates vary between sources (c. 763–779); construction is often dated from c. 775 and the consecration to 779, the year used here. The role of Padmasambhava is known only from later tradition.

summary.en: At Trisong Detsen’s court, Indian Buddhists led by Kamalashila and Chinese Chan monks led by Moheyan disputed whether enlightenment comes gradually or suddenly. Tibetan tradition holds that the Indian side won, and Tibetan Buddhism followed Indian models thereafter.
summary.zh: 在赤松德赞的宫廷中，以莲花戒为首的印度僧人与以摩诃衍为首的汉地禅僧就觉悟是渐修还是顿悟展开辩论。藏传说法认为印度一方获胜，此后藏传佛教遵循印度传统。

sources.title: Paul Demiéville, Le concile de Lhasa (1952)
Sam van Schaik, Tibetan Zen: Discovering a Lost Tradition (2015)
Wikipedia: Samye Debate

note: Whether a single formal debate took place is doubted; Tibetan sources such as the Testament of Ba describe one, while a Chinese text from Dunhuang presents Moheyan as the victor. Dates are approximate.

story.en:
By the 790s Buddhism at the Tibetan court came from two directions. Indian teachers, brought by the abbot Shantarakshita, taught that awakening was reached step by step through moral conduct, study and meditation. Chinese Chan masters, led by the monk Moheyan, taught that it came suddenly, when the mind stopped grasping at concepts, and Moheyan had many followers among the Tibetan nobility.

The Testament of Ba, a Tibetan chronicle, says that Trisong Detsen called the two sides to debate at Samye. Kamalashila, Shantarakshita’s pupil, argued that Moheyan’s teaching would make all practice pointless. The king declared the Indians victorious and ordered that the Tibetans follow the Indian path. In the dramatic version told later, the defeated Chinese monks left, and Kamalashila was murdered by their partisans.

A Chinese text found at Dunhuang tells it differently, with Moheyan winning the argument. Many historians now see a longer contest of factions rather than a single debate. Either way, the Tibetan tradition chose Indian scholastic Buddhism, though Chan ideas survived in Tibetan meditation teachings.
story.zh:
到790年代，吐蕃宫廷中的佛教来自两个方向。寂护堪布请来的印度上师主张通过持戒、闻思和禅修逐步证悟；以摩诃衍为首的汉地禅师则主张心不执著于概念时便能顿悟，摩诃衍在吐蕃贵族中拥有众多追随者。

藏文史书《巴协》记载，赤松德赞召集双方在桑耶寺辩论。寂护的弟子莲花戒指出，摩诃衍的教法会使一切修行失去意义。赞普宣布印度一方获胜，命吐蕃人遵循印度之道。在后世更富戏剧性的版本中，落败的汉僧离去，莲花戒后来被其支持者暗杀。

敦煌出土的一份汉文文献所记却截然不同，称摩诃衍辩论获胜。许多史家如今认为，这是派系之间较长时期的竞争，而非一场单一的辩论。无论如何，藏传佛教选择了印度的经院佛学，但禅宗思想仍在藏族禅修教法中保留下来。

name.en: Assassination of Langdarma and collapse of the Tibetan Empire
name.zh: 朗达玛遇刺与吐蕃王朝崩溃

summary.en: The emperor Langdarma was killed in 842, and a succession dispute between two infant heirs split the dynasty. The Tibetan Empire, which had ruled from the Tarim Basin to Gansu, broke apart into rival principalities, opening an “era of fragmentation” that lasted until the Mongols.
summary.zh: 赞普朗达玛于842年被杀，两个年幼继承人之间的王位之争使王室分裂。曾统治从塔里木盆地到河西地区的吐蕃王朝分崩离析为相互敌对的割据政权，进入一直持续到蒙古时代的“分裂时期”。

sources.title: Sam van Schaik, Tibet: A History (2011)
Matthew T. Kapstein, The Tibetans (2006)
Britannica: Tibet — History

note: Langdarma’s persecution of Buddhism and his murder by a monk are told by later Buddhist histories; contemporary sources are thin. Wikidata has no item for the collapse (Q558271 is Langdarma).

story.en:
For two centuries the Tibetan emperors had been among the great powers of Asia. Their armies had occupied Chang’an in 763, held the Tarim Basin and the Gansu corridor, and signed a treaty of equals with the Tang in 821. Their last ruler of the united empire, Udumtsen, is known to Tibetan history by the nickname Langdarma.

Buddhist chronicles written long afterwards remember him as a persecutor who closed the monasteries and forced monks to marry or hunt. They say he was killed in 842 by a monk named Lhalung Palgyi Dorje, who rode up on a horse blackened with soot, wearing a cloak that was black outside and white inside, shot the king with an arrow, then washed his horse in a river and reversed his cloak to escape. Historians treat this as legend.

What followed is clearer. Two queens each put forward an infant son, the nobles split behind them, and the empire dissolved. Garrisons in the north-east were lost to local rebels such as Zhang Yichao at Dunhuang. Central Tibet broke into small lordships, and organised Buddhism did not revive until the eleventh century.
story.zh:
两百年间，吐蕃赞普一直是亚洲强国之一。其军队曾于763年攻占长安，控制塔里木盆地和河西走廊，并于821年与唐朝订立对等的盟约。统一王朝的最后一位赞普达磨乌东赞，在藏族历史上以绰号“朗达玛”为人所知。

很久以后写成的佛教史书把他记作一个灭佛者，说他封闭寺院，强迫僧人还俗娶妻或打猎。据说842年，一位名叫拉隆·贝吉多吉的僧人骑着一匹用烟灰涂黑的马，身穿外黑内白的斗篷，一箭射死赞普，然后在河中洗净马匹、反穿斗篷逃走。史家将此视为传说。

此后的情形较为清楚：两位王妃各自拥立一个幼子，贵族分裂为两派，帝国随之瓦解。东北方的驻军领地被敦煌张议潮等地方起事者夺去，卫藏地区分裂为许多小领主，有组织的佛教直到十一世纪才复兴。

summary.en: In a gorge of the Flaming Mountains near Turfan, the Buddhist Uyghur kings of Qocho sponsored cave temples painted with vast scenes of the Buddha’s former lives and portraits of Uyghur princes and Sogdian donors. In 1905 the German explorer Albert von Le Coq cut out many murals and shipped them to Berlin.
summary.zh: 在吐鲁番附近火焰山的峡谷中，信奉佛教的高昌回鹘王室资助开凿了石窟寺，绘有大型佛本生誓愿图以及回鹘王族和粟特供养人的画像。1905年，德国探险家勒柯克割下大量壁画运往柏林。

sources.title: Albert von Le Coq, Buried Treasures of Chinese Turkestan (1928)
Valerie Hansen, The Silk Road: A New History (2012)
Wikipedia: Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves

note: The caves were begun under the Tang (from the 6th–7th century) but most surviving paintings date from the Uyghur period (9th–13th century), which the span shows.

story.en:
After the fall of their steppe empire in 840, many Uyghurs settled in the Turfan oasis and built the kingdom of Qocho. There the former Manichaeans gradually turned to Buddhism, and their kings and nobles paid for cave temples cut into the cliffs above the Murtuk river at Bezeklik, “the place of paintings”.

The most famous caves hold huge pranidhi scenes, showing the Buddha in earlier lives making vows before past Buddhas, surrounded by monks, kings and merchants from many lands. On the walls kneel the donors themselves: Uyghur princes in tall crowns and red robes, and their wives with elaborate headdresses, labelled in Uyghur script.

In 1905 Albert von Le Coq of the Berlin Ethnological Museum’s Turfan expeditions spent weeks sawing the best murals from the walls in sections and packing them for the journey to Germany. Many were destroyed when Allied bombing hit the Berlin museum during the Second World War. Those left in the caves had already lost their faces to later iconoclasts. Digital projects now try to reunite the scattered fragments.
story.zh:
840年草原帝国覆灭后，许多回鹘人定居吐鲁番绿洲，建立高昌回鹘王国。昔日的摩尼教徒在这里逐渐改信佛教，国王和贵族出资在木头沟河上方的崖壁上开凿石窟，这就是“有画的地方”柏孜克里克。

最著名的洞窟绘有巨幅誓愿图，描绘佛陀前世在过去诸佛前发愿的情景，周围簇拥着来自各地的僧人、国王和商人。墙上还跪着供养人本人：头戴高冠、身穿红袍的回鹘王子，以及头饰繁复的王妃，旁边以回鹘文题名。

1905年，柏林民族学博物馆吐鲁番考察队的勒柯克花了数周时间，把最精美的壁画分块锯下，装箱运往德国。二战期间盟军轰炸击中柏林的博物馆，其中许多被毁。留在洞窟中的壁画，人物面部早已被后来的破坏者刮去。如今的数字化项目正尝试把散落各地的残片重新拼合。

summary.en: The Samanid amir Ismail defeated and captured the Saffarid ruler Amr ibn al-Layth near Balkh. Amr was sent to Baghdad, and the caliph granted Ismail Khurasan, making the Samanids masters of the eastern Islamic world.
summary.zh: 萨曼王朝埃米尔伊斯玛仪在巴尔赫附近击败并俘获萨法尔王朝统治者阿穆尔·伊本·莱斯。阿穆尔被押往巴格达，哈里发把呼罗珊授予伊斯玛仪，萨曼王朝由此成为伊斯兰世界东部的霸主。

sources.title: Narshakhi, The History of Bukhara, tr. R. N. Frye (1954)
Richard N. Frye, The Golden Age of Persia (1975)
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Khorasan vi. History in the Taherid and Samanid Periods

story.en:
Amr ibn al-Layth had inherited from his brother, the coppersmith-turned-conqueror Ya‘qub, an empire across eastern Iran. In 898 he persuaded the caliph al-Mu‘tadid to grant him Transoxiana as well, though it was ruled by the Samanid Ismail. Amr marched to the Oxus; Ismail crossed it to meet him.

In the spring of 900 the armies met near Balkh. Amr’s troops were defeated, and the Saffarid himself was captured; one tradition says his horse bolted and carried him into the enemy lines. A famous anecdote, retold in Persian books of advice for rulers, says that on the morning of the battle Amr’s kitchen needed hundreds of camels to carry it, while that evening a dog ran off with the pot holding his meal, and the captive laughed that his kitchen had become so light.

Ismail sent Amr to Baghdad, where he was put to death in 902. The caliph rewarded Ismail with Khurasan. Under the Samanids Bukhara became the capital of a Persian-speaking court and one of the great intellectual centres of the Islamic world.
story.zh:
阿穆尔·伊本·莱斯从兄长、由铜匠起家的征服者叶尔孤白手中继承了横跨伊朗东部的帝国。898年，他说服哈里发穆阿台迪德把河中地区也封给他，尽管那里由萨曼王朝的伊斯玛仪统治。阿穆尔进军阿姆河，伊斯玛仪渡河迎战。

900年春，两军在巴尔赫附近交锋。阿穆尔的军队战败，他本人被俘；一种说法是他的坐骑受惊，把他带进了敌阵。一则在波斯君王训诫书中反复流传的轶事说，开战那天早晨，阿穆尔的御厨要用几百峰骆驼驮运，到了傍晚，一条狗就叼走了盛着他饭食的锅子，被俘的阿穆尔笑说自己的厨房变得如此轻便。

伊斯玛仪把阿穆尔送往巴格达，阿穆尔于902年在那里被处死。哈里发把呼罗珊赏给伊斯玛仪。在萨曼王朝治下，布哈拉成为一个讲波斯语的宫廷所在地，也是伊斯兰世界伟大的学术中心之一。

name.zh: 喀喇汗王朝突厥人皈依伊斯兰教

summary.en: The Karakhanid ruler Satuq Bughra Khan, who according to tradition converted in his youth, made Islam the religion of his dynasty before his death in 955; in 960 chroniclers report that 200,000 tents of Turks converted. It was the first Turkic dynasty to adopt Islam.
summary.zh: 据传喀喇汗王朝统治者萨图克·布格拉汗年少时便已皈依，他在955年去世前使伊斯兰教成为王朝的宗教；编年史家记载，960年有二十万帐突厥人改信伊斯兰教。喀喇汗王朝是第一个皈依伊斯兰教的突厥王朝。

sources.title: Ibn Miskawayh, Tajarib al-umam; Ibn al-Athir, al-Kamil fi’l-ta’rikh, s.a. 349 AH
Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Wikipedia: Sultan Satuq Bughra Khan

note: The conversion of Satuq Bughra is known from a later hagiography (Tadhkira-i Bughra Khan); the 960 mass conversion is reported by Ibn Miskawayh. The marker is at his tomb in Artux near Kashgar. No Wikidata item exists for the event.

story.en:
For three centuries Muslim armies and preachers had faced the Turks across the Syr Darya. The breakthrough came from inside a Turkic ruling family. According to a hagiography written down much later, the young Karakhanid prince Satuq, nephew of the ruler of Kashgar, met a Samanid Muslim merchant or scholar and secretly accepted Islam. With the support of Muslim followers he overthrew his uncle and took the title Bughra Khan.

Satuq died in 955 and was buried at Artux near Kashgar, where his tomb is still a place of pilgrimage. Five years later, the Arab historians Ibn Miskawayh and Ibn al-Athir report, “two hundred thousand tents of Turks” converted to Islam. The figure is surely a round number, but it marks the moment when a large Turkic confederation entered the Islamic world as a whole.

The consequences ran far. Within forty years the Karakhanids took Bukhara from the Samanids. Their court produced the first great works of Islamic Turkic literature, and the Seljuks and Ottomans later followed the same road from steppe to sultanate.
story.zh:
三百年来，穆斯林的军队和传教者一直隔着锡尔河与突厥人对峙。突破来自突厥统治家族内部。据一部很久以后才成书的圣徒传记，喀什噶尔统治者的侄子、年轻的喀喇汗王子萨图克结识了一位萨曼王朝的穆斯林商人或学者，秘密皈依伊斯兰教。他在穆斯林追随者支持下推翻叔父，号称布格拉汗。

萨图克于955年去世，葬于喀什附近的阿图什，其陵墓至今仍是朝拜之地。据阿拉伯史家伊本·米斯卡韦和伊本·艾西尔记载，五年后有“二十万帐突厥人”皈依伊斯兰教。这个数字显然是概数，但它标志着一个庞大的突厥部落联盟整体进入伊斯兰世界。

其影响十分深远。四十年内喀喇汗王朝便从萨曼王朝手中夺取布哈拉，其宫廷产生了伊斯兰突厥文学最早的伟大作品，后来的塞尔柱人和奥斯曼人也走上了从草原到苏丹国的同一条道路。

name.en: Karakhanids take Bukhara; fall of the Samanids
name.zh: 喀喇汗王朝攻占布哈拉，萨曼王朝灭亡

summary.en: In October 999 the Karakhanid Nasr ibn Ali entered Bukhara unopposed, after preachers urged its people not to fight fellow Muslims, and carried off the Samanid family. The Oxus became the border between the Karakhanids in Transoxiana and Mahmud of Ghazni in Khurasan.
summary.zh: 999年10月，喀喇汗王朝的纳斯尔·伊本·阿里兵不血刃进入布哈拉，此前宣教者劝说城民不要与同为穆斯林者交战；萨曼王族被掳走。此后阿姆河成为河中地区的喀喇汗王朝与呼罗珊的伽色尼马哈茂德之间的边界。

sources.title: Gardizi, Zayn al-akhbar
C. E. Bosworth, The Ghaznavids (1963)
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Khorasan vi. History in the Taherid and Samanid Periods

note: The last Samanid prince, Isma‘il al-Muntasir, fought on until he was killed in 1005.

summary.en: Yusuf Khass Hajib of Balasagun presented to the Karakhanid ruler at Kashgar his Kutadgu Bilig (“Wisdom That Brings Good Fortune”), a poem of some 6,500 couplets on statecraft told through dialogues between a king, his vizier, a sage and an ascetic. It is the oldest major work of Islamic Turkic literature.
summary.zh: 巴拉沙衮人优素福·哈斯·哈吉甫在喀什噶尔向喀喇汗统治者献上《福乐智慧》，这部约六千五百联的长诗通过国王、大臣、智者和隐士之间的对话论述治国之道，是伊斯兰突厥文学现存最早的重要作品。

sources.title: Yusuf Khass Hajib, Wisdom of Royal Glory (Kutadgu Bilig), tr. Robert Dankoff (1983)
Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Wikipedia: Kutadgu Bilig

name.en: Mahmud al-Kashgari’s Compendium of the Turkic Dialects
name.zh: 麻赫穆德·喀什噶里《突厥语大词典》

summary.en: In Baghdad, the Karakhanid scholar Mahmud al-Kashgari wrote in Arabic a dictionary of the Turkic languages, with poems, proverbs, notes on tribes and a round map of the world centred on Balasagun. It is the founding text of Turkic philology.
summary.zh: 喀喇汗学者麻赫穆德·喀什噶里在巴格达用阿拉伯文编写了一部突厥语词典，收录诗歌、谚语和部落知识，并附有一幅以巴拉沙衮为中心的圆形世界地图，是突厥语文学的奠基之作。

sources.title: Mahmud al-Kashgari, Compendium of the Turkic Dialects, tr. R. Dankoff & J. Kelly (1982–85)
Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Wikipedia: Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk

note: The book was written in Baghdad, where the marker stands; its author came from Kashgar.

story.en:
Mahmud al-Kashgari was probably a member of the Karakhanid royal family who left his homeland after a palace upheaval and spent years travelling among the Turkic tribes before settling in Baghdad. The Seljuk Turks now dominated the caliphate, and Arabs needed to understand their language. Mahmud set out, as he wrote, to show that Turkic was the equal of Arabic.

His Diwan Lughat al-Turk arranges thousands of Turkic words by Arabic grammatical patterns and illustrates them with verses of war, love and the seasons, proverbs and notes on customs. It is the earliest description of the Turkic dialects and their speakers, from the Oghuz to the Uyghurs. It also contains a remarkable round map, oriented with east at the top, with the Karakhanid city of Balasagun near the centre, Japan at the edge and the lands of the Turks spread across it.

Only one manuscript survives, copied in 1266. It came to light in Istanbul in 1914, when the bibliophile Ali Emiri bought it from a book dealer. Since then it has been studied as the founding text of Turkic linguistics.
story.zh:
麻赫穆德·喀什噶里可能是喀喇汗王族成员，宫廷变乱后离开故乡，在突厥各部中游历多年，最后定居巴格达。当时塞尔柱突厥人主宰哈里发政权，阿拉伯人需要了解他们的语言。麻赫穆德自述，他要证明突厥语与阿拉伯语同样优美。

他的《突厥语大词典》按阿拉伯语法的词式排列数千个突厥语词，配以关于战争、爱情和四季的诗句、谚语以及风俗注释，是对从乌古斯到回鹘各突厥方言及其使用者最早的描述。书中还有一幅非凡的圆形地图，以东方为上，喀喇汗城市巴拉沙衮位于中心附近，日本在边缘，突厥人的土地铺展其间。

此书仅存一部抄本，抄于1266年。1914年藏书家阿里·埃米里从伊斯坦布尔一位书商手中购得，它才重见天日。此后它一直被视为突厥语言学的奠基文献。

summary.en: Ordered west by Ögedei, Batu and the veteran Subutai led a great army that destroyed Volga Bulgaria, the Cumans and most of the Rus’ principalities, then struck Poland and Hungary in 1241. The death of Ögedei brought them back to the Volga, where Batu founded the Golden Horde.
summary.zh: 拔都和老将速不台奉窝阔台之命西征，率大军灭亡伏尔加保加尔、钦察和大部分罗斯公国，1241年又进攻波兰和匈牙利。窝阔台去世后大军撤回伏尔加河，拔都在那里建立金帐汗国。

label.en: Bilär, capital of Volga Bulgaria, destroyed
label.zh: 伏尔加保加尔都城比勒尔被毁

label.en: Vladimir falls; Battle of the Sit River
label.zh: 攻陷弗拉基米尔，锡季河之战

label.en: Campaigns against the Cumans and in the Caucasus
Battle of Mohi on the Sajó (April)

sources.title: Timothy May, The Mongol Conquests in World History (2012)
Peter Jackson, The Mongols and the West, 1221–1410 (2005)
Britannica: Batu

note: Wikidata’s item begins with the 1223 Kalka raid (recorded separately). The marker is at Bilär, the first great target.

story.en:
The kurultai of 1235 decided to finish the conquest of the western steppe that Jebe and Subutai had scouted twelve years earlier. Command went to Batu, son of Jochi, with Subutai as his chief strategist and princes of every branch of the family, including Möngke and Güyük, at his side.

The campaign moved with terrible speed. Volga Bulgaria fell in 1236. In the winter of 1237–38, using the frozen rivers as roads, the Mongols took Ryazan, Vladimir and a dozen other towns; Novgorod was saved only by the spring thaw. Kyiv was stormed in December 1240. In April 1241 one army destroyed a Polish and German force at Legnica while Batu and Subutai crossed the Carpathians and crushed King Béla IV of Hungary at Mohi on the Sajó.

Western Europe braced for the next blow, but in 1242 the Mongols turned back. News that Ögedei had died may have reached them, or Batu may have wanted to secure the steppe. He settled on the lower Volga, and the Rus’ principalities remained tributaries of his Golden Horde for two centuries.
story.zh:
1235年的忽里勒台决定完成对西部草原的征服，哲别和速不台十二年前已对这一带进行过侦察。指挥权交给术赤之子拔都，速不台为主要谋臣，蒙哥、贵由等黄金家族各支宗王随行。

西征推进之迅猛令人恐惧。1236年伏尔加保加尔陷落。1237—1238年冬，蒙古军以冰封的河流为道路，攻陷梁赞、弗拉基米尔等十余座城镇；诺夫哥罗德只因春季解冻才幸免。1240年12月基辅被攻破。1241年4月，一路大军在列格尼卡击溃波兰和德意志联军，拔都与速不台则翻越喀尔巴阡山，在赛约河畔的莫希大败匈牙利国王贝拉四世。

西欧惶惶不安，等待下一次打击，但1242年蒙古军却撤回了。也许是窝阔台去世的消息传到了军中，也许是拔都想先巩固草原。他在伏尔加河下游定居下来，此后两百年间，罗斯诸公国一直是金帐汗国的纳贡者。

name.en: John of Plano Carpini’s mission to the Great Khan

summary.en: Sent by Pope Innocent IV after the Mongol invasion of Europe, the Franciscan John of Plano Carpini travelled via Kyiv and Batu’s camp on the Volga to Mongolia, where he witnessed the enthronement of Güyük in 1246. He returned with the khan’s demand that the pope submit and wrote the first Latin account of the Mongols.
summary.zh: 蒙古入侵欧洲之后，教皇英诺森四世派方济各会士柏朗嘉宾出使。他经基辅和拔都在伏尔加河的营地抵达蒙古，1246年目睹贵由即位，带回大汗要求教皇臣服的国书，并写下了第一部关于蒙古人的拉丁文记述。

label.zh: 伏尔加河畔的拔都营地（4月）

label.en: Sira Ordo near Karakorum: Güyük enthroned (August)
label.zh: 哈拉和林附近的昔剌斡耳朵：贵由即位（8月）

label.en: Reports to the pope at Lyon (November)

sources.title: John of Plano Carpini, History of the Mongols, in C. Dawson (ed.), The Mongol Mission (1955)
Peter Jackson, The Mongols and the West, 1221–1410 (2005)
Britannica: Giovanni da Pian del Carpini

note: No Wikidata item exists for the mission (Q315149 is Carpini). The location of Sira Ordo, Güyük’s tent palace, is approximate.

story.en:
In 1245, four years after the Mongols had ravaged Poland and Hungary, Pope Innocent IV sent letters to the unknown ruler of the “Tartars” asking him to stop attacking Christians and to accept baptism. His envoy was John of Plano Carpini, a Franciscan in his sixties who had known Francis of Assisi.

The journey nearly killed him. The Mongols passed him from post to post across the frozen steppe, changing horses several times a day. At Batu’s camp on the Volga he had to walk between two fires to be purified. In July 1246 he reached the great tent camp near Karakorum where princes and envoys from Rus’, Georgia, the caliphate and China had gathered, and in August he watched the election and enthronement of Güyük as Great Khan.

Güyük’s reply, written in Persian and sealed with a Mongol seal, survives in the Vatican archives. It told the pope to come in person with the kings of the West to offer service, and warned that God alone knew what would happen otherwise. Carpini’s report, the first careful Western description of Mongol life and warfare, circulated widely.
story.zh:
1245年，蒙古人蹂躏波兰和匈牙利四年之后，教皇英诺森四世致书那位不知名的“鞑靼”统治者，要求他停止进攻基督徒并接受洗礼。担任使者的是六十多岁、曾与亚西西的方济各相识的方济各会士柏朗嘉宾。

这次旅程几乎要了他的命。蒙古人把他从一个驿站送到下一个驿站，穿越冰封的草原，一天要换好几次马。在伏尔加河畔的拔都营地，他必须从两堆火之间走过以示洁净。1246年7月，他抵达哈拉和林附近的大帐营地，那里聚集着来自罗斯、格鲁吉亚、哈里发国和中国的王公与使节；8月，他亲眼见证贵由被推举并登基为大汗。

贵由以波斯文写成、加盖蒙古印玺的复信至今保存在梵蒂冈档案馆。信中要求教皇亲率西方诸王前来效劳，并警告说，否则后果如何只有上帝知道。柏朗嘉宾的报告是西方第一部细致描述蒙古人生活与战争的著作，流传甚广。

name.en: Sakya Pandita meets Köden at Liangzhou
name.zh: 萨迦班智达凉州会见阔端

summary.en: Summoned by Prince Köden, grandson of Genghis Khan, the Tibetan scholar Sakya Pandita travelled to Liangzhou in Gansu with his nephews Phagpa and Chakna and agreed to Mongol overlordship on behalf of Tibet. The meeting began the patron–priest relationship between Mongol rulers and the Sakya school.
summary.zh: 应成吉思汗之孙阔端之召，藏族学者萨迦班智达携侄子八思巴和恰那多吉来到河西的凉州，代表西藏接受蒙古的统治。这次会见开启了蒙古统治者与萨迦派之间的施主与福田关系。

sources.title: Sam van Schaik, Tibet: A History (2011)
Luciano Petech, Central Tibet and the Mongols (1990)
Wikipedia: Sakya Pandita

note: The meeting is dated 1247 in Tibetan sources; the letter Sakya Pandita sent home urging submission is known from later collections, and its authenticity is debated. No Wikidata item exists for the event (Q982008 is Sakya Pandita).

story.en:
In 1240 a Mongol force sent by Köden, the son of Ögedei who governed the Gansu frontier, raided central Tibet and burned monasteries. Köden then looked for a Tibetan leader who could speak for the whole country, and chose Sakya Pandita Kunga Gyaltsen, the most famous scholar of his day, a master of logic and Sanskrit.

Sakya Pandita, by then in his sixties, set out in 1244 with two young nephews, Phagpa and Chakna, and reached Köden’s camp at Liangzhou in 1247. Tibetan histories say he cured the prince of an illness and impressed him with Buddhist teaching. A letter attributed to him, sent back to Tibet’s leaders, urged them to submit and to pay tribute, since resistance to such a power was useless.

Sakya Pandita died at Liangzhou in 1251. His nephew Phagpa grew up at the Mongol court, became the teacher of Kublai Khan, and was made Imperial Preceptor with authority over Tibet. In 1269 he designed the square Phagspa script for writing Mongolian and Chinese. The model of a Mongol patron and a Tibetan lama would be revived by Altan Khan three centuries later.
story.zh:
1240年，统领河西边地的窝阔台之子阔端派兵进入卫藏，焚毁寺院。此后阔端寻找一位能代表整个西藏发言的藏族领袖，选中了当时最负盛名的学者、精通因明和梵文的萨迦班智达·贡噶坚赞。

年过六旬的萨迦班智达于1244年带着两个年幼的侄子八思巴和恰那多吉启程，1247年到达阔端在凉州的营帐。藏文史书说他治好了阔端的病，并以佛法令其折服。一封署其名、寄回西藏各地首领的信劝他们归顺纳贡，因为抗拒这样强大的力量毫无益处。

萨迦班智达于1251年在凉州去世。其侄八思巴在蒙古宫廷长大，成为忽必烈的上师，被封为帝师，掌管西藏事务。1269年他创制了方形的八思巴字，用于书写蒙古语和汉语。蒙古施主与藏族喇嘛的这种模式，三百年后被俺答汗重新启用。

name.en: William of Rubruck at Karakorum: the debate of religions
name.zh: 鲁布鲁克在哈拉和林：宗教辩论

summary.en: The Flemish friar William of Rubruck spent the first half of 1254 at Möngke Khan’s court and capital. On 30 May, at the khan’s order, he debated Buddhists and Muslims alongside Nestorian Christians; his report describes Karakorum’s quarters, its churches and temples, and the silver fountain-tree made by a captured Parisian goldsmith.
summary.zh: 佛兰德修士鲁布鲁克于1254年上半年住在蒙哥汗的宫廷和都城。5月30日，他奉大汗之命与景教徒一道同佛教徒和穆斯林辩论；他的报告描述了哈拉和林的街区、教堂与寺庙，以及一位被俘的巴黎金匠制作的银树酒泉。

sources.title: William of Rubruck, The Mission of Friar William of Rubruck, tr. P. Jackson & D. Morgan (1990)
Thomas T. Allsen, Mongol Imperialism (1987)
Britannica: Willem van Ruysbroeck (William of Rubruck)

note: No Wikidata item exists for the debate.

story.en:
Rubruck reached Möngke’s camp at the end of 1253 after a winter journey across the steppe, and followed the court to Karakorum in the spring. He was not impressed by the size of the city, which he compared unfavourably with the village of Saint-Denis outside Paris. But he noted its two quarters, one for Muslim merchants and one for Chinese craftsmen, its twelve temples of various peoples, two mosques and a Christian church.

At the palace stood a marvel made by Guillaume Boucher, a Parisian goldsmith captured in Hungary: a great silver tree with four lions at its foot, whose pipes poured wine, mare’s milk, rice wine and mead into basins when an angel at the top sounded a trumpet.

On 30 May 1254 Möngke ordered a formal debate. Rubruck, with the Nestorians, argued against Buddhist monks and then Muslims; at the end, he says, everyone drank heavily. Before he left, Möngke told him that as God had given the hand several fingers, so He had given men several ways. Rubruck went home with no converts but with the most vivid European account of the Mongol capital.
story.zh:
1253年底，鲁布鲁克冒着严冬穿越草原到达蒙哥的营帐，春天随宫廷来到哈拉和林。他对这座城市的规模不以为然，认为还比不上巴黎郊外的圣德尼村。但他记下城中有两个街区，一个住穆斯林商人，一个住汉人工匠，还有各族的十二座寺庙、两座清真寺和一座基督教堂。

宫殿前立着一件奇物，出自在匈牙利被俘的巴黎金匠纪尧姆·布歇之手：一棵巨大的银树，树下有四头银狮，树顶的天使吹响号角时，管道便把葡萄酒、马奶酒、米酒和蜜酒注入盆中。

1254年5月30日，蒙哥下令举行正式辩论。鲁布鲁克与景教徒一起先后同佛教僧人和穆斯林论辩；据他说，最后大家都喝得酩酊大醉。临行前，蒙哥对他说，正如上帝给了手几根手指，他也给了人几条道路。鲁布鲁克没有带回任何皈依者，却带回了欧洲人对蒙古都城最生动的描述。

name.en: Özbeg Khan makes Islam the Golden Horde’s religion
name.zh: 月即别汗使伊斯兰教成为金帐汗国的宗教

summary.en: On his accession in 1313, Özbeg Khan, who had converted to Islam, made it the faith of the Golden Horde’s ruling elite, overcoming the resistance of emirs who clung to Chinggisid tradition. The khanate drew closer to Mamluk Egypt, while Özbeg allowed the Russian Orthodox Church to keep its privileges.
summary.zh: 1313年即位的月即别汗已皈依伊斯兰教，他克服坚守成吉思汗传统的部分贵族的反对，使其成为金帐汗国统治集团的信仰。汗国与马木留克埃及关系更加密切，而月即别仍保留了俄罗斯东正教会的特权。

sources.title: István Vásáry, “The Jochid Realm”, in The Cambridge History of Inner Asia: The Chinggisid Age (2009)
Devin DeWeese, Islamization and Native Religion in the Golden Horde (1994)
Wikipedia: Öz Beg Khan

note: Islamisation was gradual; Berke (r. 1257–66) had already converted. The marker is at Sarai on the lower Volga. No Wikidata item exists for the event (Q335097 is Özbeg).

summary.en: Tokhtamysh, whom Timur had helped to the Golden Horde throne, turned on his patron and raided Tabriz and Transoxiana. Timur answered with two great campaigns into the steppe, winning at the Kondurcha in 1391 and the Terek in 1395, then burned Sarai, Astrakhan and Tana, wrecking the Horde’s cities and trade.
summary.zh: 曾得帖木儿扶持登上金帐汗位的脱脱迷失反噬恩主，劫掠大不里士和河中地区。帖木儿两次大举远征草原，1391年在昆都尔察河、1395年在捷列克河获胜，随后焚毁萨莱、阿斯特拉罕和塔纳，摧毁了金帐汗国的城市与商业。

label.zh: 脱脱迷失洗劫大不里士
金帐汗国军队劫掠撒马尔罕周边

label.en: Timur wins at the Kondurcha river
label.zh: 帖木儿在昆都尔察河获胜

sources.title: Beatrice Forbes Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane (1989)
Sharaf al-Din Ali Yazdi, Zafarnama
Britannica: Timur

note: Marker at the Terek battlefield. The sack of Sarai is placed by most historians in the winter of 1395–96.

story.en:
Tokhtamysh was a Jochid prince who came to Timur as a refugee in the 1370s. Timur gave him troops again and again until, in 1378–80, he won the throne of the Golden Horde and reunited it. Once secure, he claimed the old rights of the Jochids over Khwarazm and Azerbaijan, sacked Tabriz in 1385–86 and raided Timur’s own lands.

In 1391 Timur took an army of perhaps 100,000 men on a march of months across the steppe north of the Aral Sea, living by hunting, and caught Tokhtamysh at the Kondurcha river near the Volga. The Horde broke. Tokhtamysh recovered, and in 1395 Timur came again through the Caucasus and defeated him decisively on the Terek.

This time Timur set out to ruin the Horde. His troops burned Sarai and Astrakhan, destroyed the Italian trading post at Tana on the Don, and advanced into Rus’ as far as Yelets. The great caravan route north of the Caspian never recovered, trade shifted to Timur’s own roads through Iran, and the Golden Horde began to break apart. Tokhtamysh died a fugitive in Siberia around 1406.
story.zh:
脱脱迷失是一位术赤系宗王，1370年代作为流亡者投奔帖木儿。帖木儿一再给他兵马，直到他在1378—1380年夺得金帐汗位并重新统一汗国。地位稳固后，他宣称术赤系对花剌子模和阿塞拜疆拥有旧有权利，1385—1386年洗劫大不里士，还袭扰帖木儿本土。

1391年，帖木儿率领也许多达十万人的大军，在咸海以北的草原上行军数月，以狩猎为食，终于在伏尔加河附近的昆都尔察河追上脱脱迷失，金帐军溃败。脱脱迷失东山再起，1395年帖木儿经高加索再次北上，在捷列克河畔决定性地击败了他。

这一次帖木儿决意毁掉金帐汗国。他的军队焚毁萨莱和阿斯特拉罕，摧毁顿河口意大利人的商站塔纳，并深入罗斯直到叶列茨。里海以北的大商道从此一蹶不振，贸易转向帖木儿控制的伊朗道路，金帐汗国开始分崩离析。脱脱迷失约于1406年在西伯利亚流亡中死去。

name.en: Clavijo’s embassy to Timur at Samarkand
name.zh: 克拉维约出使撒马尔罕

summary.en: Ruy González de Clavijo, envoy of King Henry III of Castile, travelled from Spain through Constantinople and Iran to Samarkand, where Timur received him in September 1404. His diary describes the feasts in the garden palaces, the building of the Bibi-Khanym mosque and the old conqueror preparing to invade China.
summary.zh: 卡斯蒂利亚国王恩里克三世的使节克拉维约从西班牙出发，经君士坦丁堡和伊朗抵达撒马尔罕，1404年9月受到帖木儿接见。他的日记描述了园林宫殿中的盛宴、比比哈努姆清真寺的修建，以及这位年迈征服者筹备进攻中国的情形。

label.en: Sails from Puerto de Santa María (May)

label.zh: 在撒马尔罕觐见帖木儿（9月）

sources.title: Ruy González de Clavijo, Embassy to Tamerlane 1403–1406, tr. G. Le Strange (1928)
Beatrice Forbes Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane (1989)
Wikipedia: Ruy González de Clavijo

note: No Wikidata item exists for the embassy (Q725872 is Clavijo).

story.en:
Henry III of Castile wanted to know more about the ruler who had just crushed the Ottomans at Ankara, and in 1403 he sent a chamberlain, Ruy González de Clavijo, east with gifts. The journey took fifteen months by sea and land, through Constantinople, Trebizond and Iran.

Timur received the Spaniards in a garden outside Samarkand on 8 September 1404. Clavijo found him old, his eyelids so drooping that he could hardly see, seated on cushions before a fountain with red apples floating in it. When the envoys were seated, Timur had them placed above the ambassador of the Ming emperor, whom he called a thief and an enemy. For two months the court moved from one garden palace to another for feasts of horse meat, wine and endless roast sheep, and royal weddings in the meadow of Kan-i Gil.

Clavijo also watched Timur, carried in a litter, scolding the builders of his great mosque for working too slowly. He saw the army gathering for the march on China. Timur left in the winter and died at Otrar in February 1405, and Clavijo went home through a realm already at war over the succession.
story.zh:
卡斯蒂利亚国王恩里克三世想更多地了解这位刚在安卡拉击溃奥斯曼人的统治者，1403年派侍从官克拉维约携礼东行。这次旅程水陆兼程，经君士坦丁堡、特拉布宗和伊朗，历时十五个月。

1404年9月8日，帖木儿在撒马尔罕城外的一座花园里接见西班牙人。克拉维约看到他已年老，眼皮下垂得几乎看不见东西，坐在垫子上，面前喷泉中漂着红苹果。使节就座时，帖木儿让他们坐在明朝皇帝使者之上，并称明朝皇帝是盗贼和敌人。此后两个月，宫廷在一座座园林宫殿之间辗转设宴，吃马肉、饮葡萄酒，烤羊源源不断，还在坎尼吉尔草地上举行王室婚礼。

克拉维约还看到坐在轿中的帖木儿斥责其大清真寺的工匠干得太慢，又看到大军集结准备远征中国。帖木儿在冬天出发，1405年2月死于讹答剌；克拉维约启程回国时，帝国已因继承问题陷入战争。

name.en: Tsongkhapa founds the Great Prayer Festival and Ganden Monastery
name.zh: 宗喀巴创立传召大法会与甘丹寺

summary.en: In 1409 the reformer Tsongkhapa held the first Great Prayer Festival (Monlam Chenmo) at the Jokhang in Lhasa and founded Ganden Monastery east of the city. His followers, the Gelug school, built Drepung and Sera soon after and became the dominant tradition of Tibetan Buddhism.
summary.zh: 1409年，改革者宗喀巴在拉萨大昭寺举行首届传召大法会（默朗钦莫），并在拉萨以东创建甘丹寺。其追随者格鲁派随即兴建哲蚌寺和色拉寺，成为藏传佛教的主导教派。

sources.title: Sam van Schaik, Tibet: A History (2011)
Thupten Jinpa, Tsongkhapa: A Buddha in the Land of Snows (2019)
Britannica: Tsong-kha-pa

story.en:
Tsongkhapa was born in Amdo, in the far north-east of the Tibetan world, and came to central Tibet as a teenager to study. Over twenty years he studied with masters of every school and became convinced that Tibetan Buddhism had grown lax. He insisted on strict monastic discipline, including celibacy and abstinence from alcohol, and on careful study of logic and the great Indian treatises before tantric practice.

In the first month of 1409 he organised a great prayer festival at the Jokhang in Lhasa, with the support of the Phagmodrupa rulers of central Tibet. Thousands of monks gathered for two weeks of prayers and offerings, and Tsongkhapa had the Jowo statue adorned with a golden crown. The same year he and his disciples founded the monastery of Ganden, “the Joyous”, on a mountain east of Lhasa.

The movement grew rapidly. Drepung was founded in 1416 and Sera in 1419, the year Tsongkhapa died. His school, called the Gelug or “Virtuous Ones”, and its “Yellow Hats” later won the patronage of the Mongols and, under the Dalai Lamas, the government of Tibet. The Monlam festival was held every year until 1959.
story.zh:
宗喀巴生于西藏东北边缘的安多，少年时来到卫藏求学。二十年间他师从各派大师，深感藏传佛教已经松弛，于是坚持严格的僧团戒律，包括独身和戒酒，并主张在修习密法之前须认真研习因明和印度诸大论。

1409年藏历正月，他在卫藏帕竹政权支持下，于拉萨大昭寺组织了一场盛大的祈愿法会。数千僧人聚集，祈祷供养长达两周，宗喀巴还为觉卧佛像献上金冠。同年，他与弟子在拉萨以东的山上创建甘丹寺，意为“兜率”（喜足）。

这一运动发展迅速：1416年建哲蚌寺，1419年建色拉寺，宗喀巴也在这一年去世。他的教派称为格鲁派，即“善规派”，俗称“黄帽派”，后来赢得蒙古人的支持，并在达赖喇嘛领导下执掌西藏政权。传召大法会每年举行，直到1959年。

name.en: Gawhar Shad’s Musalla complex in Herat
name.zh: 高哈尔·沙德在赫拉特兴建的穆萨拉建筑群

summary.en: Gawhar Shad, consort of the Timurid ruler Shah Rukh, built a congregational mosque, a madrasa and her own mausoleum north of Herat, faced with tile mosaic and framed by tall minarets. Much of the complex was demolished by Afghan troops on British advice in 1885 to clear a field of fire; a few minarets and the mausoleum survive.
summary.zh: 帖木儿王朝君主沙哈鲁的王后高哈尔·沙德在赫拉特城北兴建了一座聚礼清真寺、一座经学院和她自己的陵墓，外饰彩砖镶嵌，四周耸立高大的宣礼塔。1885年，阿富汗军队在英国人建议下拆毁了建筑群大部，以清出射界；如今仅存几座宣礼塔和陵墓。

sources.title: Lisa Golombek & Donald Wilber, The Timurid Architecture of Iran and Turan (1988)
Robert Byron, The Road to Oxiana (1937)
Wikipedia: Musalla Complex

note: Construction dates vary between sources; the mosque was begun c. 1417 and the mausoleum completed by 1438. QID Q134700035 is the mosque.

story.en:
Gawhar Shad was one of the most powerful women of the fifteenth-century Islamic world. Married to Timur’s son Shah Rukh, she was a patron of architecture on a grand scale, paying for a great mosque at the shrine of Imam Reza in Mashhad and, at Herat, a complex of mosque and madrasa on a site called the Musalla, north of the city walls.

Its buildings were covered inside and out in tile mosaic of deep blue, turquoise and white, and her mausoleum, with its ribbed melon dome, became the burial place of Timurid princes. When the Timurid prince Abu Sa‘id took Herat in 1457, the old queen, by then nearly eighty, was accused of plotting against him and put to death. She was buried in her own tomb.

The complex survived for four centuries. Then in 1885, during the Panjdeh crisis, British officers feared a Russian assault on Herat and advised the Afghan emir to clear the ground in front of the walls. Most of the Musalla was blown up. The traveller Robert Byron, seeing the surviving minarets in 1933, thought the mosaic finer than anything he knew in Iran.
story.zh:
高哈尔·沙德是十五世纪伊斯兰世界最有权势的女性之一。她嫁给帖木儿之子沙哈鲁，大规模资助建筑，在马什哈德伊玛目礼萨圣陵出资修建一座大清真寺，又在赫拉特城墙以北名为“穆萨拉”的地方兴建了清真寺与经学院建筑群。

这些建筑内外贴满深蓝、松绿和白色的彩砖镶嵌，她那座带瓜棱形穹顶的陵墓成为帖木儿王族的墓地。1457年帖木儿王子阿布·赛义德攻占赫拉特时，年近八十的老王后被指控密谋反对他，遭到处死，葬于自己的陵墓中。

建筑群保存了四百年。1885年潘吉德危机期间，英国军官担心俄军进攻赫拉特，建议阿富汗埃米尔清理城墙前方的地面，穆萨拉大部分建筑被炸毁。1933年旅行家罗伯特·拜伦看到幸存的宣礼塔时，认为其彩砖镶嵌胜过他在伊朗所见的一切。

summary.en: Driven out of Fergana and Samarkand by Muhammad Shaybani’s Uzbeks, the young Timurid prince Babur crossed the Hindu Kush and took Kabul in October 1504. It became his kingdom for twenty years and the base from which he invaded India in 1526; he chose to be buried there.
summary.zh: 被昔班尼的乌兹别克人逐出费尔干纳和撒马尔罕后，年轻的帖木儿王子巴布尔翻越兴都库什山，于1504年10月夺取喀布尔。这里成为他二十年间的王国，也是他1526年入侵印度的基地；他选择死后葬在这里。

sources.title: Babur, The Baburnama, tr. Wheeler M. Thackston (1996)
Stephen F. Dale, The Garden of the Eight Paradises: Babur and the Culture of Empire (2004)
Britannica: Babur

note: No Wikidata item exists for the event.

story.en:
Babur inherited the small kingdom of Fergana at eleven and spent his youth fighting cousins for Samarkand, which he took and lost twice. In 1501 Muhammad Shaybani’s Uzbeks beat him at Sar-i Pul, and by 1504 he was a wanderer in the hills with a couple of hundred followers, some with clubs instead of swords, as he admits in his memoirs.

He turned south across the Hindu Kush. Kabul was held by Muqim, son of the Arghun ruler of Kandahar, who surrendered after a short siege in October 1504. Babur, now twenty-one, wrote that Kabul’s climate was delightful and that within a day’s ride one could find both snow and hot country, the fruits of the cold lands and of the warm.

For two decades he ruled Kabul, laid out gardens, made one more failed attempt on Samarkand, and raided India. In 1526 he defeated the Delhi sultan at Panipat and founded the Mughal empire. He died at Agra in 1530, but his body was brought back to the terraced garden on a hillside in Kabul that is still called Bagh-e Babur.
story.zh:
巴布尔十一岁继承小小的费尔干纳王国，青年时代一直与堂兄弟争夺撒马尔罕，两度得而复失。1501年他在萨里普勒败于昔班尼的乌兹别克人，到1504年已成为山中的流浪者，身边只有两三百名随从，据他在回忆录中坦言，有些人手里拿的是棍棒而不是刀剑。

他转而南越兴都库什山。喀布尔当时由坎大哈阿尔浑统治者之子穆基姆据守，1504年10月经短暂围城后投降。二十一岁的巴布尔写道，喀布尔气候宜人，骑马一日之内既可见到积雪，也可到达炎热之地，寒带与暖带的水果都能找到。

此后二十年他统治喀布尔，修建花园，又一次进攻撒马尔罕未果，并多次袭掠印度。1526年他在帕尼帕特击败德里苏丹，建立莫卧儿帝国。他于1530年死于阿格拉，遗体后来被运回喀布尔山坡上的阶梯式花园，那里至今仍称为“巴布尔花园”。

name.en: Altan Khan meets Sonam Gyatso: the title “Dalai Lama”
name.zh: 俺答汗会见索南嘉措：“达赖喇嘛”称号的由来

summary.en: At a temple near Kokonor, the Tümed Mongol ruler Altan Khan met the Gelug abbot Sonam Gyatso and gave him the title Dalai Lama, “ocean” lama; the title was applied retroactively to his two predecessors. Altan Khan adopted Buddhism, and the Gelug school gained the Mongol patrons who would later bring it to power in Tibet.
summary.zh: 土默特蒙古首领俺答汗在青海湖附近的一座寺院会见格鲁派高僧索南嘉措，赠予他“达赖喇嘛”称号，意为“大海般的”上师；这一称号也被追授给他的两位前世。俺答汗皈依佛教，格鲁派由此获得蒙古施主，后者日后助其在西藏掌权。

sources.title: Johan Elverskog, Our Great Qing: The Mongols, Buddhism and the State in Late Imperial China (2006)
Sam van Schaik, Tibet: A History (2011)
Britannica: Dalai Lama

note: The meeting took place at Chabchiyal (Thegchen Chönkhor) south-east of Kokonor; the coordinates are approximate. No Wikidata item exists for the event.

story.en:
Altan Khan of the Tümed had spent decades raiding Ming China and in 1571 finally won a peace treaty that opened border markets. Rich and powerful but not the senior Chinggisid khan, he looked for new sources of legitimacy. His nephew, who had campaigned in Tibet, suggested he invite a famous lama.

In 1578 Sonam Gyatso, abbot of Drepung and head of the Gelug school, travelled to meet him at a new temple near Kokonor. According to the Mongol and Tibetan accounts, the two men declared that they had met before: Altan was the reincarnation of Kublai Khan and Sonam Gyatso of Phagpa, Kublai’s Tibetan teacher. Altan gave him the title Dalai Lama, dalai being the Mongol word for ocean, and Sonam Gyatso gave Altan the title of a Buddhist king. Because he was held to be the rebirth of two earlier Gelug masters, Gendun Drup and Gendun Gyatso, who were then counted as the first two, Sonam Gyatso became the Third Dalai Lama.

Altan’s new laws banned blood sacrifices, including the killing of animals at funerals, and ordered the felt images of ancestral spirits to be burned, and Mongols began to build monasteries. When Sonam Gyatso died in 1588, his reincarnation was found in Altan Khan’s own great-grandson.
story.zh:
土默特部的俺答汗数十年间不断袭扰明朝，1571年终于达成和议，开放边境互市。他富有而强大，却并非成吉思汗后裔中的正统大汗，于是寻求新的合法性来源。曾在西藏作战的侄子建议他邀请一位著名喇嘛。

1578年，哲蚌寺住持、格鲁派领袖索南嘉措前往青海湖附近的一座新寺院与他会面。据蒙藏文献记载，二人宣称前世相识：俺答是忽必烈的转世，索南嘉措是忽必烈的上师八思巴的转世。俺答赠予他“达赖喇嘛”的称号，“达赖”在蒙古语中意为大海；索南嘉措则授予俺答一个佛教法王称号。由于他被视为两位格鲁派前辈根敦朱巴和根敦嘉措的转世，二人被追认为第一、二世，索南嘉措便成为第三世达赖喇嘛。

俺答颁布新法，禁止血祭，包括在葬礼上宰杀牲畜，并下令焚毁供奉祖灵的毡制翁衮像，蒙古人开始兴建寺院。1588年索南嘉措圆寂后，他的转世灵童在俺答汗的曾孙中被找到。

name.en: Erdene Zuu monastery founded at Karakorum
name.zh: 额尔德尼召在哈拉和林故址兴建

summary.en: Abtai Sain Khan of the Khalkha Mongols, newly converted to Gelug Buddhism, founded Erdene Zuu beside the ruins of Karakorum, partly with stones from the old capital. Enclosed by a long wall lined with stupas (108 were planned), it is probably the earliest surviving Buddhist monastery in Mongolia.
summary.zh: 刚皈依格鲁派的喀尔喀蒙古阿巴岱赛音汗在哈拉和林废墟旁兴建额尔德尼召，部分建材取自这座古都。寺院四周长墙上排列着佛塔（原计划108座），可能是蒙古现存最早的佛教寺院。

sources.title: UNESCO: Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape
Charles R. Bawden, The Modern History of Mongolia (1968)
Wikipedia: Erdene Zuu Monastery

note: The monastery was closed in the purges of 1937 and most of its temples were destroyed on Choibalsan’s orders by 1939; three temples survive and it is again an active monastery.

name.zh: 希尔多尔经学院建成，雷吉斯坦广场成形

summary.en: Yalangtush Bahadur, governor of Samarkand under the Ashtarkhanid khans of Bukhara, built the Sher-Dor (“Having Lions”) Madrasa facing Ulugh Beg’s, with tile tigers chasing deer beneath human-faced suns on its portal. With the later Tilya-Kori it completed the three-sided Registan.
summary.zh: 布哈拉阿斯特拉罕王朝诸汗治下的撒马尔罕总督亚兰格图什·巴哈杜尔在兀鲁伯经学院对面兴建希尔多尔（“有狮子的”）经学院，其门楼上彩砖图案描绘猛虎追逐小鹿，上方是有人脸的太阳。它与稍后的提拉卡里经学院一起，完成了三面环绕的雷吉斯坦广场。

sources.title: UNESCO: Samarkand – Crossroad of Cultures
Robert D. McChesney, Central Asia: Foundations of Change (1996)
Wikipedia: Sherdar Madrasa

name.en: Güshi Khan makes the Fifth Dalai Lama ruler of Tibet
name.zh: 固始汗扶立五世达赖喇嘛执掌西藏

summary.en: After the Khoshut Mongol army of Güshi Khan defeated the Tsang king at Shigatse, the Fifth Dalai Lama was enthroned there as ruler of Tibet in 1642. His government, the Ganden Phodrang, named after his residence at Drepung, ruled Tibet from Lhasa until 1959.
summary.zh: 和硕特蒙古固始汗的军队在日喀则击败藏巴汗之后，五世达赖喇嘛于1642年在那里被拥立为西藏统治者。他的政府以其在哲蚌寺的居所命名为“甘丹颇章”，以拉萨为中心统治西藏，直到1959年。

sources.title: Sam van Schaik, Tibet: A History (2011)
Kurtis R. Schaeffer, Matthew T. Kapstein & Gray Tuttle (eds.), Sources of Tibetan Tradition (2013)
Britannica: Tibet — History

note: No separate Wikidata item exists for the event (Q17500081 is the Ganden Phodrang government). Marker at Shigatse, where the enthronement took place.

story.en:
In the early seventeenth century the kings of Tsang in western Tibet patronised the rival Karma Kagyu school and pressed hard on the Gelug monasteries around Lhasa. The young Fifth Dalai Lama and his shrewd treasurer Sonam Chophel looked north for help, to the Oirat Mongols, and found it in Güshi Khan, chief of the Khoshut.

Between 1637 and 1641 Güshi Khan defeated the Gelug’s enemies in Kokonor and Kham, then marched on Tsang. In 1642, after a long siege, the fortress of Shigatse fell and the Tsang king was captured and later executed. In a ceremony at Shigatse, Güshi Khan presented the whole of Tibet to the Dalai Lama as an offering, keeping for himself the title of king and command of the army.

The new government took its name from Ganden Phodrang, the Dalai Lama’s palace at Drepung. The Fifth Dalai Lama, known to Tibetans as “the Great Fifth”, turned the offering into real authority: he organised a tax census, appointed governors, forcibly converted many Kagyu monasteries, and began building the Potala as the seat of the new state.
story.zh:
十七世纪初，西藏西部的藏巴汗扶持噶玛噶举派，对拉萨周围的格鲁派寺院施加重压。年轻的五世达赖喇嘛与精明的强佐索南群培向北方的卫拉特蒙古求援，找到了和硕特部首领固始汗。

1637至1641年间，固始汗在青海和康区击败格鲁派的敌人，随后进军后藏。1642年，经长期围攻，日喀则宗堡陷落，藏巴汗被俘，后被处死。在日喀则举行的仪式上，固始汗把全藏作为供养献给达赖喇嘛，自己保留汗王称号和兵权。

新政府以达赖喇嘛在哲蚌寺的宫殿“甘丹颇章”命名。被藏人尊称为“伟大的五世”的五世达赖喇嘛把这份供养变成了实际权力：他组织赋税清查，任命地方长官，强令许多噶举派寺院改宗，并开始修建布达拉宫作为新政权的中心。

summary.en: The Fifth Dalai Lama began building the White Palace on Marpori hill in Lhasa in 1645 and moved in in 1649; after his death his regent Desi Sangye Gyatso added the Red Palace, finished in 1694. The thirteen-storey palace, on the site of Songtsen Gampo’s earlier castle, was the seat of the Dalai Lamas until 1959.
summary.zh: 五世达赖喇嘛于1645年开始在拉萨红山上修建白宫，1649年迁入；他去世后，第巴桑结嘉措增建红宫，于1694年完工。这座高十三层的宫殿建在松赞干布早年宫堡的旧址上，直到1959年一直是达赖喇嘛的驻锡地。

sources.title: UNESCO: Historic Ensemble of the Potala Palace, Lhasa
Kurtis R. Schaeffer, The Culture of the Book in Tibet (2009)
Britannica: Potala Palace

note: Wikidata dates the site to Songtsen Gampo’s 7th-century palace; this record covers the 17th-century building.

story.en:
Tradition says that Songtsen Gampo built a palace on the Red Hill of Lhasa in the seventh century, but nothing visible remains of it. In 1645, three years after becoming ruler of Tibet, the Fifth Dalai Lama began a new palace there, named after Potalaka, the mountain home of the bodhisattva of compassion, Avalokiteshvara, of whom the Dalai Lamas were held to be emanations. The White Palace was ready for him in 1649.

The Fifth Dalai Lama died in 1682. His regent, Desi Sangye Gyatso, kept the death secret for some fifteen years, telling the Mongols and the Qing court that the Dalai Lama was in long meditative retreat, so that the building work and the government could continue undisturbed. Thousands of workers built the Red Palace, which holds the gilded tomb of the Fifth Dalai Lama, and the work was finished in 1694.

Rising more than a hundred metres above the city, with over a thousand rooms, the Potala was palace, monastery, treasury and tomb at once. It became a World Heritage site in 1994.
story.zh:
传说松赞干布在七世纪曾在拉萨红山上修建宫殿，但如今已看不到任何遗迹。1645年，即执掌西藏三年后，五世达赖喇嘛在此开建新宫，以观世音菩萨所居的普陀洛迦山命名，达赖喇嘛被视为观世音的化身。白宫于1649年建成，供他居住。

五世达赖喇嘛于1682年圆寂。第巴桑结嘉措秘不发丧约十五年，对蒙古人和清廷称达赖喇嘛正在长期闭关，以便工程和政务不受干扰。数千名工匠修建了红宫，其中安放着五世达赖喇嘛的鎏金灵塔，工程于1694年完成。

布达拉宫高出拉萨城一百多米，有一千多个房间，集宫殿、寺院、宝库和陵墓于一身。1994年它被列入世界遗产名录。

name.en: Dolon Nor assembly: Khalkha Mongols submit to the Qing
name.zh: 多伦会盟：喀尔喀蒙古归附清朝

summary.en: Driven from their homeland by the Dzungar ruler Galdan in 1688, the Khalkha Mongol khans and their spiritual leader Zanabazar sought refuge with the Qing. In 1691 at Dolon Nor the Kangxi emperor received their formal submission and reorganised them into banners.
summary.zh: 1688年喀尔喀蒙古诸汗及其宗教领袖哲布尊丹巴·扎那巴扎尔被准噶尔首领噶尔丹逐出故土，投奔清朝。1691年康熙帝在多伦诺尔接受其正式归附，并将其编为旗。

sources.title: Peter C. Perdue, China Marches West: The Qing Conquest of Central Eurasia (2005)
Charles R. Bawden, The Modern History of Mongolia (1968)
Wikipedia: Dolon Nor

note: No Wikidata item exists for the assembly (Q3494312 is the town).

story.en:
In 1688 Galdan Boshugtu, the Dzungar khan, invaded Khalkha, the heartland of the eastern Mongols, to punish its Tüsheet Khan for killing his brother. The Khalkha armies were routed, monasteries burned, and tens of thousands of Khalkhas fled south across the Gobi.

Their leaders had to choose a protector. Mongol tradition says the Tüsheet Khan’s brother Zanabazar, the revered First Jebtsundamba, settled the debate: Russia was a different religion and its people buttoned their coats the other way, while the Manchu emperor shared their faith and way of life. Whatever was actually said, the Khalkhas turned to the Qing.

In May 1691 the Kangxi emperor held a great assembly at Dolon Nor, the old site of Kublai’s summer capital. The Khalkha khans performed the kowtow, received Qing titles and were organised into banners on the Manchu model. The emperor marked the occasion by founding a monastery there. Five years later his armies broke Galdan at Jao Modo, and Khalkha remained part of the Qing empire until 1911.
story.zh:
1688年，准噶尔首领噶尔丹博硕克图为报其弟被杀之仇，入侵东蒙古腹地喀尔喀。喀尔喀军队溃败，寺院被焚，数万喀尔喀人南越戈壁逃难。

他们的首领必须选择一个保护者。蒙古传说称，土谢图汗之弟、备受尊崇的一世哲布尊丹巴扎那巴扎尔一锤定音：俄罗斯信仰不同，衣襟也是反着系的，而满洲皇帝与蒙古人信仰相同、生活方式相近。不论实际说了什么，喀尔喀人最终投向了清朝。

1691年5月，康熙帝在多伦诺尔，即忽必烈上都故地附近，举行盛大会盟。喀尔喀诸汗行跪拜礼，接受清朝封号，并仿照满洲制度编为旗。康熙帝还在当地兴建寺院以为纪念。五年后清军在昭莫多击溃噶尔丹，喀尔喀此后一直是清帝国的一部分，直到1911年。

name.zh: “赤脚逃亡”（阿克塔班·舒布伦德）

summary.en: A surprise Dzungar invasion in the spring of 1723 overran the Kazakh pastures of the Talas, Chu and Syr Darya and took Tashkent and Turkistan. Kazakh clans fled west and south in panic, losing herds and people; the catastrophe is remembered as the “Years of the Great Disaster”.
summary.zh: 1723年春，准噶尔军队突然入侵，席卷塔拉斯河、楚河和锡尔河的哈萨克牧场，攻占塔什干和突厥斯坦城。哈萨克各部惊慌地向西、向南逃亡，损失大量牲畜和人口；这场灾难被称为“大灾年”。

sources.title: Martha Brill Olcott, The Kazakhs (2nd ed., 1995)
Peter C. Perdue, China Marches West (2005)
Wikipedia: Barefooted Flight

note: The flight is dated 1723 with its effects lasting to about 1727; Kazakh tradition is the main source for its details. Marker at Turkistan, which the Dzungars took.

story.en:
By the 1720s the Dzungar Khanate under Tsewang Rabtan was the strongest power on the steppe, and the Kazakh hordes were divided after the death of Tauke Khan. In the spring of 1723, when the Kazakh herds were weak after winter, Dzungar armies struck without warning across the Tian Shan and down the Talas and Chu valleys.

The Kazakh clans of the Senior and Middle hordes fled in panic, abandoning their herds, their tents and many of their old people. Survivors streamed towards the oases of Bukhara, Khiva and Samarkand and the Syr Darya, where some were enslaved or starved. Kazakh oral tradition named the time Aqtaban Shubyryndy, “the barefooted flight” or “flight until the soles were white” and remembered it in the song of lament Elim-ai. The cities of Tashkent and Turkistan fell to the Dzungars.

The disaster pushed the three hordes into a rare common effort. In 1726 their leaders gathered at Ordabasy, and in the following years their united forces defeated the Dzungars at Bulanty and Anrakay. It also led the Junior Horde’s khan Abulkhair to seek Russian protection in 1731.
story.zh:
到1720年代，策妄阿拉布坦统治下的准噶尔汗国已是草原上最强大的力量，而头克汗死后哈萨克诸玉兹四分五裂。1723年春，正当哈萨克牲畜经冬瘦弱之际，准噶尔大军越过天山，沿塔拉斯河谷和楚河河谷突然袭来。

大玉兹和中玉兹的哈萨克各部惊慌逃散，丢下牲畜、毡帐和许多老人。幸存者涌向布哈拉、希瓦、撒马尔罕的绿洲和锡尔河一带，其中一些人沦为奴隶或饿死。哈萨克口头传统称这段时期为“阿克塔班·舒布伦德”，意为“赤脚逃亡”或“逃到脚底发白”，并以哀歌《祖国啊》（Elim-ai）纪念这段苦难。塔什干和突厥斯坦城落入准噶尔之手。

这场灾难促使三个玉兹难得地联合起来。1726年各部首领在奥尔达巴西会盟，此后几年联军在布兰提和安拉凯击败准噶尔。它也使小玉兹的阿布勒海尔汗于1731年寻求俄国保护。

name.en: Ahmad Shah Durrani proclaimed king at Kandahar
name.zh: 艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼在坎大哈称王

summary.en: After the murder of Nader Shah in 1747, a council of Pashtun tribal chiefs near Kandahar chose the young Abdali commander Ahmad Khan as their king. Taking the title Durr-i Durran, “pearl of pearls”, he founded the Durrani Empire, usually seen as the beginning of the Afghan state.
summary.zh: 1747年纳迪尔沙遇刺后，坎大哈附近的普什图部落首领会议推举年轻的阿布达里部将领艾哈迈德汗为王。他号称“珍珠中的珍珠”，建立杜兰尼帝国，通常被视为阿富汗国家的开端。

sources.title: Thomas J. Barfield, Afghanistan: A Cultural and Political History (2010)
Louis Dupree, Afghanistan (1973)
Britannica: Ahmad Shah Durrani

note: Details of the jirga (its place at Sher Surkh and the story of the wheat sheaf) come from later Afghan tradition. No Wikidata item exists for the event (Q467627 is the empire).

story.en:
Ahmad Khan of the Sadozai clan of the Abdali Pashtuns was about twenty-five and commanded Nader Shah’s Afghan cavalry when the Persian conqueror was assassinated by his own officers in June 1747. Ahmad led his men home towards Kandahar, reportedly carrying part of Nader’s treasure, including, according to some accounts, the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

Near Kandahar the Abdali chiefs met in a jirga to choose a leader. Afghan tradition says the debate dragged on for days because the leaders of the larger clans each wanted the throne, until a respected holy man, Sabir Shah, placed a sheaf of wheat in Ahmad’s turban as a crown, and the chiefs accepted the young man from a small clan precisely because none of them felt threatened by him. Ahmad took the title Durr-i Durran, “pearl of pearls”, and his tribe became the Durranis.

Over twenty-five years Ahmad Shah built an empire from Khurasan to Kashmir and Delhi, defeating the Marathas at Panipat in 1761. His great-grandsons lost most of it, but Afghans have remembered him as Ahmad Shah Baba, the father of the nation.
story.zh:
1747年6月波斯征服者纳迪尔沙被部下刺杀时，阿布达里普什图人萨多扎伊氏族的艾哈迈德汗约二十五岁，统领纳迪尔沙的阿富汗骑兵。他率部返回坎大哈，据说带走了纳迪尔的部分财宝，有些记载称其中包括“光之山”钻石。

阿布达里各部首领在坎大哈附近召开支尔格会议推选领袖。据阿富汗传说，由于大氏族的首领们都想登上王位，会议拖延了多日，直到一位德高望重的圣者萨比尔·沙把一束麦穗插在艾哈迈德的头巾上作为王冠；首领们之所以接受这位小氏族出身的年轻人，正是因为谁都不觉得他是威胁。艾哈迈德号称“珍珠中的珍珠”，其部落从此称为杜兰尼人。

二十五年间，艾哈迈德沙建立了一个从呼罗珊到克什米尔和德里的帝国，并于1761年在帕尼帕特击败马拉塔人。他的曾孙们失去了大部分疆土，但阿富汗人一直把他当作国父，尊称为“艾哈迈德沙巴巴”。

summary.en: Fearing Russian influence, the East India Company invaded Afghanistan in 1839 to replace Dost Mohammad Khan with the exiled Shah Shuja. A rising in Kabul in 1841 forced the British garrison to retreat in January 1842 through the winter passes, where almost all of it was destroyed. A punitive army retook Kabul and withdrew; Dost Mohammad returned to the throne.
summary.zh: 东印度公司担心俄国势力渗透，于1839年入侵阿富汗，以流亡的舒贾沙取代多斯特·穆罕默德汗。1841年喀布尔爆发起义，英军驻军被迫于1842年1月冒着严冬穿越山口撤退，几乎全军覆没。一支惩罚性军队重新攻占喀布尔后撤出，多斯特·穆罕默德重登王位。

label.en: Kabul rising; Burnes and Macnaghten killed
label.zh: 喀布尔起义，伯恩斯与麦克诺滕被杀
甘达马克最后抵抗（1月13日）
布赖登医生抵达贾拉拉巴德

sources.title: William Dalrymple, Return of a King: The Battle for Afghanistan (2013)
Thomas J. Barfield, Afghanistan: A Cultural and Political History (2010)
Britannica: Anglo-Afghan Wars

story.en:
In 1838 the Governor-General of India, Lord Auckland, convinced that the Afghan ruler Dost Mohammad Khan was leaning towards Russia and Persia, decided to replace him with Shah Shuja, a Durrani king who had lost his throne thirty years earlier. The Army of the Indus marched through the Bolan Pass in 1839, blew in the gate of Ghazni and installed Shah Shuja in Kabul that August.

The occupation lasted two years. British officers lived in a badly sited cantonment outside Kabul, subsidies to the tribes were cut, and resentment grew. In November 1841 a crowd killed the political agent Alexander Burnes at his house; in December Dost Mohammad’s son Akbar Khan shot the envoy William Macnaghten during negotiations. On 6 January 1842 some 4,500 troops and about 12,000 camp followers marched out of Kabul in the snow.

They were cut to pieces in the passes. The last organised group made a stand on the hill of Gandamak on 13 January, and that afternoon an army surgeon, William Brydon, rode alone into Jalalabad on a wounded pony. An Army of Retribution burned Kabul’s great covered bazaar later that year and left. Dost Mohammad came back and ruled for twenty more years.
story.zh:
1838年，印度总督奥克兰勋爵认定阿富汗统治者多斯特·穆罕默德汗倾向俄国和波斯，决定以三十年前失去王位的杜兰尼国王舒贾沙取而代之。1839年，印度河军团穿过波伦山口，炸开加兹尼城门，于当年8月把舒贾沙扶上喀布尔王位。

占领持续了两年。英国军官住在喀布尔城外一处选址不当的兵营里，给各部落的津贴被削减，怨恨日积月累。1841年11月，一群民众在家中杀死政治代表亚历山大·伯恩斯；12月，多斯特·穆罕默德之子阿克巴尔汗在谈判中枪杀特使麦克诺滕。1842年1月6日，约4500名士兵和约12000名随军人员冒雪撤出喀布尔。

他们在山口中被逐段歼灭。最后一支成建制的队伍于1月13日在甘达马克山丘上作最后抵抗；当天下午，军医威廉·布赖登骑着一匹受伤的小马，独自进入贾拉拉巴德。同年晚些时候，“报复之军”焚毁了喀布尔的大型有顶巴扎后撤离。多斯特·穆罕默德重返王位，又统治了二十年。

name.en: Stoddart and Conolly executed in Bukhara
name.zh: 斯托达特与康诺利在布哈拉被处决

summary.en: Two British officers, Colonel Charles Stoddart and Captain Arthur Conolly, who had come to Bukhara on missions during the First Anglo-Afghan War, were held for years by Emir Nasrullah and beheaded in front of the Ark in June 1842. Conolly had coined the phrase “the Great Game” for the Anglo-Russian rivalry.
summary.zh: 第一次英阿战争期间，英国军官斯托达特上校和阿瑟·康诺利上尉先后奉命来到布哈拉，被埃米尔纳斯鲁拉扣押多年，1842年6月在阿尔克城堡前被斩首。康诺利曾用“大博弈”一词称呼英俄之间的角逐。

sources.title: Peter Hopkirk, The Great Game (1990)
Fitzroy Maclean, A Person from England and Other Travellers (1958)
Wikipedia: Charles Stoddart

note: No Wikidata item exists for the execution (Q1066168 is Stoddart). The exact day in June 1842 is uncertain.

story.en:
Colonel Charles Stoddart reached Bukhara in December 1838 to reassure Emir Nasrullah about the British invasion of Afghanistan and to seek the release of Russian slaves. He began badly: by one account he rode into the square before the citadel instead of dismounting, and he carried no letter from Queen Victoria herself. The emir had him thrown into the “bug pit”, a deep dungeon beneath the Ark kept stocked with vermin.

Stoddart spent the next years in and out of prison. In 1841 Captain Arthur Conolly, an evangelical officer with dreams of freeing Central Asia’s slaves, came to Bukhara to seek his release, and was imprisoned too. Conolly had been the first to use the phrase “the Great Game” in a letter describing the contest with Russia for influence in Central Asia.

News of the British disaster in Kabul removed any fear of reprisal. In June 1842 both men were led out, made to dig their own graves before the Ark, and beheaded. An eccentric clergyman, Joseph Wolff, travelled to Bukhara in 1844 in full canonical dress to discover their fate and barely escaped with his life.
story.zh:
1838年12月，查尔斯·斯托达特上校抵达布哈拉，向埃米尔纳斯鲁拉解释英国入侵阿富汗之事，并争取释放被奴役的俄国人。他一开始就出了差错：据一种说法，他骑马进入城堡前的广场而没有下马，而且没有带来维多利亚女王本人的信件。埃米尔把他扔进“虫坑”，即阿尔克城堡下一处养满害虫的深牢。

此后几年，斯托达特时而入狱、时而获释。1841年，怀着解放中亚奴隶梦想的福音派军官阿瑟·康诺利上尉前来营救，结果也被关押。康诺利曾在一封信中第一次用“大博弈”一词形容与俄国在中亚的势力角逐。

英军在喀布尔惨败的消息传来，埃米尔再也不必担心报复。1842年6月，两人被押出，被迫在城堡前挖好自己的墓穴，随后被斩首。1844年，一位古怪的牧师约瑟夫·沃尔夫身着全套教士服前往布哈拉查明他们的下落，险些丧命。

summary.en: A Russian force under Vasily Perovsky, governor of Orenburg, besieged and stormed the Kokand fortress of Ak-Mechet on the Syr Darya and renamed it Fort Perovsky. It became the anchor of the Syr Darya line from which Russia advanced into Turkestan.
summary.zh: 奥伦堡总督佩罗夫斯基率俄军围攻并强攻锡尔河畔浩罕汗国的阿克梅切季要塞，将其改名为佩罗夫斯克堡。它成为俄国锡尔河防线的支点，俄国由此向突厥斯坦推进。

sources.title: Alexander Morrison, The Russian Conquest of Central Asia (2020)
Seymour Becker, Russia’s Protectorates in Central Asia (1968)
Wikipedia: Kyzylorda

summary.en: General Konstantin von Kaufman routed the army of the Bukharan emir on the Chupan-Ata heights and entered Samarkand in May 1868; a small Russian garrison then survived a week-long siege in the citadel. Bukhara accepted Russian protection, and Samarkand with Timur’s tomb became part of Russian Turkestan.
summary.zh: 1868年5月，考夫曼将军在丘班阿塔高地击溃布哈拉埃米尔的军队，进入撒马尔罕；随后一支小规模俄国守军在内城坚守了一周的围攻。布哈拉接受俄国保护，拥有帖木儿陵墓的撒马尔罕并入俄属突厥斯坦。

sources.title: Alexander Morrison, The Russian Conquest of Central Asia (2020)
Britannica: Samarkand
Wikipedia: Siege of Samarkand (1868)

note: Russian sources use Julian dates (Samarkand entered 2 May O.S. = 14 May N.S. 1868). No Wikidata item was found for the event.

story.en:
In the spring of 1868 the Emir of Bukhara, pressed by his clergy, declared a holy war on the Russians who had taken Tashkent. General Kaufman, the new governor-general of Turkestan, marched on Samarkand. On 1 May (Old Style) his infantry waded the Zeravshan under fire and drove the Bukharan army off the Chupan-Ata heights; the next day the city’s notables opened the gates.

Kaufman then marched on with most of his troops, leaving about 650 men in Samarkand’s citadel. In early June the forces of Shahrisabz and the townspeople rose and besieged them. For a week the garrison fought off assaults at the breaches. Among the defenders was the painter Vasily Vereshchagin, attached to Kaufman’s staff, who fought with a rifle and won the Order of St George before Kaufman returned to relieve the citadel.

Bukhara signed a treaty that made it a Russian protectorate. Vereshchagin turned his experiences into a series of Turkestan paintings, among them The Apotheosis of War, a pyramid of skulls in the desert dedicated “to all great conquerors, past, present and to come”.
story.zh:
1868年春，布哈拉埃米尔在宗教人士的压力下，向已占领塔什干的俄国人宣布圣战。新任突厥斯坦总督考夫曼将军进军撒马尔罕。5月1日（俄历），他的步兵冒着炮火涉过泽拉夫尚河，把布哈拉军队赶下丘班阿塔高地；次日，城中显要打开城门。

考夫曼随后率主力继续进军，只在撒马尔罕内城留下约650人。6月初，沙赫里萨布兹的军队和城中居民起事，将守军围困。一周之内，守军在城墙缺口处一次次击退进攻。守军中有随考夫曼参谋部出征的画家瓦西里·韦列夏金，他持枪作战，获得圣乔治勋章，直到考夫曼回师解围。

布哈拉签订条约，成为俄国的保护国。韦列夏金把这段经历画成了一组“突厥斯坦系列”作品，其中《战争的礼赞》描绘荒漠中一座头骨堆成的金字塔，题献给“一切伟大的征服者，过去的、现在的和将来的”。

summary.en: Columns from Tashkent, Orenburg and the Caspian converged across the deserts on Khiva, which surrendered to General Kaufman in May 1873. The Treaty of Gandomian made the khanate a Russian protectorate, ceded the right bank of the Amu Darya and abolished slavery.
summary.zh: 俄军分别从塔什干、奥伦堡和里海沿岸出发，穿越沙漠会攻希瓦，希瓦于1873年5月向考夫曼将军投降。《甘多米安条约》使该汗国成为俄国保护国，割让阿姆河右岸，并废除奴隶制。

summary.en: After a rising against Khan Khudayar and the Russians in 1875, troops under Mikhail Skobelev crushed the rebels and in February 1876 the khanate was abolished and turned into the Fergana province of Russian Turkestan.

Wikipedia: Khanate of Kokand
