summary.en: After Emir Sher Ali received a Russian mission but turned back a British one, British India invaded Afghanistan in 1878. The war saw the massacre of the British envoy in Kabul, an Afghan victory at Maiwand and Roberts’s march from Kabul to Kandahar; it ended with Abdur Rahman Khan as emir and Britain in control of Afghan foreign policy.
summary.zh: 埃米尔希尔·阿里接待俄国使团却拒绝英国使团之后，英属印度于1878年入侵阿富汗。战争中英国驻喀布尔使节遇害，阿富汗人在迈万德获胜，罗伯茨率军从喀布尔进军坎大哈；战争以阿卜杜·拉赫曼汗出任埃米尔、英国控制阿富汗外交告终。

label.en: British columns cross the Khyber and Kurram passes (November)
label.zh: 英军穿越开伯尔与库拉姆山口（11月）

label.en: Treaty of Gandamak with Yaqub Khan (May)
label.zh: 与叶尔孤白汗签订《甘达马克条约》（5月）

label.en: Envoy Cavagnari killed; Roberts occupies Kabul
label.zh: 使节卡瓦尼亚里被杀，罗伯茨占领喀布尔

label.en: Ayub Khan defeats the British at Maiwand (27 July)
label.zh: 阿尤布汗在迈万德击败英军（7月27日）
罗伯茨解坎大哈之围（9月1日）

sources.title: Thomas J. Barfield, Afghanistan: A Cultural and Political History (2010)
Britannica: Anglo-Afghan Wars
Wikipedia: Second Anglo-Afghan War

note: Marker at Maiwand, the war’s best-remembered battle.

story.en:
In the summer of 1878, as Britain and Russia confronted each other over the Ottoman Empire, a Russian mission arrived in Kabul. When Emir Sher Ali refused to receive a British mission as well, the Viceroy, Lord Lytton, sent three armies across the frontier. Sher Ali fled north and died at Mazar-i Sharif, and his son Yaqub Khan signed the Treaty of Gandamak, accepting a British envoy in Kabul.

The envoy, Sir Louis Cavagnari, lasted six weeks. In September 1879 mutinous Afghan troops stormed the residency and killed him and his escort. General Frederick Roberts occupied Kabul and hanged dozens of men accused of the attack, but resistance spread. On 27 July 1880 Sher Ali’s son Ayub Khan destroyed a British brigade at Maiwand, west of Kandahar. Afghan tradition remembers a young woman, Malalai, who rallied the wavering fighters with a verse and was killed carrying a banner.

Roberts marched some 500 kilometres from Kabul to Kandahar in about three weeks and defeated Ayub Khan on 1 September. Britain then recognised Abdur Rahman Khan as emir and withdrew, keeping control only of Afghanistan’s foreign relations.
story.zh:
1878年夏，英俄两国因奥斯曼帝国问题对峙之际，一个俄国使团抵达喀布尔。埃米尔希尔·阿里拒绝同时接待英国使团，印度总督利顿勋爵遂派三路大军越过边界。希尔·阿里北逃，死于马扎里沙里夫；其子叶尔孤白汗签订《甘达马克条约》，同意英国使节驻喀布尔。

使节卡瓦尼亚里爵士只待了六个星期。1879年9月，哗变的阿富汗士兵攻入使馆，杀死他和卫队。罗伯茨将军占领喀布尔，绞死数十名被控参与袭击的人，但抵抗反而蔓延。1880年7月27日，希尔·阿里之子阿尤布汗在坎大哈以西的迈万德全歼一个英军旅。阿富汗传说中，一位名叫马拉莱的年轻女子吟诵诗句鼓舞动摇的战士，最后手执旗帜阵亡。

罗伯茨率军用约三周时间从喀布尔行军约500公里赶到坎大哈，9月1日击败阿尤布汗。随后英国承认阿卜杜·拉赫曼汗为埃米尔并撤军，只保留对阿富汗外交的控制。

summary.en: In Kabul, Emir Abdur Rahman Khan and the British Indian foreign secretary Sir Mortimer Durand agreed a frontier between Afghanistan and British India some 2,600 km long. It divided the Pashtun and Baloch tribal lands and is still not recognised by Afghan governments as the border with Pakistan.
summary.zh: 埃米尔阿卜杜·拉赫曼汗与英属印度外务秘书莫蒂默·杜兰德爵士在喀布尔议定阿富汗与英属印度之间长约2600公里的边界。这条边界分割了普什图人和俾路支人的部落地区，阿富汗历届政府至今不承认其为与巴基斯坦的国界。

sources.title: Thomas J. Barfield, Afghanistan: A Cultural and Political History (2010)
Britannica: Durand Line
Wikipedia: Durand Line

note: Signed on 12 November 1893.

name.en: Sven Hedin discovers the ruins of Loulan
name.zh: 斯文·赫定发现楼兰古城

summary.en: Crossing the dry Lop Nur desert in March 1900, the Swedish explorer Sven Hedin’s caravan stumbled on the ruins of a walled town; he returned in 1901 and excavated documents identifying it as Loulan, a garrison and kingdom of the Han–Jin era abandoned in the fourth century.
summary.zh: 1900年3月，瑞典探险家斯文·赫定的驼队穿越干涸的罗布泊荒漠时，偶然发现一座有城墙的古城遗址；1901年他重返此地发掘，出土文书证明这里就是楼兰，汉晋时期的一个屯戍之地和王国，于四世纪被废弃。

sources.title: Sven Hedin, Scientific Results of a Journey in Central Asia, 1899–1902 (1904–07)
Valerie Hansen, The Silk Road: A New History (2012)
Britannica: Sven Anders Hedin

note: No Wikidata item exists for the discovery (Q1057551 is the Loulan kingdom).

story.en:
In March 1900 Sven Hedin was crossing the dry bed of the ancient Lop Nur, searching for evidence for his theory that the lake had wandered over the centuries. When the caravan stopped to dig a well, the men found that their only spade had been left behind at the previous camp. Hedin’s guide Ördek rode back to fetch it, lost his way in a sandstorm, and came upon ruined houses and carved wooden beams half-buried in the sand.

Hedin could not stay, as his water was running low, but he came back in March 1901 with a larger party. In a week of digging among the ruins of a walled town and a Buddhist stupa he found coins, silk, wooden tablets and paper documents in Chinese and in Kharoshthi, the Indian script used in the Tarim kingdoms. Back in Europe, the sinologist Karl Himly read the name of the place: Loulan.

Loulan had been the Han dynasty’s key garrison on the road from Dunhuang into the Tarim Basin and was abandoned in the fourth century as its rivers shifted. The discovery set off a race of archaeological expeditions to the region, led by Aurel Stein, Albert von Le Coq and Ōtani Kōzui.
story.zh:
1900年3月，斯文·赫定正穿越古罗布泊干涸的湖床，寻找证据支持他关于湖泊数百年来不断“游移”的理论。驼队停下来挖井时，众人发现唯一的铁锹落在了上一个营地。向导奥尔得克骑马回去取，在风沙中迷了路，却意外看到半埋在沙中的房屋废墟和雕花木梁。

由于饮水不足，赫定未能停留，但他于1901年3月带着更大的队伍回来。他在一座有城墙的古城和一座佛塔废墟中发掘了一周，找到钱币、丝绸、木简以及用汉文和佉卢文（塔里木诸国使用的一种印度文字）书写的纸文书。回到欧洲后，汉学家希姆莱从文书中读出了这个地方的名字：楼兰。

楼兰曾是汉朝从敦煌进入塔里木盆地道路上的重要屯戍据点，四世纪时因河道改变而被废弃。这一发现引发了斯坦因、勒柯克和大谷光瑞等人竞相前往该地区考古探险的热潮。

name.zh: 英国入侵西藏（荣赫鹏远征）

summary.en: Fearing Russian influence in Lhasa, the Viceroy Lord Curzon sent Colonel Francis Younghusband with an armed escort into Tibet. Its troops machine-gunned hundreds of Tibetan soldiers at Chumik Shenko, stormed Gyantse fort and entered Lhasa in August 1904; the Thirteenth Dalai Lama fled to Mongolia, and a treaty opened Tibet to British trade.
summary.zh: 印度总督寇松担心俄国势力进入拉萨，派荣赫鹏上校率武装卫队进入西藏。英军在曲米辛古用机枪射杀数百名藏军，攻占江孜宗堡，1904年8月进入拉萨；十三世达赖喇嘛出走蒙古，英方强迫签订的条约使西藏向英国贸易开放。

label.en: Crosses the Jelep La into Tibet (December)
label.zh: 翻越则里拉山口进入西藏（12月）

label.en: Massacre at Chumik Shenko near Guru (31 March)
label.zh: 古鲁附近曲米辛古屠杀（3月31日）

label.en: Enters Lhasa (3 August); Convention of Lhasa (September)
label.zh: 进入拉萨（8月3日），签订《拉萨条约》（9月）

sources.title: Charles Allen, Duel in the Snows: The True Story of the Younghusband Mission to Lhasa (2004)
Sam van Schaik, Tibet: A History (2011)
Britannica: Sir Francis Edward Younghusband

note: Marker at Gyantse. Tibetan deaths at Chumik Shenko are estimated at 600–700.

story.en:
Lord Curzon, Viceroy of India, became convinced in 1903 that the Thirteenth Dalai Lama was drifting into the Russian orbit through his Buryat adviser Agvan Dorzhiev. He sent Colonel Francis Younghusband, a soldier-explorer of the Great Game, with an escort of more than a thousand troops, machine guns and thousands of porters, to force talks.

On 31 March 1904 at Chumik Shenko, near the village of Guru, a Tibetan force blocking the road was surrounded. The British began to disarm them; a scuffle broke out, a Tibetan general fired a pistol, and the British opened fire with rifles and Maxim guns. In a few minutes some 600 to 700 Tibetans, armed mostly with matchlocks and swords, were killed as they walked away. One British officer wrote home that he hoped never again to have to shoot down men walking away.

The column stormed the fort of Gyantse in July and reached Lhasa on 3 August. The Dalai Lama had already fled to Mongolia. The Convention of Lhasa imposed an indemnity and trade marts, but London soon scaled it back. The real long-term winner was the Qing, which reasserted its own claims in Tibet in the following years.
story.zh:
1903年，印度总督寇松认定十三世达赖喇嘛正通过其布里亚特顾问德尔智向俄国靠拢。他派“大博弈”中以探险闻名的军人荣赫鹏上校，率一千多名士兵、机枪和数千名脚夫组成的卫队入藏，以武力逼迫谈判。

1904年3月31日，在古鲁村附近的曲米辛古，一支阻挡道路的藏军被包围。英军开始解除其武装，双方发生推搡，一名藏军将领开了一枪，英军随即用步枪和马克沁机枪开火。几分钟内，大多只持火绳枪和刀剑的约六七百名藏军在转身离开时被射杀。一名英国军官在家信中写道，希望再也不必射杀那些正在走开的人。

英军于7月攻占江孜宗堡，8月3日抵达拉萨，达赖喇嘛此前已出走蒙古。《拉萨条约》强加了赔款和商埠，但伦敦很快将其条款缩减。长期来看真正的获益者是清朝，此后几年它在西藏重申并强化了自身的主权要求。

name.en: Mongolia declares independence; the Bogd Khan enthroned
name.zh: 外蒙古宣布独立，博克多汗即位

summary.en: As the Qing dynasty collapsed, Khalkha nobles and lamas expelled the Manchu amban from Urga and on 29 December 1911 enthroned the Eighth Jebtsundamba Khutugtu as Bogd Khan of an independent Mongolia. Russia and China later reduced it to autonomy under Chinese suzerainty by the Kyakhta treaty of 1915.
summary.zh: 清朝崩溃之际，喀尔喀贵族和喇嘛驱逐驻库伦办事大臣，于1911年12月29日拥立第八世哲布尊丹巴呼图克图为独立蒙古的博克多汗。后来俄国与中国通过1915年《恰克图条约》将其降为中国宗主权下的自治。

sources.title: Charles R. Bawden, The Modern History of Mongolia (1968)
Urgunge Onon & Derrick Pritchatt, Asia’s First Modern Revolution: Mongolia Proclaims Its Independence in 1911 (1989)
Britannica: History of Mongolia

note: Independence was declared on 1 December 1911 and the enthronement held on 29 December. No separate Wikidata item exists for the event (Q2475921 is the Bogd Khanate).

story.en:
In the last years of the Qing, the “New Policies” of the court threatened Mongolia with Chinese settlement, garrisons and taxes. In the summer of 1911 a group of Khalkha nobles, with the blessing of the Jebtsundamba Khutugtu, the head of Mongolian Buddhism, secretly went to St Petersburg to ask for Russian support.

When revolution broke out in China in October, they acted. On 1 December 1911 the Mongols told the Qing amban in Urga to leave, and on 29 December the Jebtsundamba, a Tibetan-born lama in his early forties, was enthroned as Bogd Khan, “holy ruler”, of the Mongol state. Mongols in Inner Mongolia and Barga were invited to join, and in 1913 Mongolia and Tibet signed a treaty recognising each other.

Neither Russia nor the new Chinese republic was ready to accept full independence. By the Kyakhta agreement of 1915 Mongolia became an autonomous state under Chinese suzerainty, and in 1919 a Chinese warlord army abolished even that. Yet 1911 remained the founding date of modern Mongolian statehood, and its independence was restored after the revolution of 1921.
story.zh:
清朝末年，朝廷推行的“新政”使蒙古面临汉人移垦、驻军和征税的威胁。1911年夏，一批喀尔喀贵族在蒙古佛教领袖哲布尊丹巴呼图克图的支持下，秘密前往圣彼得堡寻求俄国支持。

10月中国爆发革命，他们随即行动。1911年12月1日，蒙古人令清朝驻库伦办事大臣离境；12月29日，生于西藏、四十出头的哲布尊丹巴即位为蒙古国的博克多汗，意为“圣主”。他们邀请内蒙古和呼伦贝尔的蒙古人加入；1913年蒙古与西藏签订条约相互承认。

无论俄国还是新成立的中华民国都不准备接受完全独立。根据1915年的恰克图协定，蒙古成为中国宗主权下的自治国家；1919年，中国军阀部队连这一自治也取消了。但1911年仍被视为现代蒙古国家的建立之年，1921年革命之后其独立得以恢复。

name.en: Third Anglo-Afghan War and Afghan independence
name.zh: 第三次英阿战争与阿富汗独立

summary.en: Shortly after taking the throne, Emir Amanullah Khan declared Afghanistan fully independent and sent troops across the frontier in May 1919. After a month of fighting and British air raids on Kabul and Jalalabad, an armistice was followed by the Treaty of Rawalpindi, by which Britain gave up control of Afghan foreign policy.
summary.zh: 埃米尔阿曼努拉汗即位不久便宣布阿富汗完全独立，并于1919年5月派兵越过边界。经过一个月的战斗和英国对喀布尔、贾拉拉巴德的空袭，双方停火，随后签订《拉瓦尔品第条约》，英国放弃对阿富汗外交的控制。

sources.title: Thomas J. Barfield, Afghanistan: A Cultural and Political History (2010)
Britannica: Anglo-Afghan Wars
Wikipedia: Third Anglo-Afghan War

note: Marker at the Khyber Pass, where fighting began. The treaty was signed on 8 August 1919; Afghanistan celebrates independence on 19 August.

story.en:
In February 1919 Emir Habibullah Khan was shot dead in his tent on a hunting trip. His son Amanullah, governor of Kabul, seized the throne and, to win over the army and the nationalists, proclaimed Afghanistan fully independent. In May Afghan troops crossed into British India at Bagh, near the Khyber Pass, hoping for a frontier rising.

The British Indian army, exhausted after the World War, still had aircraft. A single large Handley Page bomber flew over the mountains and bombed Kabul, a shock to a city that had never seen an aeroplane. After a month of fighting both sides accepted an armistice. By the Treaty of Rawalpindi in August, Britain stopped paying the Afghan subsidy and recognised Afghanistan’s right to conduct its own foreign relations. Afghanistan became one of the first states to recognise Soviet Russia.

Amanullah then launched rapid reforms: a constitution, schools for girls, Western dress at court, and in 1928 an appearance by Queen Soraya without a veil during a tour of Europe. The backlash was fierce. In 1929 a rebellion drove him from the throne, and he died in exile in Switzerland in 1960.
story.zh:
1919年2月，埃米尔哈比布拉汗在一次狩猎途中于帐篷里被枪杀。其子、喀布尔总督阿曼努拉夺取王位，为争取军队和民族主义者的支持，宣布阿富汗完全独立。5月，阿富汗军队在开伯尔山口附近的巴格越境进入英属印度，希望引发边境部落起事。

一战后疲惫不堪的英属印度军队仍拥有飞机。一架大型汉德利·佩奇轰炸机飞越群山轰炸喀布尔，令这座从未见过飞机的城市大为震惊。战斗一个月后双方接受停火。根据8月签订的《拉瓦尔品第条约》，英国停止支付对阿富汗的津贴，承认阿富汗有权自主处理外交。阿富汗成为最早承认苏俄的国家之一。

此后阿曼努拉推行急速改革：颁布宪法、兴办女子学校、宫廷改穿西式服装；1928年访问欧洲时，王后索拉娅不戴面纱公开露面。反弹十分激烈。1929年一场叛乱迫使他退位，他于1960年在瑞士流亡中去世。

name.en: The Hujum: Soviet unveiling campaign in Uzbekistan
name.zh: “胡居姆”：乌兹别克斯坦的苏联揭面纱运动

summary.en: On International Women’s Day, 8 March 1927, the Communist Party staged mass meetings in Uzbek cities at which thousands of women threw off and burned their paranji robes and horsehair veils. The “Hujum” (assault) on seclusion met fierce resistance, and hundreds of unveiled women were murdered.
summary.zh: 1927年3月8日国际妇女节，共产党在乌兹别克各城市组织群众大会，数千名妇女当众扔掉并焚烧帕兰吉长袍和马鬃面纱。这场针对妇女隔离习俗的“胡居姆”（进攻）运动遭到激烈抵抗，数以百计揭去面纱的妇女被杀害。

sources.title: Douglas Northrop, Veiled Empire: Gender and Power in Stalinist Central Asia (2004)
Marianne Kamp, The New Woman in Uzbekistan (2006)
Wikipedia: Hujum

note: Counts of women killed in the backlash vary; Northrop and Kamp cite figures in the hundreds to over a thousand for 1927–29.

story.en:
In much of urban Uzbekistan in the 1920s, women went out in a paranji, a long robe draped from the head, with a heavy veil of black horsehair, the chachvon, over the face. To Bolshevik activists the veil symbolised everything they meant to destroy, and women, they argued, could be a “surrogate proletariat” in a land with few industrial workers.

On 8 March 1927 the party’s women’s department organised rallies in Tashkent, Samarkand, Kokand and other cities. Women, many of them the wives and daughters of party members, came forward to tear off their veils and throw them on bonfires while speakers proclaimed their liberation. Activists counted tens of thousands unveiled in the following months.

The reaction was violent. Clergy and neighbours condemned unveiled women as prostitutes; many put the veil back on, and hundreds were raped or killed, sometimes by their own relatives. The party responded with show trials and treated such killings as counter-revolutionary crimes. Historians such as Douglas Northrop argue that the campaign made the veil, for a time, a symbol of Uzbek national identity against Soviet rule.
story.zh:
1920年代，在乌兹别克斯坦的许多城镇，妇女出门要披上从头垂下的长袍“帕兰吉”，脸上罩着厚重的黑色马鬃面纱“恰奇冯”。在布尔什维克活动家看来，面纱象征着他们要摧毁的一切；他们还认为，在一个产业工人稀少的地方，妇女可以充当“替代的无产阶级”。

1927年3月8日，党的妇女部在塔什干、撒马尔罕、浩罕等城市组织集会。许多妇女是党员的妻女，她们走上前去扯下面纱扔进篝火，演讲者则宣告她们获得解放。此后几个月，活动家统计称有数万人揭去了面纱。

反应十分暴烈。宗教人士和邻里把揭去面纱的妇女斥为娼妓，许多人重新戴上面纱，数以百计的妇女遭到强奸或杀害，有时凶手就是她们的亲属。党以公开审判回应，把这类谋杀定为反革命罪行。诺思罗普等史家认为，这场运动反倒使面纱一度成为乌兹别克民族认同对抗苏联统治的象征。

summary.en: Forced collectivisation and the confiscation of livestock from nomadic Kazakhs destroyed the herds on which they lived. About 1.5 million people died, most of them Kazakhs, perhaps 38 percent of the nation, and hundreds of thousands fled to China and neighbouring republics.
summary.zh: 强制集体化和没收游牧哈萨克人的牲畜，摧毁了他们赖以为生的畜群。约150万人死亡，其中大多数是哈萨克人，约占哈萨克族的38%；数十万人逃往中国和邻近的加盟共和国。

sources.title: Sarah Cameron, The Hungry Steppe: Famine, Violence, and the Making of Soviet Kazakhstan (2018)
Niccolò Pianciola, “The Collectivization Famine in Kazakhstan, 1931–1933”, Harvard Ukrainian Studies 25 (2001)
Wikipedia: Kazakh famine of 1930–1933

note: Death toll estimates range from about 1.5 to 2.3 million. The marker is placed in central Kazakhstan.

story.en:
In 1928 Filipp Goloshchekin, the party chief of Kazakhstan, announced a “Little October” in the steppe. Wealthy herders were stripped of their animals and deported, and from 1929 nomads were ordered to settle in collective farms and hand over meat and grain to meet impossible quotas. Many slaughtered their animals rather than give them up.

The herds collapsed. Kazakhstan lost roughly nine-tenths of its livestock within a few years, and for a people who lived on meat and milk, that meant starvation. Starving Kazakhs wandered into towns and railway stations; others fled across the border to Xinjiang, to Uzbekistan and to Siberia. Some local communists, among them Turar Ryskulov, wrote to Stalin to describe the catastrophe.

About 1.5 million people died, the great majority of them Kazakhs. The famine killed a larger share of its victims’ nation than any other Soviet famine and made the Kazakhs a minority in their own republic for half a century. Kazakhstan now commemorates the victims each year on 31 May, and the event is known in Kazakh as the Asharshylyk, “the great hunger”.
story.zh:
1928年，哈萨克斯坦党的首脑戈洛晓金宣布在草原上发动“小十月革命”。富裕牧主的牲畜被没收，本人遭流放；从1929年起，游牧民被勒令定居到集体农庄，并按照根本无法完成的指标上缴肉类和粮食。许多人宁可宰杀牲畜也不愿上交。

畜群随之崩溃。短短几年内，哈萨克斯坦损失了约九成牲畜，对于以肉和奶为生的民族而言，这意味着饥饿。饥饿的哈萨克人涌入城镇和火车站，另一些人越境逃往新疆，或逃到乌兹别克斯坦和西伯利亚。图拉尔·雷斯库洛夫等一些当地共产党人曾写信向斯大林报告这场灾难。

约150万人死亡，其中绝大多数是哈萨克人。按死者占本民族的比例计算，这是苏联最惨烈的饥荒，并使哈萨克人在此后半个世纪中成为本共和国内的少数民族。哈萨克斯坦现在每年5月31日悼念死难者，这场灾难在哈萨克语中称为“阿沙尔谢勒克”，意为“大饥饿”。

name.en: Deportation of Soviet Koreans to Central Asia
name.zh: 苏联远东朝鲜人被强制迁往中亚

summary.en: In September–October 1937 the Soviet government deported about 172,000 Koreans from the Far East to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan in cattle trains, the first deportation of a whole nationality. Volga Germans, Chechens, Ingush, Crimean Tatars and others followed in 1941–44, making Central Asia a land of exiles.
summary.zh: 1937年9—10月，苏联政府用运牲畜的火车把约17.2万名朝鲜人从远东押送到哈萨克斯坦和乌兹别克斯坦，这是第一次整个民族被强制迁移。1941—1944年，伏尔加德意志人、车臣人、印古什人、克里米亚鞑靼人等相继被迁来，中亚成为流放者之地。

sources.title: Terry Martin, The Affirmative Action Empire (2001)
J. Otto Pohl, Ethnic Cleansing in the USSR, 1937–1949 (1999)
Wikipedia: Deportation of Koreans in the Soviet Union

note: The marker is at Ushtobe in Kazakhstan, where many of the first trains were unloaded.

story.en:
Koreans had settled in the Russian Far East since the 1860s, many fleeing famine and later Japanese rule. In August 1937, as tension with Japan grew, Stalin and Molotov signed a decree ordering the whole Korean population of the border region removed, on the grounds that Japanese spies might hide among them.

Within two months some 172,000 people were loaded into freight cars for a month-long journey across Siberia. Many were unloaded in the open steppe around Ushtobe in south-eastern Kazakhstan, and on the Syr Darya in Uzbekistan, with autumn coming on; they dug earth shelters to survive the first winter. Thousands died, especially children and the old. In the following years the Koreans became known as skilled rice farmers on the collective farms, and their descendants, the Koryo-saram, still live across Central Asia.

The Korean deportation set a pattern. In 1941 the Volga Germans were sent east, and in 1943–44 the Karachays, Kalmyks, Chechens, Ingush, Balkars, Crimean Tatars and Meskhetian Turks followed, hundreds of thousands of them to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan. Most were allowed to leave only after Stalin’s death.
story.zh:
自1860年代起，朝鲜人陆续迁居俄国远东，许多人是为了逃避饥荒，后来又为躲避日本统治。1937年8月，随着与日本关系紧张，斯大林和莫洛托夫签署法令，以日本间谍可能藏身其中为由，下令迁走边境地区的全部朝鲜人。

两个月内，约17.2万人被装进货运车厢，横穿西伯利亚，旅途长达一个月。许多人被卸在哈萨克斯坦东南部乌什托别周围的旷野上，或乌兹别克斯坦的锡尔河边，此时秋天已至，他们挖地窝子熬过第一个冬天。数千人死去，尤其是儿童和老人。此后朝鲜人在集体农庄中以种稻能手著称，其后裔“高丽人”至今仍分布在中亚各地。

朝鲜人的流放开了先例。1941年伏尔加德意志人被迁往东方，1943—1944年卡拉恰伊人、卡尔梅克人、车臣人、印古什人、巴尔卡尔人、克里米亚鞑靼人和梅斯赫特土耳其人相继被流放，其中数十万人被送到哈萨克斯坦、吉尔吉斯斯坦和乌兹别克斯坦。大多数人直到斯大林死后才获准离开。

summary.en: Under Soviet pressure, Marshal Choibalsan’s security forces arrested and executed tens of thousands of Mongolians as counter-revolutionaries and Japanese spies, including some 17,000 Buddhist lamas. Nearly all of the country’s monasteries were closed and most were destroyed.
summary.zh: 在苏联压力下，乔巴山元帅的安全部门以反革命和日本间谍的罪名逮捕并处决了数万名蒙古人，其中包括约1.7万名佛教喇嘛。全国几乎所有寺院被关闭，大部分被摧毁。

sources.title: Christopher Kaplonski, The Lama Question: Violence, Sovereignty, and Exception in Early Socialist Mongolia (2014)
Baabar, History of Mongolia (1999)
Wikipedia: Stalinist repressions in Mongolia

note: Estimates of the dead range from about 20,000 to over 30,000. No Wikidata item was found for the event.

story.en:
In the mid-1930s the Buddhist church was still the richest institution in Mongolia, with hundreds of monasteries and perhaps a third of the country’s men in robes. Stalin pressed the Mongolian leadership to break it and to purge anyone suspected of sympathy with Japan, which now occupied neighbouring Manchuria. When Prime Minister Peljidiin Genden resisted, he was removed and later shot in Moscow.

From September 1937, with NKVD advisers, Khorloogiin Choibalsan’s interior ministry carried out mass arrests. Special commissions sentenced thousands at a time, often after torture; lamas, nobles, party members and Buryat refugees were taken away by truck and shot. Mass graves found in recent decades near Ulaanbaatar and elsewhere have confirmed the scale. About 17,000 lamas were killed and most of the rest forced into lay life, and the great monasteries were dynamited or left to ruin.

The purge made Choibalsan the dominant figure in Mongolia until his death in 1952. After 1990 the victims were rehabilitated, and Mongolia marks 10 September as a day of remembrance for the victims of political repression.
story.zh:
1930年代中期，佛教僧团仍是蒙古最富有的机构，拥有数百座寺院，全国男性中也许有三分之一是僧人。斯大林逼迫蒙古领导层摧毁僧团，并清洗一切被怀疑同情日本的人，因为日本此时已占领邻近的满洲。总理根敦抵制，结果被撤职，后在莫斯科被枪决。

1937年9月起，乔巴山领导的内务部在内务人民委员部顾问参与下开展大逮捕。特别委员会往往在刑讯之后一次判决数千人；喇嘛、贵族、党员和布里亚特难民被卡车拉走枪杀。近几十年在乌兰巴托附近等地发现的乱葬坑证实了其规模。约1.7万名喇嘛被杀，其余大多被迫还俗，大寺院或被炸毁，或任其倾颓。

这场清洗使乔巴山成为蒙古的主宰人物，直到1952年去世。1990年后受害者获得平反，蒙古将9月10日定为政治迫害受害者纪念日。

name.zh: 哈拉哈河战役（诺门罕战役）

summary.en: A border dispute between the Mongolian People’s Republic and Japanese-ruled Manchukuo grew into a summer of fighting between Soviet–Mongolian and Japanese forces. In August Georgy Zhukov’s armoured offensive encircled and destroyed the Japanese 23rd Division; Japan turned away from war with the USSR.
summary.zh: 蒙古人民共和国与日本控制的伪满洲国之间的边界争端，演变为苏蒙军队与日军之间持续一个夏天的战斗。8月，朱可夫指挥装甲部队发动攻势，包围并歼灭日军第23师团；日本从此放弃与苏联开战。

sources.title: Stuart D. Goldman, Nomonhan, 1939: The Red Army’s Victory That Shaped World War II (2012)
Alvin D. Coox, Nomonhan: Japan Against Russia, 1939 (1985)
Britannica: Mongolia — Counterrevolution and Japan

story.en:
Mongolia said its eastern border ran some 20 kilometres east of the Khalkhin Gol river; Japan’s Kwantung Army, which ran Manchukuo, said it followed the river itself. In May 1939 a clash between Mongolian cavalry and Manchukuo troops over the strip of grassland escalated, and both sides poured in forces.

Moscow sent a little-known corps commander, Georgy Zhukov. Through July the Japanese crossed the river and were driven back at Bayan Tsagaan. Zhukov then built up a force of some 500 tanks, aircraft and heavy artillery at the end of a long supply line, while disguising his preparations. On 20 August he attacked. In ten days his armoured pincers closed behind the Japanese 23rd Division and destroyed it. Some 8,000 Japanese and nearly 10,000 Soviet and Mongolian soldiers died over the summer.

A ceasefire was signed in Moscow on 15 September, three weeks after the Nazi–Soviet pact. The defeat persuaded Tokyo to expand south rather than north, and in April 1941 Japan and the USSR signed a neutrality pact. Zhukov, promoted after the battle, later commanded the defence of Moscow.
story.zh:
蒙古认为其东部边界在哈拉哈河以东约20公里处，而控制伪满洲国的日本关东军则认为边界就是哈拉哈河本身。1939年5月，蒙古骑兵与伪满军队因这片草原发生冲突，事态升级，双方不断增兵。

莫斯科派来了当时名气不大的军长朱可夫。整个7月，日军渡河进攻，在巴音查岗被击退。随后朱可夫在漫长补给线的末端集结了约500辆坦克以及飞机和重炮，同时隐蔽其准备。8月20日他发起进攻，十天之内装甲钳形攻势在日军第23师团后方合拢，将其歼灭。整个夏天约8000名日军和近1万名苏蒙军人阵亡。

9月15日，即苏德条约签订三周后，双方在莫斯科签署停火协议。这次失败使东京决定向南而非向北扩张，1941年4月日苏签订中立条约。战后获得晋升的朱可夫后来指挥了莫斯科保卫战。

summary.en: When Gorbachev replaced Kazakhstan’s long-serving Kazakh party leader Dinmukhamed Kunaev with Gennady Kolbin, a Russian with no ties to the republic, thousands of young Kazakhs protested in Alma-Ata’s central square. Troops and police broke up the demonstrations; the number killed is still disputed.
summary.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫撤换长期担任哈萨克斯坦党的领导人的哈萨克族人库纳耶夫，代之以与该共和国毫无渊源的俄罗斯人科尔宾，数千名哈萨克青年在阿拉木图中心广场抗议。军警驱散了示威，死亡人数至今仍有争议。

sources.title: Martha Brill Olcott, The Kazakhs (2nd ed., 1995)
Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021)
Wikipedia: Jeltoqsan

note: Official Soviet figures gave two deaths; later Kazakh inquiries and witnesses suggest more. The protests took place on 17–18 December 1986.

summary.en: Officers loyal to the communist People’s Democratic Party of Afghanistan stormed the presidential palace in Kabul on 27–28 April 1978, killing President Mohammad Daoud Khan and his family. The new regime’s radical reforms and repression provoked revolts across the country.
summary.zh: 1978年4月27—28日，忠于共产主义的阿富汗人民民主党的军官攻入喀布尔总统府，杀死总统达乌德汗及其家人。新政权激进的改革和镇压在全国各地激起反抗。

sources.title: Thomas J. Barfield, Afghanistan: A Cultural and Political History (2010)
Britannica: People’s Democratic Party of Afghanistan
Wikipedia: Saur Revolution

summary.en: In December 1979 Soviet troops entered Afghanistan, killed the communist leader Hafizullah Amin and installed Babrak Karmal. For nine years the 40th Army fought mujahideen guerrillas backed by the United States, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. About 15,000 Soviet soldiers and perhaps a million Afghans died before the last troops left in February 1989.
summary.zh: 1979年12月苏军进入阿富汗，杀死共产党领导人阿明，扶植卡尔迈勒。此后九年，苏联第40集团军与美国、巴基斯坦和沙特阿拉伯支持的圣战者游击队作战。约1.5万名苏军士兵和也许上百万阿富汗人死亡，最后一批苏军于1989年2月撤离。

label.en: Soviet columns cross the Amu Darya at Termez (25 December)
label.zh: 苏军在铁尔梅兹渡过阿姆河（12月25日）

label.en: Tajbeg Palace stormed; Amin killed (27 December)
label.zh: 强攻塔吉贝克宫，阿明被杀（12月27日）

label.en: Offensives against Ahmad Shah Massoud in the Panjshir
label.zh: 在潘杰希尔谷地围剿马苏德

label.en: First Stinger missiles used against Soviet helicopters near Jalalabad
label.zh: 贾拉拉巴德附近首次用“毒刺”导弹打击苏军直升机

label.en: Last Soviet troops cross the Friendship Bridge (15 February)
label.zh: 最后一批苏军经友谊大桥撤离（2月15日）

sources.title: Rodric Braithwaite, Afgantsy: The Russians in Afghanistan 1979–89 (2011)
Steve Coll, Ghost Wars (2004)
Britannica: Soviet invasion of Afghanistan

note: Afghan death toll estimates range from about 0.5 to 2 million. Marker at the Tajbeg Palace in Kabul.

story.en:
By late 1979 the communist government in Kabul was falling apart. Its reforms had provoked uprisings, its leaders had murdered one another, and the new strongman Hafizullah Amin distrusted Moscow. On 25 December Soviet troops crossed the Amu Darya and flew into Kabul. Two days later special forces stormed the Tajbeg Palace and killed Amin, and Babrak Karmal was installed in his place.

The Soviet leaders expected a short operation. Instead the 40th Army, which grew to about 100,000 men, was drawn into a war against a patchwork of mujahideen groups. They were armed and funded by the United States, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan’s intelligence service, and joined by volunteers from across the Muslim world, among them Osama bin Laden. Commanders such as Ahmad Shah Massoud in the Panjshir valley beat off one Soviet offensive after another. Bombing and the destruction of villages drove some five million Afghans into Pakistan and Iran.

From 1986 American Stinger missiles made Soviet helicopters vulnerable, and Gorbachev decided to leave. The Geneva Accords were signed in April 1988, and on 15 February 1989 General Boris Gromov walked last across the Friendship Bridge at Termez. The war left Afghanistan to a civil war, and many Soviet citizens saw it as a cause of the USSR’s collapse.
story.zh:
到1979年底，喀布尔的共产党政府已濒临崩溃。其改革激起各地起义，领导人相互残杀，新上台的强人阿明对莫斯科心存戒备。12月25日，苏军渡过阿姆河并空运进入喀布尔。两天后特种部队攻入塔吉贝克宫杀死阿明，扶植卡尔迈勒取而代之。

苏联领导人原以为这将是一次短期行动。结果兵力增至约10万人的第40集团军，却陷入与各派圣战者的战争。这些游击队得到美国、沙特阿拉伯和巴基斯坦情报机构的武器与资金，还有来自伊斯兰世界各地的志愿者加入，其中包括本·拉登。潘杰希尔谷地的马苏德等指挥官一次次击退苏军的围剿。轰炸和对村庄的摧毁迫使约五百万阿富汗人逃往巴基斯坦和伊朗。

从1986年起，美国提供的“毒刺”导弹使苏军直升机变得脆弱，戈尔巴乔夫决定撤军。1988年4月签署日内瓦协议，1989年2月15日，格罗莫夫将军最后一个走过铁尔梅兹的友谊大桥。战争使阿富汗陷入内战，许多苏联人也把它视为苏联解体的原因之一。

summary.en: Inspired by events in Eastern Europe, young Mongolians led by Sanjaasürengiin Zorig held rallies and in March 1990 a hunger strike in Ulaanbaatar’s central square. The ruling party’s Politburo resigned, multi-party elections were held that July, and a democratic constitution was adopted in 1992.
summary.zh: 受东欧局势鼓舞，以桑加苏伦·卓里格为首的蒙古青年在乌兰巴托中心广场举行集会，并于1990年3月绝食抗议。执政党政治局集体辞职，同年7月举行多党选举，1992年通过民主宪法。

sources.title: Morris Rossabi, Modern Mongolia: From Khans to Commissars to Capitalists (2005)
Britannica: History of Mongolia
Wikipedia: 1990 Democratic Revolution in Mongolia

note: The movement began with a rally on 10 December 1989; the Politburo resigned on 9 March 1990.

summary.en: After the 11 September attacks, the United States and its allies, with the anti-Taliban Northern Alliance, overthrew the Taliban government that sheltered al-Qaeda. A new Afghan republic was built with Western support, but a Taliban insurgency grew; after the 2020 Doha agreement the last foreign troops left in August 2021.
summary.zh: “9·11”袭击之后，美国及其盟友联合反塔利班的北方联盟，推翻了庇护“基地”组织的塔利班政府。在西方支持下建立了新的阿富汗共和国，但塔利班叛乱不断扩大；2020年多哈协议之后，最后一批外国军队于2021年8月撤离。

sources.title: Carter Malkasian, The American War in Afghanistan: A History (2021)
Steve Coll, Directorate S (2018)
Britannica: Afghanistan War

story.en:
On 9 September 2001 two al-Qaeda suicide bombers posing as television journalists killed Ahmad Shah Massoud, the leader of the last resistance to the Taliban, in his headquarters in the north. Two days later al-Qaeda attacked New York and Washington. When the Taliban leader Mullah Omar refused to hand over Osama bin Laden, the United States began bombing on 7 October.

American air power, special forces and the Northern Alliance broke the Taliban within weeks: Kabul fell on 13 November and Kandahar in early December. At a conference in Bonn, Afghan factions chose Hamid Karzai to lead an interim government, and NATO took over the international force. Millions of refugees returned, girls went back to school, and elections were held, but the state depended on foreign money and was riddled with corruption.

The Taliban regrouped in Pakistan and from 2005 waged a growing insurgency. A surge raised US troops to about 100,000 in 2010–11, and bin Laden was killed in Pakistan in 2011, but the war ground on. In February 2020 the United States and the Taliban signed an agreement in Doha for a full withdrawal, which was completed in August 2021 as the republic collapsed.
story.zh:
2001年9月9日，两名伪装成电视记者的“基地”组织自杀式袭击者在北方的指挥部里杀死了最后一支反塔利班抵抗力量的领袖马苏德。两天后，“基地”组织袭击了纽约和华盛顿。塔利班领导人奥马尔拒绝交出本·拉登，美国于10月7日开始轰炸。

美国的空中力量、特种部队与北方联盟在数周内击溃塔利班：喀布尔于11月13日陷落，坎大哈于12月初陷落。在波恩会议上，阿富汗各派推举卡尔扎伊领导临时政府，北约接管国际部队。数百万难民回国，女孩重返校园，选举得以举行，但国家依赖外国资金，腐败丛生。

塔利班在巴基斯坦重整旗鼓，从2005年起发动日益扩大的叛乱。2010—2011年美军增兵至约10万人，2011年本·拉登在巴基斯坦被击毙，但战争仍在拖延。2020年2月，美国与塔利班在多哈签署全面撤军协议，2021年8月撤军完成之时，共和国也随之崩溃。

summary.en: After armed men freed 23 local businessmen on trial for Islamist extremism from Andijan prison, thousands gathered in Babur Square to air grievances. On 13 May 2005 Uzbek security forces fired on the crowd; the government said 187 died, while witnesses and rights groups put the toll in the hundreds.
summary.zh: 武装人员从安集延监狱救出23名被控宗教极端主义而受审的当地商人后，数千人聚集在巴布尔广场诉说不满。2005年5月13日，乌兹别克安全部队向人群开枪；政府称187人死亡，而目击者和人权组织估计死者达数百人。

sources.title: Human Rights Watch, “Bullets Were Falling Like Rain”: The Andijan Massacre, May 13, 2005 (2005)
Britannica: Andijon
Wikipedia: Andijan massacre

note: The death toll remains disputed; Uzbekistan refused an international inquiry.

summary.en: As US and NATO forces withdrew, a Taliban offensive took most of Afghanistan’s provincial capitals in ten days and entered Kabul on 15 August 2021 after President Ashraf Ghani fled. A chaotic airlift from Kabul airport evacuated over 120,000 people before the last US flight left on 30 August.
summary.zh: 美国和北约部队撤离之际，塔利班在十天内攻占阿富汗大部分省会，2021年8月15日总统加尼出逃后进入喀布尔。喀布尔机场混乱的空中撤离行动撤出了12万多人，最后一架美国飞机于8月30日离开。

sources.title: Carter Malkasian, The American War in Afghanistan: A History (2021)
Britannica: Taliban
Wikipedia: Fall of Kabul (2021)

story.en:
In April 2021 President Joe Biden announced that all American troops would leave Afghanistan by September. Over the summer the Taliban took district after district, often by negotiating the surrender of unpaid and demoralised government forces. On 6 August the first provincial capital, Zaranj, fell; within ten days Kandahar, Herat, Mazar-i Sharif and Jalalabad had followed.

On the morning of 15 August Taliban fighters reached the edges of Kabul. That afternoon President Ashraf Ghani flew out of the country, and by evening Taliban commanders were sitting in the presidential palace. Crowds of Afghans desperate to leave rushed Kabul airport; television showed young men clinging to the side of an American transport plane as it took off.

Over the next two weeks American and allied aircraft flew out more than 120,000 people. On 26 August a suicide bomber of the Islamic State’s Khorasan branch struck the crowd at the airport’s Abbey Gate, killing some 170 Afghans and 13 American soldiers. The last American plane left just before midnight on 30 August, and the Taliban restored their Islamic Emirate, imposing sweeping restrictions on women’s education and work.
story.zh:
2021年4月，拜登总统宣布美军将于9月前全部撤出阿富汗。整个夏天，塔利班逐一攻取各区，常常是通过谈判让欠饷、士气低落的政府军投降。8月6日第一个省会扎兰季陷落，十天之内坎大哈、赫拉特、马扎里沙里夫和贾拉拉巴德相继失守。

8月15日上午，塔利班武装抵达喀布尔郊外。当天下午总统加尼乘飞机出国，到傍晚塔利班指挥官已坐进总统府。急于离开的阿富汗人涌向喀布尔机场；电视画面上，年轻人紧紧攀附在一架正在起飞的美国运输机机身上。

此后两周，美国及盟国飞机撤出了12万多人。8月26日，“伊斯兰国”呼罗珊分支的一名自杀式袭击者在机场阿比门的人群中引爆炸弹，炸死约170名阿富汗人和13名美军士兵。最后一架美国飞机在8月30日午夜前起飞，塔利班恢复其“伊斯兰酋长国”，对妇女受教育和工作施加全面限制。

name.zh: 2022年1月哈萨克斯坦骚乱（“血色一月”）

summary.en: A sharp rise in the price of liquefied gas set off protests in the oil town of Zhanaozen on 2 January 2022 that spread nationwide; in Almaty government buildings were stormed and burned. President Tokayev called in troops of the Russian-led CSTO and ordered security forces to shoot without warning; 238 people died, and the political power of ex-president Nazarbayev was broken.
summary.zh: 2022年1月2日，液化气价格大幅上涨在石油城扎瑙津引发抗议，并迅速蔓延全国；在阿拉木图，政府大楼遭冲击和焚烧。托卡耶夫总统请俄罗斯主导的集体安全条约组织派兵，并下令安全部队可不经警告开枪；238人死亡，前总统纳扎尔巴耶夫的政治权力随之瓦解。

sources.title: Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021; 2022 ed.)
Britannica: Kazakhstan — Recent history
Wikipedia: 2022 Kazakh unrest

note: The death toll of 238 is the official figure from the Kazakh prosecutor-general.

name.en: Short-lived East Turkestan republic at Kashgar
name.zh: 喀什噶尔短暂的“东突厥斯坦共和国”

summary.en: During the Kumul rebellion against the Xinjiang governor Jin Shuren, Uyghur and Kyrgyz insurgents in the Tarim Basin proclaimed an Islamic republic at Kashgar in November 1933. Hui troops of the warlord Ma Zhongying destroyed it in early 1934, and the province passed to the Soviet-backed rule of Sheng Shicai.
summary.zh: 在反对新疆省主席金树仁的哈密暴动期间，塔里木盆地的维吾尔和柯尔克孜叛军于1933年11月在喀什噶尔宣布成立一个伊斯兰共和国。1934年初它被军阀马仲英的回族军队摧毁，新疆随后落入苏联支持的盛世才统治之下。

sources.title: Andrew D. W. Forbes, Warlords and Muslims in Chinese Central Asia (1986)
James A. Millward, Eurasian Crossroads: A History of Xinjiang (2007)
Wikipedia: First East Turkestan Republic

note: No separate Wikidata event item; Q986665 denotes the short-lived state.

name.en: Kujula Kadphises unites the Yuezhi: rise of the Kushans
name.zh: 丘就却统一月氏五翕侯，贵霜兴起

summary.en: More than a century after the Yuezhi settled in Bactria, Kujula Kadphises, prince of the Guishuang clan, destroyed the other four Yuezhi principalities and made himself king, according to the Hou Hanshu. He went on to take the Kabul valley and Jibin (Kapisa–Gandhara), founding the Kushan Empire.
summary.zh: 据《后汉书》，月氏人定居大夏一百多年后，贵霜翕侯丘就却攻灭其余四翕侯，自立为王。他随后夺取高附（喀布尔河谷）和罽宾（迦毕试—犍陀罗），建立了贵霜帝国。

sources.title: Fan Ye, Hou Hanshu, ch. 88: The Western Regions, tr. John E. Hill, section 13 (Da Yuezhi)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kushan dynasty
N. Sims-Williams & J. Cribb, “A new Bactrian inscription of Kanishka the Great”, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 4 (1996)

note: The Hou Hanshu gives no date; Kujula’s reign is placed c. 30–80 CE on numismatic grounds. The seat of the Guishuang prince is unidentified, so the marker is at Bactra (Balkh). No Wikidata item exists for the event (Q560157 is Kujula Kadphises).

story.en:
In the second century BCE the Yuezhi, nomads of the Gansu corridor, were driven west by the Xiongnu. When the Han envoy Zhang Qian found them around 129 BCE they were camped north of the Oxus as overlords of Bactria, the old Greek kingdom. According to the Hou Hanshu, compiled in the fifth century from Han reports, they divided the country among five princes, called xihou in Chinese.

More than a hundred years later the prince of the Guishuang, Qiujiuque, whom his coins call Kujula Kadphises, destroyed the other four and made himself king. He invaded Parthian territory, took the Kabul valley and conquered Jibin, the lands around Gandhara, and died, the chronicle says, at over eighty. His coins copy those of the last Greek king Hermaeus and even a Roman imperial head, a sign of how many worlds met in his realm.

His son conquered north-western India, and the Rabatak inscription later named Kujula as Kanishka’s great-grandfather. Other peoples now called the ruler “the Kushan king”, though the Han kept the old name Yuezhi. In 90 CE, the Hou Hanshu says, a Yuezhi army of 70,000 under a viceroy named Xie crossed the Pamirs against Ban Chao, failed to take his strongholds, ran short of supplies and asked leave to go home.
story.zh:
公元前二世纪，河西走廊的游牧民月氏被匈奴赶往西方。约公元前129年，汉使张骞找到他们时，他们已在阿姆河以北驻牧，成为昔日希腊人王国大夏的主人。据五世纪依据汉代报告编成的《后汉书》，他们把这片土地分给五位首领，汉文称为“翕侯”。

一百多年后，贵霜翕侯丘就却（钱币上称库朱拉·卡德菲塞斯）攻灭其余四翕侯，自立为王。他侵入安息，夺取高附，攻灭罽宾即犍陀罗一带，据史书记载享年八十余岁。他的钱币仿照最后一位希腊国王赫尔迈欧斯的钱币，甚至模仿罗马皇帝的头像，可见其国境内多种文明交汇。

其子征服了印度西北部；后来的罗巴塔克铭文称丘就却为迦腻色伽的曾祖父。其他民族从此称其君主为“贵霜王”，汉朝则仍沿用“月氏”旧称。据《后汉书》记载，公元90年，月氏副王谢率七万大军翻越葱岭进攻班超，攻城不下，粮草匮乏，只得请求退兵回国。

name.en: Kanishka’s dynastic sanctuary at Surkh Kotal
name.zh: 苏尔赫·科塔尔的迦腻色伽王朝神庙

summary.en: On a hill above the Surkh Ab valley in Bactria, Kanishka built a terraced sanctuary with a fire altar and statues of Kushan kings. Its great inscription, found in 1957, was the first long text known in Bactrian, the Iranian language the Kushans wrote in Greek letters.
summary.zh: 迦腻色伽在大夏苏尔赫河谷上方的山丘上修建了一座阶梯式神庙，内有火坛和贵霜诸王雕像。1957年在此发现的长篇铭文是已知第一篇较长的大夏语文献；大夏语是贵霜人用希腊字母书写的伊朗语。

sources.title: D. Schlumberger, M. Le Berre & G. Fussman, Surkh Kotal en Bactriane, vol. I (Mémoires de la DAFA 25, 1983)
John M. Rosenfield, The Dynastic Arts of the Kushans (1967)
Wikipedia: Surkh Kotal

note: Founded under Kanishka (accession c. 127 in the chronology used here); the great inscription dates the restoration to year 31 of his era, c. 158 CE. Q1799523 is the archaeological site.

story.en:
Surkh Kotal, the “red pass”, lies on the road north from the Hindu Kush, about 18 kilometres north of Pul-i Khumri in Baghlan province. French archaeologists led by Daniel Schlumberger dug there from 1952. They found a temple on a hilltop reached by a monumental stairway over several terraces, a fire altar, and large statues of kings in the Kushan riding dress of long coat, trousers and felt boots.

In 1957 the team uncovered a long inscription in Greek letters but in a language no one could read. It proved to be Bactrian, the local Iranian tongue that the Kushans had adopted for their coins and documents in place of Greek. The text says that King Kanishka founded the sanctuary and gave it his name, that it was abandoned when its water supply failed, and that in year 31 of Kanishka’s era a royal favourite called Nokonzoko dug a well, walled the hill and restored the shrine.

The temple honoured the kings among Iranian gods, a reminder that Kanishka, remembered in Buddhist tradition as a great patron, supported many cults. Its finds went to the Kabul Museum, where the Taliban smashed the probable statue of Kanishka in 2001; conservators later pieced it together.
story.zh:
苏尔赫·科塔尔意为“红色山口”，位于翻越兴都库什山北下的道路上，在巴格兰省普勒胡姆里以北约18公里。1952年起，施伦贝格尔率领的法国考古队在此发掘，发现一座山顶神庙，由宏伟的台阶连通几层台地，还有一座火坛，以及身穿长袍、长裤和毡靴等贵霜骑装的国王大型雕像。

1957年，考古队发现一篇用希腊字母写成、却无人能读懂的长篇铭文。后来证明它是大夏语，即贵霜人取代希腊语、用于钱币和文书的当地伊朗语。铭文说，这座神庙由迦腻色伽王创建并以他的名字命名，后因水源断绝而荒废；在迦腻色伽纪年第31年，一位名叫诺孔佐科的王室宠臣掘井、筑墙，修复了神庙。

这座神庙在伊朗诸神之间供奉君王，提醒人们：佛教传统中以护法著称的迦腻色伽，其实扶持多种信仰。出土文物运往喀布尔博物馆，2001年塔利班砸毁了那尊可能是迦腻色伽的雕像，后来文物修复人员将其重新拼合。

name.en: Lokakṣema translates the first Mahayana sutras at Luoyang
name.zh: 支娄迦谶在洛阳首译大乘佛经

summary.en: A monk from the Kushan lands known in Chinese as Zhi Loujiachen (Lokakṣema) translated the first Mahayana Buddhist scriptures into Chinese at Luoyang, among them the Perfection of Wisdom in 8,000 Lines, dated 179. His work carried the Buddhism of the Kushan world to China.
summary.zh: 来自贵霜地区的僧人支娄迦谶在洛阳首次把大乘佛经译为汉文，其中包括记为179年译出的《道行般若经》。他的译经把贵霜世界的佛教带到了中国。

sources.title: Erik Zürcher, The Buddhist Conquest of China (1959; 3rd ed. 2007)
Jan Nattier, A Guide to the Earliest Chinese Buddhist Translations (2008)
Wikipedia: Lokaksema (Buddhist monk)

note: He reached Luoyang under Emperor Huan (r. 146–168) and was active as a translator c. 178–189; which of the texts attributed to him are really his is debated (Zürcher, Harrison, Nattier). No Wikidata item exists for the event (Q370115 is Lokakṣema).

story.en:
Buddhism reached Han China along the trade roads through the Kushan lands, and its first known translators were foreigners. An Shigao, a Parthian, rendered meditation texts at Luoyang from the 140s. A generation later came a monk the Chinese called Zhi Loujiachen. The surname Zhi marked men of the Yuezhi, the Chinese name for the Kushans, and his Indian name is reconstructed as Lokakṣema.

He arrived near the end of Emperor Huan’s reign and from about 178 to 189 recited Indian texts that Chinese assistants wrote down. The catalogues credit him with the Daoxing banruo jing of 179, a version of the Perfection of Wisdom in 8,000 Lines, and with the Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra, which contains the earliest datable mention of the Buddha Amitābha. They are among the first Mahayana scriptures known to have been translated into any language.

His literal style, crowded with transliterated Indian words, was later smoothed by others. He disappears from the record as the Han dynasty collapsed into civil war, but the Mahayana teachings he introduced became the dominant Buddhism of East Asia.
story.zh:
佛教沿着穿越贵霜领土的商路传入汉朝，最早有名可考的译经者都是外来僧人。安息人安世高自140年代起在洛阳翻译禅修经典。一代人之后，又来了一位汉人称为支娄迦谶的僧人。“支”姓表示来自月氏，即汉人对贵霜人的称呼；他的梵名被构拟为Lokakṣema。

他在汉桓帝末年来到洛阳，约178至189年间口诵印度经文，由汉人助手笔录成文。经录记载他于179年译出《道行般若经》，即《八千颂般若》的一个译本，还译出《般舟三昧经》，其中有关于阿弥陀佛的最早可确定年代的记载。这些是已知最早被译成其他语言的大乘佛经之一。

他的译文直译色彩浓重，充满音译的印度词语，后来经他人润色。东汉陷入内战后，他从史籍中消失，但他引入的大乘佛教成为东亚佛教的主流。

name.en: Abulkhair Khan of the Junior Juz swears allegiance to Russia
name.zh: 小玉兹阿布勒海尔汗宣誓效忠俄国

summary.en: Seeking protection against the Dzungars and his rivals, Abulkhair, khan of the Junior Juz, asked to become a Russian subject. Empress Anna accepted in a charter of February 1731, and in October, at his camp on the Irgiz river, he and some thirty elders swore the oath before her envoy, the first step in Russia’s absorption of the Kazakh steppe.
summary.zh: 为对抗准噶尔人和内部对手，小玉兹的阿布勒海尔汗请求成为俄国臣民。女皇安娜于1731年2月颁诏接受；同年10月，他与约三十位长老在伊尔吉兹河畔的营地当着俄国使节宣誓，这是俄国吞并哈萨克草原的第一步。

sources.title: Martha Brill Olcott, The Kazakhs (2nd ed., 1995), ch. 2
Presidential Library: Incorporation of Kazakh Khanate into Russia was launched
Wikipedia: Abul Khair Khan

note: The charter is dated 19 February and the oath 10 October 1731 (Old Style). The oath was taken in the Manityube tract on the right bank of the Irgiz; the marker is approximate. No Wikidata item exists for the event (Q2498819 is Abulkhair).

story.en:
The Barefooted Flight of 1723 left the Junior Juz, westernmost of the three Kazakh hordes, squeezed between the Dzungars, the Volga Kalmyks, the Bashkirs and Khiva. Its khan Abulkhair was a capable war leader with little hold over the clans, and he decided that Russia could be his patron. In 1730 his envoys reached St Petersburg asking that he become a Russian subject.

Empress Anna signed a charter accepting him on 19 February 1731 and sent Alexei Tevkelev, a Tatar interpreter of the foreign office, to receive the oath. Tevkelev reached the khan’s camp on the Irgiz in October and found many elders hostile: they had wanted an alliance, not subjection. On 10 October Abulkhair swore on the Qur’an, followed by about thirty notables, and in December some leaders of the Middle Juz did the same.

For Abulkhair the oath was a bid for support, and he went on raiding and bargaining as he chose; rivals called it betrayal, and Sultan Barak killed him in 1748. For Russia it became the legal basis for the Orenburg line of forts, begun in 1735, and, ninety years later, for abolishing the khans. Soviet historians called it a voluntary union; Kazakh historians today stress its tactical character.
story.zh:
1723年的“赤脚逃亡”之后，三个哈萨克玉兹中最西面的小玉兹被夹在准噶尔、伏尔加河卡尔梅克人、巴什基尔人和希瓦之间。可汗阿布勒海尔善于征战，却难以号令各部，他决定以俄国为靠山。1730年，他的使者到达圣彼得堡，请求成为俄国臣民。

1731年2月19日，女皇安娜签署诏书予以接受，并派外务衙门的鞑靼人译员捷夫克列夫前去接受宣誓。捷夫克列夫于10月抵达可汗在伊尔吉兹河畔的营地，发现许多长老心怀敌意：他们想要的是结盟，而非臣服。10月10日，阿布勒海尔手按《古兰经》宣誓，约三十位显要随后宣誓；12月，中玉兹的部分首领也照此宣誓。

对阿布勒海尔来说，宣誓是争取支持的手段，此后他仍按自己的意愿劫掠和讨价还价；对手斥之为背叛，1748年巴拉克苏丹杀死了他。对俄国而言，这次宣誓成为1735年开始修筑奥伦堡要塞线、以及九十年后废除汗位的法律依据。苏联史学称之为“自愿归并”，今天的哈萨克史家则强调其策略性。

summary.en: Signed in St Petersburg on 31 August 1907, the convention wound down the Great Game. Persia was split into a Russian zone in the north, a British zone in the south-east and a neutral belt between; Russia accepted Afghanistan as outside its sphere; and both powers agreed to deal with Tibet only through China.
summary.zh: 1907年8月31日在圣彼得堡签订的这项协约结束了“大博弈”。波斯被划分为北部的俄国势力范围、东南部的英国势力范围和中间的中立地带；俄国承认阿富汗不属其势力范围；双方同意只通过中国与西藏交涉。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Anglo-Russian Entente
Jennifer Siegel, Endgame: Britain, Russia and the Final Struggle for Central Asia (2002)
Wikipedia: Anglo-Russian Convention

note: Dated 31 August 1907 (New Style; 18 August Old Style). The marker is at the Russian Foreign Ministry on Palace Square, St Petersburg, where it was signed.

story.en:
For most of the nineteenth century Britain and Russia eyed each other across Central Asia, the rivalry the British called the Great Game. Russia’s defeat by Japan in 1905 and the rise of Germany changed the calculation in both capitals. After a year of talks, the Russian foreign minister Alexander Izvolsky and the British ambassador Sir Arthur Nicolson signed a convention in St Petersburg on 31 August 1907.

It disposed of three countries, none of which was consulted. Persia, in the middle of its constitutional revolution, was divided into spheres of influence: a large Russian zone in the north that included Tehran and Isfahan, a smaller British zone in the south-east next to India, and a neutral zone between. Russia declared Afghanistan outside its sphere and agreed to deal with the emir through Britain, which promised not to annex it. Both recognised Chinese suzerainty over Tibet and undertook to send no agents to Lhasa.

The Afghan emir Habibullah never accepted the agreement, and Persian constitutionalists felt betrayed. In Europe it completed the Triple Entente of Britain, France and Russia, which went to war together in 1914. The Bolsheviks repudiated it after the revolution of 1917.
story.zh:
十九世纪的大部分时间里，英俄两国在中亚相互戒备，英国人称这种角逐为“大博弈”。1905年俄国败于日本、德国日益崛起，改变了两国首都的算计。经过一年谈判，俄国外交大臣伊兹沃利斯基与英国大使尼科尔森于1907年8月31日在圣彼得堡签订协约。

协约处置了三个国家，却未征询其中任何一国的意见。正处于立宪革命中的波斯被划分为势力范围：北部包括德黑兰和伊斯法罕在内的大片地区归俄国，与印度相邻的东南部较小地区归英国，中间为中立地带。俄国声明阿富汗不在其势力范围之内，同意通过英国与埃米尔打交道，英国则承诺不吞并阿富汗。双方都承认中国对西藏的宗主权，并保证不向拉萨派驻代表。

阿富汗埃米尔哈比布拉始终不承认该协约，波斯立宪派深感被出卖。在欧洲，它使英、法、俄三国协约最终形成，三国在1914年并肩参战。1917年革命后，布尔什维克废除了这项协约。
